title: WCAG conformance target, scope and status
target_answer: Unbound conforms to WCAG 2.2 Level AA (which also satisfies WCAG 2.1 AA and 2.0 AA) on every surface and role: donor, advisor, successor, sponsor staff, administrator, charity and embedded partner widgets, on supported mobile and desktop platforms. Complex accounting workbenches may be desktop-optimized but remain conformant with reflow. Third-party embedded components are in scope and either conform or are documented exceptions with alternatives. Session timeouts warn users and allow extension except where a financial-security limit applies, and that limit is disclosed. The claim names the evaluation it rests on and is updated on material change.
intended_practice: Evaluate each surface before activation under the activation gate.
owner: Proposed: Accessibility Lead (role not yet staffed)

title: VPAT and Accessibility Conformance Report
target_answer: A current ACR in the ITI VPAT INT edition covers WCAG 2.2, the Revised Section 508 Standards and EN 301 549, is tied to a product version, states the evaluation methods and AT used, and is updated for each major release. The ACR is derived from continuously generated test evidence rather than a one-time audit, and an independent third-party evaluation validates it at least annually for customers who require it. Customers are notified when conformance changes.
intended_practice: Produce the first ACR when the first surface is ready for activation.
owner: Proposed: Accessibility Lead (role not yet staffed)

title: Accessibility testing methodology
target_answer: Testing combines automated rule checks on every build (blocking regressions), layout checks at 320, 390, 768 and 1280 CSS px with 200 percent text and text spacing, forced-colors and reduced-motion checks, keyboard-only walkthroughs, screen-reader testing on named AT and browser pairs across desktop and mobile, and moderated usability sessions with disabled participants for essential journeys. AI agents that generate UI code are subject to the same gates; generated changes cannot merge without passing them and human review. Designers, engineers and support staff receive role-specific accessibility training.
intended_practice: Adopt Forma's conformance helpers in the Unbound pipeline and add manual and AT testing.
owner: Proposed: Accessibility Lead (role not yet staffed)

title: Accessibility remediation commitments
target_answer: Anyone can report an accessibility barrier through an accessible channel; Echelon acknowledges within two business days, provides an equivalent alternative or workaround promptly, and remediates by severity (blocking barriers on essential journeys within a short defined period, others in scheduled releases). Known non-conformances and their target dates are published in the ACR, and remediation targets can be made contractual.
intended_practice: Define the intake channel and remediation targets with the first ACR.
owner: Proposed: Accessibility Lead (role not yet staffed)

title: Accessible documents, exports and communications
target_answer: Every issued document (statements, contribution acknowledgments, grant letters, reports) is available at issuance as accessible HTML generated from the same data snapshot with the same integrity reference, and any PDF is tagged and validated against PDF/UA-1 before release. Charts carry text or table alternatives; data exports are structured with headers; email templates pass accessibility checks with plain-text alternatives. Documents uploaded by sponsors or charities are outside Echelon's control; Echelon flags inaccessible uploads and the allocation of responsibility is stated in the contract.
intended_practice: Run the rendering spike (RCD-009 DG-04) to confirm accessible HTML and a PDF/UA-capable pipeline before statements launch.
owner: Proposed: Unbound product owner

title: Design-system accessibility contracts and branding
target_answer: Unbound builds all interface elements from Forma components whose semantics, focus visibility, contrast-gated color roles, forced-colors behavior, reflow at 320 CSS px and target sizes are contractually specified and tested in the design system, so applications inherit them. Sponsor branding is compiled through a contrast gate that fails any non-conforming color pair, so white-labeling cannot reduce accessibility. Each Forma component used is pinned by release digest and covered by a conformance statement or an Unbound contract test.
intended_practice: Consume Forma in Unbound with pinned versions and contract tests; implement sponsor brand compilation with the contrast gate.
owner: Proposed: Unbound product owner

title: Accessibility legal obligations and contract terms
target_answer: Echelon has a counsel-reviewed assessment of which accessibility laws apply by customer segment: the DOJ ADA Title II rule (WCAG 2.1 AA for state and local government web content and mobile apps, including content provided through contractors) for public-entity customers such as public universities; ADA Title III exposure for sponsors serving the public; Section 508 for any federal agency buyer; state accessibility laws; and the European Accessibility Act only if Echelon provides in-scope services to EU consumers. Contracts include an accessibility warranty to WCAG 2.2 AA with remediation commitments; indemnity is negotiated case by case.
intended_practice: Commission the applicability assessment before selling to public-sector or EU customers.
owner: Proposed: General Counsel (role not yet staffed)

title: Accessible authentication, verification, timeouts and support
target_answer: Every identity-verification and step-up path has an accessible alternative reaching the same assurance level (mailed one-time code, outbound call to a verified number, captioned assisted video, in-person or notarized verification), relay calls are accepted at the same assurance as voice, and authentication does not require a cognitive function test without an alternative. Session timeouts warn and allow extension except where a disclosed security limit applies. Support channels and documentation meet Section 508 Chapter 6 and EN 301 549 clause 12 expectations, and accommodation requests never presume incapacity.
intended_practice: Build accessible assurance paths with the identity and contact-change features.
owner: Proposed: Accessibility Lead (role not yet staffed)

title: Balanced double-entry journals by entity, currency and balancing segment
target_answer: Every Unbound posting is double-entry and must balance, in exact decimal, separately for each combination of accounting entity, transaction currency and every balancing segment declared in the posting policy; for DAF books fund and restriction are mandatory balancing segments (RR-UNB-ACC-002-r1, UNB-RCN-FIN-006). A journal that fails any check is rejected, not posted. Multicurrency postings balance in both transaction and functional currency under an approved FX method and unlike currencies are never summed (ACC-MDL-003, UNB-ACC-016). Every posted line carries valid required dimensions (ACC-MDL-001). Internal fund transfers use clearing lines that net to zero sponsor-wide per currency. The balance rule is enforced both in the typed posting command and by database constraints on the journal tables, and property-based tests generate random journals to prove unbalanced entries cannot persist.
intended_practice: Implement a single posting command with a private-constructor F# journal type and database CHECK or deferred constraints; publish the balancing-segment policy per book.
owner: Not assigned; proposed: Unbound ledger product owner (role not staffed) with each sponsor's controller as accounting-policy owner

title: Append-only journals, linked corrections and tamper evidence
target_answer: Posted journals are never updated or deleted. Corrections are new reversal, reclassification or adjustment entries with explicit linkage to the original, reason, evidence, authorization and both effective and recorded dates (ACC-MDL-002, UNB-ACC-003, UNB-IMM-002, UNB-IMM-003). Normal operational database roles cannot UPDATE, DELETE or TRUNCATE authoritative rows, and schema deployment refuses destructive changes to ledger tables, including removal of append-only triggers or privilege revocations (UNB-IMM-001, RR-UNB-ACC-026-r1). Queries answer both what was true on an effective date and what was known on a recorded date, so backdated corrections never rewrite an earlier as-known view (UNB-IMM-004). Missing, reordered, duplicated or altered records are detectable through integrity checkpoints, with ledger digests anchored externally at least daily (UNB-IMM-007, CNV-PLT-010).
intended_practice: Use PostgreSQL privileges and triggers for append-only enforcement; use Strata only for declarative schema management with destructive-change refusal; anchor digests outside the database.
owner: Not assigned; proposed: Unbound ledger product owner (role not staffed) with each sponsor's controller as accounting-policy owner

title: Fund accounting under FASB ASC 958 and DAF account classification
target_answer: Unbound separates financial statement classification from fund advisory designation. Each account type carries one CPA-approved accounting treatment determined from its transfer-instrument terms, not marketing labels: contribution without donor restrictions (variance power granted, advisory privileges only), contribution with donor restrictions, agency or pass-through liability, or equity transaction (CNV-FIN-008, UNB-XIN-ACC-001). Receipts into liability-treated accounts never increase contribution revenue or Schedule D DAF aggregates. A DAF subfund designation does not by itself imply donor-restricted net assets (ACC-MDL-008, UNB-ACC-033). Cash and assets held, fund net asset balances, grant commitments, restricted net assets and available-to-recommend amounts are distinct; available-to-recommend is a controlled projection, not a GL account (ACC-MDL-004). Pledges, conditional gifts and contingent commitments are modeled separately from settled assets (UNB-ACC-032). An account type without an approved treatment cannot accept receipts.
intended_practice: Ship an account-type register whose treatment field is approved by the sponsor's CPA before activation; the posting policy derives revenue versus liability from it.
owner: Not assigned; proposed: Unbound ledger product owner (role not staffed) with each sponsor's controller as accounting-policy owner

title: Grant expense recognition and period-end cutoff
target_answer: Each sponsor book declares an effective-dated grant recognition point: approval communicated to the grantee (default), sponsor approval (only under a documented sponsor policy that approval creates the obligation with no free rescission right) or payment released (only where payment is the first communication) (CNV-FIN-007, which supersedes the narrower rule in UNB-XIN-ACC-002). Approval, communication, condition and rescission evidence is always captured; a recommendation alone never creates a payable (UNB-SCTRL-026). Conditional grants carry no expense until a recorded barrier-met or waiver event. At each period end a cutoff register lists approved-but-uncommunicated, communicated-but-unpaid and conditional grants with their recognition status.
intended_practice: Generate the cutoff register automatically from grant lifecycle facts; recognition rule versions are CPA-approved.
owner: Not assigned; proposed: Unbound ledger product owner (role not staffed) with each sponsor's controller as accounting-policy owner

title: Period close, period locks and late-arriving events
target_answer: Accounting periods have soft and hard close states, close checklists and reopen approvals (UNB-ACC-017). Every posting reads the period row with a shared lock (or runs serializable) and a hard close takes an exclusive lock, so a posting cannot slip into a period while it closes; a posting dated in a hard-closed period is rejected with PERIOD_CLOSED and recorded instead as a prior-period adjustment in the first open period carrying the original relates-to period and effective date, with controller approval above a sponsor threshold (UNB-XIN-EVA-002). A hard-closed period may be reopened only before its statements are issued and only with controller and CFO approval. Closed periods remain immutable and originally issued statements are preserved (ACC-MDL-010). Unbalanced or unexplained control-account breaks block unsupported close certification (ACC-MDL-009), and the preparer cannot certify their own close (UNB-SCTRL-027).
intended_practice: Implement period state as a locked row with transactional checks; close certification is a separate command subject to SoD.
owner: Not assigned; proposed: Unbound ledger product owner (role not staffed) with each sponsor's controller as accounting-policy owner

title: Audit adjustments, prior-period adjustments and accounting changes
target_answer: Each fiscal year has an AuditAdjustment period after period 12 that accepts only journals linked to an auditor finding (auditor reference, proposer, controller decision); every proposed adjustment is recorded as Booked or Passed with amount and rationale, and Passed items feed a summary of unadjusted differences (UNB-XIN-ACC-005, CNV-FIN-011). Audited statements are generated from period 12 plus audit-adjustment journals. Every posting-rule change and every correction of a posted error carries an AccountingChangeRecord classified by an authorized controller as change in principle, change in estimate or error correction, with materiality assessment and CPA approval reference; changes in principle recast comparatives as separately versioned as-adjusted reports while preserving as-originally-issued reports (UNB-XIN-ACC-004). After issuance, late items post as immaterial current-period corrections with disclosure or as material restatements, judged against the sponsor's materiality setting agreed with its auditor (UNB-XIN-EVA-002).
intended_practice: Model audit findings and accounting changes as first-class records that gate the journals they authorize.
owner: Not assigned; proposed: Unbound ledger product owner (role not staffed) with each sponsor's controller as accounting-policy owner

title: Multi-entity and multi-sponsor ledgers, isolation and book of record
target_answer: Unbound runs one double-entry journal component serving distinct entity books with separate permissions (CNV-FIN-012). Each sponsor tenant has its own schema and database role with row-level security on every tenant table and negative isolation tests, and can move to a dedicated database when risk or contract requires (CNV-ARC-001, UNB-ACC-027). Cross-tenant authorization is enforced for append, projection, replay, export and correction (UNB-IMM-009). Multiple legal entities, intercompany and interfund transactions and eliminations are supported where authorized (UNB-ACC-015). For each entity and function the sponsor designates Unbound as Authoritative, Shadow or NotUsed; in Shadow mode Unbound never posts to that function and reconciles daily to the external book, and changing designation requires a cutover record with opening-balance tie-out (UNB-XIN-ACC-010). Transfers between sponsors post as independent entries in each sponsor's books (UNB-XIN-EVA-009).
intended_practice: Implement per-tenant schema and role isolation with a negative test suite run on every release.
owner: Not assigned; proposed: Unbound ledger product owner (role not staffed) with each sponsor's controller as accounting-policy owner

title: Audit support, reproducible statements and DAF regulatory bridges
target_answer: Unbound supports audit schedules, roll-forwards, workpapers, transaction drill-down from statement line to source event and evidence, external auditor access and independently verifiable as-of snapshots (UNB-ACC-020). Every report figure is computed from a sealed snapshot identified by entity, period and ledger commit watermark, so the same report recomputed later is identical (UNB-XIN-EVA-003). For each sponsor and tax year a DAF bridge reconciles Form 990 Schedule D Part I values, the sum of fund statements and the DAF component of audited net assets using only typed reconciling items; any unexplained residual blocks sign-off (UNB-XIN-ACC-006, CNV-FIN-009). Folio renders versioned statements and audit packages with source, policy and template provenance (UNB-ACC-025).
intended_practice: Provide an auditor portal and generated audit package per period built from sealed snapshots.
owner: Not assigned; proposed: Unbound ledger product owner (role not staffed) with each sponsor's controller as accounting-policy owner

title: Chart of accounts mapping and general ledger export to sponsor ERP
target_answer: Unbound provides a configurable, versioned chart of accounts with entity, sponsor, program, fund, restriction, currency and other approved dimensions and enforces dimension validity (UNB-ACC-001). By default the sponsor's ERP remains the book of record for entity financial statements, accounts payable, payroll and fixed assets; Unbound exports balanced, summarized, dimension-complete journals for DAF program activity to that ERP and reconciles the receiving control accounts (RR-UNB-ACC-012-r1, CNV-FIN-012). Exports carry control totals, the source snapshot identifier and the mapping version; imports from ERP, bank and custodian feeds are reconciliation sources and never silently replace Unbound's authoritative books (UNB-ACC-028).
intended_practice: Publish a versioned account mapping per sponsor and an export manifest with control totals; reconcile ERP control accounts daily or per sponsor frequency.
owner: Not assigned; proposed: Unbound ledger product owner (role not staffed) with each sponsor's controller as accounting-policy owner

title: Agent identity and attribution of agent actions
target_answer: Every agent, in engineering and in the product, has a unique non-shared identity distinct from human users. Each action records agent identity, model and prompt version, tool, initiating human or principal, delegation chain and effective permission (AIN-013). Agent credentials are short-lived and bound to the run. Sub-agent delegation carries attribution and cannot amplify authority (AIN-010). Records are append-only and tamper-evident, retained as audit evidence.
intended_practice: Extend the Praxis actor model to runtime agents through the Unbound evidence envelope (SOC2-002) and AIN-013 fields.
owner: Not assigned (proposed: Echelon engineering owner for Praxis; Unbound platform owner for runtime)

title: Least privilege and deterministic authorization for agents
target_answer: Agent permissions are declared in the authority matrix per command class and actor type, approved by an authorized human, and enforced by deterministic server-side code. Unmapped commands are refused. Agents cannot grant or change their own permissions or approve their own outputs. In release 1 no agent can execute anything above A2. Repeated out-of-authority requests are rate-limited and reported to the agent owner, never escalated into a decision. Agent permissions are reviewed periodically and on change, and unused permissions are removed.
intended_practice: Implement CNV-GOV-010 and GOV-AUTH-001 through 004 and AUTH-T01, T04 negative tests.
owner: Not assigned (proposed: Unbound platform owner)

title: Reserved human authority for consequential actions; agents never hold human-authority operations or clear risk
target_answer: AI agents may observe, prepare and recommend. They never approve grants, release payments, change bank or payee details, instruct trades, clear sanctions, fraud or eligibility concerns, or exercise any reserved authority. Only an authorized human, or a deterministic rule that a sponsor board has delegated in writing with limits and expiry, can clear or decide. Approval binds to a hash of the exact proposal and evidence; any material change invalidates it. The approver must be someone other than the preparer, and the agent that initiated a transaction cannot attest to its reconciliation. Anti-rubber-stamp measures include risk-stratified sampling of approved items, approval-time metrics and required review of the deterministic findings section.
intended_practice: Implement the authority matrix with A4 and A5 tiers and the approval binding before any agent feature ships.
owner: Not assigned (proposed: sponsor board for delegation; Unbound product owner for enforcement)

title: Interruptibility, emergency stop and safe degradation
target_answer: Authorized humans can suspend a single agent, an agent class or all agents immediately. Queued autonomous actions are safely suspended, in-flight steps settle to an explicit state, and nothing irreversible proceeds after the stop. Deterministic processes continue without AI. Resumption requires recorded approval and revalidation of authority and evidence (AIN-017, AIN-020). Emergency stop is tested on a schedule and evidence of each test is kept.
intended_practice: Implement per GOV-AUTH-024 and AUTH-T07.
owner: Not assigned (proposed: Echelon operations owner)

title: Decision accountability records and explainability
target_answer: Every consequential decision has a record naming the accountable human or delegated rule, the exact evidence snapshot, what AI contributed and in which model and prompt version, the policy version applied and the outcome. Facts, inferences, recommendations and decisions are labeled distinctly. Affected parties can challenge an AI-contributed fact and get independent human review with preserved provenance. Decision packages can be replayed and rendered for auditors and examiners.
intended_practice: Implement the evidence envelope (SOC2-002) and Folio decision packages.
owner: Not assigned (proposed: Unbound product owner)

title: Reliability of AI-generated or AI-processed control and audit evidence
target_answer: Control evidence is produced by deterministic systems as a byproduct of operation, signed and hash-chained, never authored by AI. AI may summarize or extract, but summaries are labeled, link to the underlying records and are never accepted as evidence on their own. Agents have no write or delete access to evidence or logs. Test and synthetic evidence is labeled and stored apart from production evidence. When an AI summary is found wrong, the summary is withdrawn, dependent assertions are flagged and the correction is recorded.
intended_practice: Implement the evidence envelope and continuous control monitoring with AI restricted to labeled summaries.
owner: Not assigned (proposed: Echelon compliance owner)

title: Reliability of AI-completed questionnaires and customer-facing assertions
target_answer: Echelon tells customers when questionnaire answers are AI-drafted. Every answer is generated from a canonical answer unit with a controlled status, a customer statement that the build tool checks against that status, cited evidence and sources, and a named human signatory who reviews and accepts accountability before release. Answers are reproducible: the same answer unit yields the same response across questionnaires, and changes are versioned.
intended_practice: Define a release step requiring a named human signatory per questionnaire response and record it.
owner: Not assigned (proposed: Echelon managing member as signatory)

title: Governance of AI agents in engineering and operations: change approval, segregation and access
target_answer: AI coding and operations agents can propose changes but cannot merge to protected branches, release, deploy or change production configuration without approval by an authorized human who did not prompt the change; control-relevant modules need two such approvers (CNV-PLT-010). An agent or model session cannot both author and approve. Agents get no standing production access and no break-glass access; production operations by agents are limited to read-only diagnostics scoped and approved per CNV-ARC-002, with any write requiring per-case human approval. A named human is accountable for every merged change regardless of author.
intended_practice: Configure branch protection and CI approval rules across Echelon repositories and document them; apply CNV-ARC-002 operator access rules to agents.
owner: Not assigned (proposed: Echelon engineering owner)

title: AI system and AI use inventory, including AI used to build and operate the service
target_answer: Echelon maintains one machine-readable AI inventory generated from configuration rather than assembled by hand. Each entry names the AI system or use (product feature, internal assistant, AI coding agent, operations agent), its owner, model provider and model version, prompt and tool versions, data classes it may access, tenants in scope, authority ceiling from the authority matrix, and the risk assessment that approved it. Product agents are registered through the capability manifest that the tool broker enforces, so an agent that is not in the inventory cannot obtain tools. Engineering agents are registered through Praxis execution identity. Customers receive a tenant-specific extract on request.
intended_practice: Build the inventory from the Unbound agent capability manifest (AIN-002), Praxis execution identity records and the vendor inventory, and reconcile them on every release.
owner: Not assigned (proposed: Echelon AI governance owner)

title: AI policy, accountable ownership and acceptable use
target_answer: A board- or owner-approved AI policy states permitted and prohibited AI uses, the rule that AI may recommend and prepare but never hold human-authority operations or clear risk concerns (NoAiClearance), data handling rules for AI tools (no customer data in unmanaged tools), an accountable AI risk owner, an exception process with expiry, and AI literacy training for every person and agent operator. The policy is versioned in source control and its rules are enforced where possible by the tool broker and authority matrix rather than by attestation.
intended_practice: Draft an AI policy from the existing invariants (EDF AGENTS.md, CNV-AIO-001, GOV-AUTH-003) and the Unbound authority tiers A0 to A5, and adopt it formally.
owner: Not assigned (proposed: Echelon managing member)

title: Alignment with NIST AI RMF and ISO/IEC 42001, and independent assessment of AI governance
target_answer: Echelon publishes a crosswalk from its AI controls to the NIST AI RMF functions and the Generative AI Profile, ISO/IEC 42001 Annex A and the CSA AI Controls Matrix, generated from the control register so it cannot drift. Each mapped control links to continuously produced evidence. Echelon decides on ISO/IEC 42001 certification by customer demand and cost, and in the meantime offers the crosswalk plus SOC 2 coverage of agent controls (SOC2-017) as its assurance path.
intended_practice: Produce the crosswalk once AI controls exist in the control register; evaluate ISO/IEC 42001 certification after SOC 2 readiness.
owner: Not assigned (proposed: Echelon compliance owner)

title: AI risk and impact assessment before deployment and on change
target_answer: Every AI use passes a recorded risk and impact assessment before activation and on any model, prompt, tool, data or use change. The assessment classifies the use against the authority tiers, identifies affected people (donors, advisors, grantees, staff), evaluates accuracy, bias, security, privacy and misuse, records the regulatory classification (EU AI Act, Colorado AI Act) and names the human decision owner. Assessments for any automated scoring that affects people include measured error rates by relevant subgroup. Activation is refused by the release gate when no current assessment exists.
intended_practice: Use the SOC2-030 design review as the gate and extend it with an AI impact template aligned to ISO/IEC 42005 and NIST AI RMF MAP functions.
owner: Not assigned (proposed: Echelon AI governance owner)

title: AI model and AI provider due diligence
target_answer: AI providers are tiered as vendors and, when they process customer data, as subprocessors. Before adoption Echelon reviews the provider's assurance reports and complementary user entity controls, data retention and training terms, model documentation (system cards, evaluations, known limitations), deprecation policy and incident history. Models are pinned by version; provider-initiated changes trigger the change process and re-run of the frozen evaluation set before production use. Open-weight models are accepted only with a recorded license review and verified artifact provenance.
intended_practice: Apply the critical-vendor register (RR-REQ-X-073-r2) to AI providers and add model-specific fields.
owner: Not assigned (proposed: Echelon vendor risk owner)

title: AI provider data retention, training use and confidentiality terms
target_answer: Echelon commits contractually that customer data is not used to train or fine-tune any model, by Echelon or any provider, without the customer's separate written opt-in, and it uses only provider offerings whose terms prohibit training on inputs and outputs. Echelon records, per provider, prompt and output retention periods, abuse-monitoring human review terms, zero-retention eligibility and processing region, and it selects zero or minimal retention where available. Evaluation sets built from customer data require the same opt-in and are tenant-scoped.
intended_practice: Record provider terms in the vendor register and publish a customer-facing AI data use statement based on business plan section 10.04.
owner: Not assigned (proposed: Echelon privacy owner)

title: Applicability of AI-specific law (EU AI Act, Colorado AI Act, state automated decision rules, NAIC bulletin)
target_answer: Echelon maintains, in its regulatory applicability register, one row per AI law with its role (provider, deployer, developer), the assessed classification of each AI use, the facts relied on, counsel review date and the triggers for re-evaluation. For EU AI Act, Echelon records whether any system falls in Article 6 and Annex III, which transparency duties under Article 50 apply and its AI literacy measures under Article 4. For the Colorado AI Act, Echelon records whether any AI use is a substantial factor in a consequential decision and, if so, provides deployers the documentation the law requires. Echelon supports insurer customers' third-party AI oversight under the NAIC model bulletin with documentation and audit cooperation.
intended_practice: Add AI law rows to the UNB-REGMAP register and obtain counsel review before any customer-facing AI capability ships.
owner: Not assigned (proposed: Echelon counsel)

title: Model risk management support for bank customers (SR 11-7 and OCC 2011-12 expectations applied to vendor models)
target_answer: Echelon classifies each quantitative or AI component by whether a bank customer would treat it as a model (for example sanctions match scoring, risk tiering, anomaly detection). For each, Echelon provides a model documentation package: purpose, conceptual design, data and assumptions, limitations, evaluation results on frozen test sets, monitoring metrics and change history, with advance notice of material changes. Deterministic rules are documented as rules, not models. Generative AI used only to draft labeled narrative is documented as a tool that cannot alter findings, which narrows what the customer must validate.
intended_practice: Generate model documentation packages through Folio from the model and prompt version records required by RR-AIN-027-r1.
owner: Not assigned (proposed: Unbound product owner)

title: Transparency to customers and end users about AI use, including AI-assisted software development
target_answer: Echelon publishes and keeps current an AI use statement covering product AI features, the providers behind them, the data each receives and the authority each holds, and states plainly that Echelon builds its software largely with AI coding agents under human-controlled review and release gates. AI-generated content is labeled in the product and in donor or grantee communications. Each tenant can disable AI features without losing deterministic functions. New AI features or providers that process tenant data follow the subprocessor notice process.
intended_practice: Publish the AI use statement from the AI inventory; implement tenant-level AI disable switch as a configuration flag enforced by the tool broker.
owner: Not assigned (proposed: Echelon AI governance owner)

title: Prompt injection containment, direct and indirect
target_answer: Echelon assumes prompt injection will sometimes succeed and limits what a successful injection can do. Product agents hold only A0 to A2 authority, every tool call is authorized by deterministic code against the principal's recorded authority (CNV-AIO-001), tools that can send data outside the tenant are removed by the broker for tasks that read untrusted content, and AI narrative cannot change or reorder deterministic findings shown to approvers. Uploaded documents are parsed into typed data at the Limen and Strata boundaries and passed to models as quoted data. Classifiers and prompt hardening are secondary layers measured in the adversarial suite. Engineering agents that read untrusted repositories, issues or web pages run with no production credentials and their changes pass human-controlled review and release gates.
intended_practice: Implement the tool broker and authority matrix first; then add the adversarial suite required by RR-AIN-027-r1.
owner: Not assigned (proposed: Unbound platform security owner, with Tutela as security engineering discipline)

title: Tenant isolation of AI context, retrieval, caching and memory
target_answer: AI context is assembled only through tenant-scoped APIs under the requesting principal's authority, never from shared stores. Any embedding index, prompt cache, conversation memory or evaluation set is partitioned per tenant and keyed by tenant identity, and retrieval re-checks authorization at query time. Provider-side prompt caching is used only where cache scope is per account and Echelon's account structure prevents cross-tenant reuse. Engineering and operations agents have no standing access to production tenant data. Cross-tenant leakage tests run in CI with canary records.
intended_practice: Extend CNV-ARC-001 tenant partitioning to every AI store and add canary-based leakage tests to the isolation test suite.
owner: Not assigned (proposed: Unbound platform security owner)

title: Tool misuse and excessive agency
target_answer: Each agent task receives the smallest tool set needed, expressed as typed F# commands with validated parameters. Tools execute through the same server-side authorization as human calls, under the principal's identity, never a privileged service identity. Parameters that change money, recipients or authority are not agent-settable at all. Tools with external egress (email, web requests, rendering of remote URLs) are unavailable to tasks that process untrusted content. Every run has token, tool-call, time and cost budgets and stops safely when they are exhausted.
intended_practice: Implement per CNV-GOV-010 authority matrix and RR-AIN-028-r1 budgets.
owner: Not assigned (proposed: Unbound platform owner)

title: Handling of model output as untrusted
target_answer: Model output is untrusted input. It is parsed into typed values or rendered as plain text with contextual encoding; it is never executed as code, SQL, shell or HTML, and remote resources it references are not fetched or rendered automatically. Outputs carry a type (Proposal, Finding, Explanation) and a label so they cannot be stored or displayed as authoritative records. Factual claims in AI narrative must cite stored evidence; uncited claims are marked as unverified.
intended_practice: Apply SEC-UI-001, SEC-UI-002 and SEC-EXEC-001 to all AI output paths and implement typed AI output per RR-UNB-AI-STD-003-r1.
owner: Not assigned (proposed: Unbound platform owner)

title: AI supply chain: models, AI libraries, agent frameworks, tool servers and data
target_answer: Models, AI SDKs, agent frameworks, tool servers and datasets are dependencies under SEC-SUPPLY-001: approved, pinned, provenance-verified and listed in the SBOM with AI-specific fields (model identifier, provider, version, dataset lineage). Third-party tool servers connected to any agent are approved per server and per tool, run with scoped credentials, and are re-reviewed on version change. Retrieval corpora and evaluation sets have recorded lineage and write access limited to deterministic ingestion jobs. Agent credentials are short-lived, scoped and never present in prompts or agent-readable files.
intended_practice: Extend SEC-SUPPLY-001 and the SBOM process to AI components and add a tool server approval list.

title: Security of AI-generated code in Echelon's own software
target_answer: Echelon states openly that most code is written by AI coding agents and shows why that is acceptable: (1) language and architecture remove whole weakness classes regardless of author (memory-unsafe code, dynamic SQL, HTML injection sinks, arbitrary evaluation); (2) every change, whoever writes it, passes the same release gates: compiler with warnings as errors, property and negative tests, SAST, SCA with dependency allow-listing that defeats hallucinated or typosquatted packages, secret scanning; (3) changes to control-relevant modules need review by a human who did not prompt the change (CNV-PLT-010); (4) agents cannot weaken tests or gates, because changes to tests, gate configuration and security rules are themselves control-relevant; (5) Praxis records which agent, model and run produced each change, so defects can be traced to their source; (6) defect and vulnerability rates of agent-written code are measured and published to customers.

title: Sanctions screening coverage and timing across parties and the grant lifecycle
target_answer: Donors, advisors, successors, grantees and payors are screened at onboarding, re-screened automatically whenever a list changes, and screened again immediately before each irreversible release; a match found during release prevents transmission because the check and the dispatch are one atomic step. title: Screening list freshness and fail-closed behavior
target_answer: Echelon ingests official list updates from OFAC (and other configured sources) within a defined bound, verifies integrity of the downloaded data, versions each list snapshot, and triggers delta re-screening of all parties. title: Name matching method, threshold tuning, effectiveness testing and subgroup fairness
target_answer: The matching method (normalization, transliteration, token, phonetic and edit-distance components, secondary identifiers) is documented. title: Alert disposition, blocking and rejecting, and OFAC reporting

Prior false-positive dispositions are reused only within the same sponsor and expire on subject or list change, new match, 12 months or reviewer authority revocation. title: Charity-specific diligence: Treasury guidelines, foreign grants, prohibited benefits and grant fraud red flags
