A release fails if a new store or column lacks an inventory entry (CNV-TEN-001 AC-2 and AC-3). Data flow diagrams are generated from the same source.
intended_practice: Implement the isolation map and SharedStoreRegister as schema-checked registers; generate flow diagrams.
owner: Unassigned; proposed data owner (Unbound architecture)

title: Third-party service and external attack-surface inventory
target_answer: Echelon maintains a service inventory listing each third-party and subservice organization, the data classes it receives, the tenants affected, criticality, contract and assurance status, and a fallback. New SaaS tools, including AI assistants, require approval before receiving company or customer data. An external attack-surface inventory of domains, certificates and endpoints is generated from DNS and deployment configuration and monitored for unexpected exposure.
intended_practice: Create the service inventory alongside vendor risk management; automate attack-surface inventory from deployment configuration.
owner: Unassigned; proposed Security Lead

title: Secure configuration baselines and drift detection, including database privileges
target_answer: All infrastructure, container, cloud service and database configuration is declared in version control and deployed only through reviewed pipelines. Baselines derive from CIS Benchmarks where applicable, with documented deviations. Drift is detected continuously and either reverted automatically or raised as an incident. For PostgreSQL, Strata compiles declared schema, grants and row-level security policies into an artifact, diffs it against the live database before every deployment, and reports items it could not compare as not-compared or unverifiable rather than as matches, so an unverifiable configuration is never reported as compliant.
intended_practice: Adopt Strata for schema, grant and policy baselines; adopt infrastructure-as-code with CIS-derived baselines; run drift detection continuously.
owner: Unassigned; proposed Engineering Lead

title: Asset ownership, classification and secure decommissioning
target_answer: Every inventoried asset has an owner, classification and lifecycle state. Decommissioning follows a recorded plan: credentials and certificates revoked, data destroyed by tenant-scoped key destruction under dual control or by media sanitization consistent with NIST SP 800-88 on provider-managed media (relying on provider attestations), and a destruction certificate issued that states what persists (for example immutable backups until expiry). Orphaned resources are found by daily reconciliation against provider billing and APIs.
intended_practice: Implement owner and classification fields in the generated inventory; implement tenant key destruction and certificates.
owner: Unassigned; proposed Engineering Lead

title: SOC 2 examination status, scope and use
target_answer: Echelon will obtain a SOC 2 Type I followed by a Type II examination covering Security and Availability, plus Confidentiality and Processing Integrity for Unbound, with a system description scoped to the named product, environment and legal entity. Controls emit evidence as a byproduct of operation (SOC2-004) so the observation period is cheap to evidence. Exceptions and opinion modifications are disclosed with remediation. We publish the complementary user entity controls customers must operate and the carved-out subservice organizations with how we monitor them.
intended_practice: Readiness through continuous evidence; Type I after first production release, Type II after a 6 to 12 month observation period.
owner: Managing member of Echelon Foundry, LLC (role not yet formally assigned)

title: SOC 1 relevance for customers' financial reporting
target_answer: Because Unbound records ledgers, fund balances, fees and grant payments that flow into sponsors' financial statements, Echelon will provide a SOC 1 Type II report under SSAE 18 AT-C 320 with control objectives for transaction recording, NAV and unitization, fee computation, grant authorization and payment file preparation, and information produced by the entity. Customer auditors may contact the service auditor and Echelon for reliance purposes.
intended_practice: Design control objectives with a CPA firm in parallel with the SOC 2 readiness.
owner: Managing member of Echelon Foundry, LLC (role not yet formally assigned)

title: Bridge letters and assurance coverage gaps
target_answer: Within 15 business days of request, Echelon issues a bridge letter signed by management covering the period from the report end date to the requested date, stating whether material changes to the system or controls occurred and whether any known deficiencies exist. Because a bridge letter is a management assertion, we supplement it with access to continuous control evidence for the gap period. Report periods are planned so the gap to customers' common fiscal year ends does not exceed three months.
intended_practice: Template bridge letter and evidence feed once the first report is issued.
owner: Managing member of Echelon Foundry, LLC (role not yet formally assigned)

title: ISO and other certifications and program authorizations
target_answer: We hold certifications that our customers' requirements actually justify, chosen by evidence of customer demand rather than in advance. Likely sequence: CSA STAR Level 1 self-assessment (low cost, public CAIQ), then SOC 2, then ISO/IEC 27001 if international or enterprise demand appears, and ISO/IEC 42001 if AI governance assurance is demanded. Any certificate comes from an accredited certification body with its scope published. PCI DSS is out of scope while card acceptance is disabled (CNV-PAY-008); public-sector authorizations are not pursued unless a public-sector customer requires them.
intended_practice: Complete a CAIQ-based self-assessment once controls exist; decide on ISO from recorded customer demand.
owner: Managing member of Echelon Foundry, LLC (role not yet formally assigned)

title: Independent technical assessment reports and labeling of first-party assessments
target_answer: We share, under NDA, an attestation letter from an independent penetration tester with tester identity, qualifications, dates, scope and findings summary by severity with remediation status, at least annually and after major architecture change. First-party assessments (architectural assurance matrix, scanner validation, monthly assurance summary) are labeled first-party in their title and metadata. Customers may run their own security testing under an agreed rules-of-engagement document.
intended_practice: Commission an independent test before production launch of Unbound.
owner: Managing member of Echelon Foundry, LLC (role not yet formally assigned)

title: Right to audit and regulator access
target_answer: The agreement grants the customer, its auditors and its regulators the right to audit Echelon's compliance with its obligations once per year on 30 days' notice, and at any time after a security incident or regulatory request, with each party bearing its own costs unless the audit finds material non-compliance. Regulators receive access to records, personnel and systems as required by law (for example Bank Service Company Act examination authority over services to banks, DORA Article 30 for EU financial entities). Audit rights flow down to critical subcontractors where we can obtain them, and where we cannot (large cloud providers), we provide their independent reports. We offer audit evidence remotely through time-bounded, reproducible evidence packages to reduce fieldwork. Findings are remediated on agreed timelines and re-tested.
intended_practice: Include audit and regulator access clauses in the standard agreement; build evidence package export.
owner: Managing member of Echelon Foundry, LLC (role not yet formally assigned)

title: Internal audit, continuous control monitoring and evidence integrity
target_answer: Controls emit attributable, time-stamped, tamper-evident evidence as a byproduct of operation; a missing expected control heartbeat raises an exception; production evidence is labeled separately from test or synthetic evidence. Because there is no internal audit function, an external reviewer independent of the control operator tests a sample of controls semi-annually, and no control is verified solely by the person or AI agent that operates it.
intended_practice: Implement continuous control monitoring for Unbound; engage external reviewer.
owner: Managing member of Echelon Foundry, LLC (role not yet formally assigned)

title: Auditor qualification and integrity of assurance claims
target_answer: Our SOC examinations are performed by a licensed CPA firm with a current AICPA peer review, whose name we disclose. Every public statement of assurance status (trust center, website, questionnaires, contracts) is generated from a single assurance record and cannot claim a report type, period or scope beyond what the issued report states. We keep a dated history of every public assurance statement and correction.
intended_practice: Generate trust center statements from this repository's answer units.
owner: Managing member of Echelon Foundry, LLC (role not yet formally assigned)

title: Multi-factor authentication coverage for workforce and administrators
target_answer: MFA is enforced at the workforce identity provider for every workforce and contractor account and every system federated to it, including email, source control, package registries, cloud consoles, CI/CD and support tools; systems that cannot federate are listed with their own MFA configuration evidence. All workforce authenticators are phishing-resistant (AAL2 minimum); platform privileged roles use AAL3-grade hardware or device-bound keys with two registered keys per person. There are no standing MFA exceptions; any temporary exception requires CISO approval, an expiry and a compensating control.
intended_practice: Select a workforce IdP that enforces phishing-resistant MFA by policy and enroll all personnel before production.
owner: Unassigned; proposed Security Lead

title: Phishing-resistant authenticators and resistance to MFA bypass
target_answer: Workforce users authenticate only with phishing-resistant authenticators (FIDO2/WebAuthn security keys or device-bound platform authenticators). Customer users are offered passkeys as the default and phishing-resistant options at no extra cost; SMS and voice codes are not offered for workforce and, for customers, are only a restricted fallback with compensating controls (cooling-off and sponsor-direct confirmation for high-risk actions). Synced passkeys are accepted for sign-in at AAL2 but are not sufficient alone for high-risk actions such as adding a new grant recipient. Push-based approval, if used, requires number matching. Session tokens are bound to the authenticated client where the platform supports it to reduce adversary-in-the-middle token theft. Accessible alternatives exist for users who cannot use device-bound authenticators.
intended_practice: Implement WebAuthn for all populations from the first release and treat other factors as restricted.
owner: Unassigned; proposed Security Lead

title: Customer federation: SSO via SAML 2.0 and OpenID Connect
target_answer: Unbound supports SAML 2.0 and OpenID Connect federation for sponsor and partner workforce on all plans without a surcharge. Customers can require SSO-only sign-in and disable local credentials for their realm. Assertions are validated for signature, issuer, audience, recipient, time window and replay using a maintained library, with negative tests for known assertion attacks (signature wrapping, unsigned assertions, algorithm confusion). Identities are mapped by issuer plus subject, never by email; mapping changes need dual control and notice to the affected person. A compromised partner IdP can at most sign users into that partner's realm, and cannot satisfy step-up for high-risk actions, which uses a sponsor-controlled verifier.
intended_practice: Select a maintained federation library; implement validation negative tests; implement realm-scoped trust per IdP.
owner: Unassigned; proposed Security Lead

title: Automated user lifecycle via SCIM and federated deprovisioning latency
target_answer: Unbound exposes a SCIM 2.0 endpoint per customer realm, authenticated with a dedicated, scoped, rotatable credential and rate-limited, that can create, update and deactivate users and group-based role assignments but cannot create platform or sponsor-reserved privileged roles. Deactivation through SCIM revokes sessions, refresh tokens, API tokens and delegated agent grants for that principal on the next request, within a stated maximum latency that is a contractual term. Open items owned by a deactivated user (pending recommendations, approval tasks) are reassigned or held by sponsor policy, never silently executed.
intended_practice: Implement SCIM with scoped credentials; define and measure deprovisioning latency.
owner: Unassigned; proposed Security Lead

title: Password policy aligned to NIST SP 800-63-4 and credential storage
target_answer: Passwords are optional for customers (passkeys are the default) and not used alone for workforce. Where passwords are used, the policy follows NIST SP 800-63B-4: length-based minimums with no composition rules, a generous maximum length, screening against breached and commonly used passwords, paste and password managers allowed, no security questions, no periodic forced rotation, and forced change on evidence of compromise. Passwords are stored with a memory-hard or iterated, salted password hashing function from an approved library. Online guessing is throttled per account and per source with bot detection, designed so that throttling cannot be used to lock legitimate users out at will. Where a customer contract or PCI-scoped context requires periodic rotation, the conflict is documented and resolved by MFA rather than rotation.
intended_practice: Implement 800-63B-4 password handling if passwords are supported at all.
owner: Unassigned; proposed Security Lead

title: Session management, token handling and revocation
target_answer: Browser sessions use opaque, server-side session identifiers in cookies marked Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite, never placed in browser-readable storage; new identifiers are issued at login and at any privilege change. Idle and absolute timeouts are risk-tiered (shorter for staff and privileged roles) and configurable by the sponsor within platform limits. Users and administrators can list and terminate sessions. Password, authenticator or contact changes, deactivation and authority changes revoke or recheck all sessions and refresh tokens within a stated maximum staleness. API refresh tokens rotate on use with reuse detection, and long-lived API tokens are scoped, expiring and revocable.
intended_practice: Decide session architecture compatible with the Limen kernel boundary; implement revocation and timeouts.
owner: Unassigned; proposed Security Lead

title: Account recovery, authenticator changes and help-desk resets
target_answer: Recovery after loss of all authenticators requires re-proofing at the original assurance level (or a pre-registered second authenticator), never knowledge-based questions or email alone. Enrolling an authenticator, changing email, phone or recovery factors notifies the previous channel with a revert link and starts a cooling-off period (default 72 hours, sponsor-configurable) during which authority changes, successor changes and new-recipient grants above a threshold are held for confirmation. Support staff cannot reset authenticators or change contact details beyond the contact assurance matrix and cannot override it. Accessible recovery paths (mailed code, outbound call to a verified number, captioned assisted video, in-person or notarized verification, relay calls) each reach a defined assurance level.
intended_practice: Implement recovery, cooling-off and contact assurance matrix as part of the identity core.
owner: Unassigned; proposed Security Lead

title: Step-up authentication and transaction binding for high-risk and financial actions
target_answer: Each high-risk action class (authenticator or recovery change, authority or delegation change, payee or destination change, data export, grant recommendation above a sponsor threshold, API credential creation, sponsor policy publication) has a required assurance level and maximum authentication age in one StepUpPolicy matrix. The step-up event identifier is bound to the specific command and its parameters; a command without a fresh, matching step-up is rejected, and a step-up cannot be reused for another action. The step-up prompt shows the action's key details so the user confirms what will happen. Step-up is performed by a sponsor-controlled verifier, not delegated to a partner IdP. Auto-approval ceilings depend on session assurance, so a phishable or agent-initiated session cannot obtain an auto-approved grant to a new recipient. This implements the layered, risk-based approach of the FFIEC 2021 authentication guidance for the sponsor's and partner bank's customers.
intended_practice: Implement the StepUpPolicy matrix in the authorization core with command binding.
owner: Unassigned; proposed Security Lead

title: Authentication of APIs, widgets, webhooks and AI agents
target_answer: Partner and integration APIs use OAuth 2.0 client credentials or mutual TLS with per-client, scoped, expiring credentials; shared static API keys are not issued for new integrations. User-delegated API access uses OAuth authorization code with PKCE and scoped, short-lived access tokens. Embedded widgets run in an isolated origin and receive narrowly scoped, short-lived tokens never exposed to host-page scripts; they expire and clear data when authority changes. Inbound webhooks are signed, timestamped and replay-protected; outbound webhooks are signed. AI agents authenticate as their own Workload principals with delegated grants derived from a user, and an agent session is treated as lower assurance than a fresh human step-up for high-risk actions.
intended_practice: Define API authentication standards per UNB-API-STD-005 before the first integration.
owner: Unassigned; proposed Security Lead

title: Server-side, deny-by-default, centrally enforced authorization
target_answer: All Unbound capabilities are reachable only through governed F# command and query handlers. A handler cannot be registered without declaring its command class in the authority matrix; the build fails if a handler lacks a classification, and the runtime refuses unclassified commands with UnclassifiedCommand. The handler signature requires an authorization proof value that only the central authorization module can construct, so an unauthorized call path does not type-check. Decisions are evaluated server-side in the same transaction as the state change; browser-side logic in the Limen engine is display-only. Background jobs, exports, analytics, support tools and agents use the same handlers and the same proof requirement; there is no privileged side door other than break-glass.
intended_practice: Implement the authorization core and handler registration so that missing classification fails the build and missing proof fails compilation; keep negative tests as a second line.
owner: Unassigned; proposed Engineering Lead with Security Lead

title: Object-level and property-level authorization (BOLA, IDOR, mass assignment)
target_answer: Queries are constructed only through the persistence layer, which requires a VerifiedTenantContext and the principal's relationship scope; a query function that returns funds, grants or parties takes the scope as a parameter and filters at the database, so code cannot ask for 'fund 123' without asking 'fund 123 as visible to this principal'. Out-of-scope identifiers return not-found, not forbidden, and record a denial event. Commands accept explicit, versioned input schemas per role (no binding of arbitrary fields), and responses are projected per role so non-permitted fields never leave the server. Function-level authorization (what the principal may do) and object-level authorization (to which object) are both required. Identifiers may be unguessable but security never depends on that.
intended_practice: Implement scope-parameterized query functions and role-projected responses; add negative tests per endpoint.
owner: Unassigned; proposed Engineering Lead

title: Authorization model: roles, attributes, entitlements and policy versioning
target_answer: Authorization combines role (what kind of actor), relationship (which funds, programs, partners), entitlement (what the customer contracted for), and context (policy version, effective dates, fund restrictions, jurisdiction, regulatory blocks) in one deterministic policy evaluated by the authorization core. Customers may compose custom roles only from permissions the platform marks delegable; reserved permissions cannot be included. Policies and entitlements are versioned, effective-dated, append-only records; each decision records the policy and entitlement versions used, so any past decision can be reproduced and explained.
intended_practice: Implement the AuthorityMatrix, entitlement records and decision logging.
owner: Unassigned; proposed Product Owner with Security Lead

title: Separation of duties enforced at transaction time
target_answer: Separation of duties is a constraint evaluated by the authorization core on every consequential command: the system refuses an approval by any principal who initiated, prepared, authored the governing policy, or has deployment or administration rights over the release gate for that transaction, and it applies across human, service and agent principals including through delegation chains. Until the sponsor's external auditor and board accept a deterministic release gate as the releaser, three distinct persons are required. Reconciliation is performed by a party outside the payment chain. Small sponsors without enough staff receive documented alternative controls with expiry and committee review, never a silent waiver.
intended_practice: Implement SoD constraints in the authority engine with delegation-chain awareness.
owner: Unassigned; proposed Governance owner

title: Delegated authority: scope, expiry, revocation propagation and emergency authority
target_answer: Delegations are first-class records naming grantor, grantee, scope (command classes, funds, limits), start, mandatory expiry and source authority; a grantor can delegate only a subset of what they hold. Ending a parent authority ends all derived delegations at the same effective time. Authority changes take effect at command execution: cached decisions, widget instances, partner tokens and agent grants derived from old authority are invalidated or rechecked on next use, within a stated maximum staleness. Changing who can approve requires dual control and cannot be self-approved. Emergency and substitute authority are pre-defined by the sponsor, time-bound and reviewed after use.
intended_practice: Implement delegation records and revocation propagation in the authorization core.
owner: Unassigned; proposed Security Lead

title: DAF role semantics: sponsor authority versus donor, advisor and partner permissions
target_answer: The permission model encodes DAF legal structure: donor and advisor relationships (original, additional, successor, authorized viewer, professional advisor) can only create recommendations within their fund scope; approval, payment instruction and execution are sponsor-reserved command classes that no donor, advisor, partner or agent role can hold. Professional advisors see only funds where they hold a relationship. Distribution-partner staff can service their own channel's donors within sponsor-authorized data and cannot approve grants or change sponsor policy. Sponsor staff access to donor personal data is limited by role need. Concurrent recommendations and conflicts follow sponsor policy. Agents acting for donors may draft recommendations under the donor's delegation but can never approve.
intended_practice: Encode relationship types and sponsor-reserved classes in the AuthorityMatrix; test with negative cases per role.
owner: Unassigned; proposed Product Owner

title: Authorization verification: negative tests, generated matrix and independent testing
target_answer: Every command class has generated negative tests (each role attempting each command it must not perform, each principal requesting objects outside its scope) and property-based tests over random principals and objects; these run on every change and block release on failure. The effective authorization matrix is generated from the build and published to customers under NDA, with a diff per release. Production authorization denials are monitored for anomalies. An independent penetration test with authorization and tenant-isolation focus is performed before production and at least annually, with results summarized for customers.
intended_practice: Build the negative test generator alongside the authorization core; commission an independent test before production.
owner: Unassigned; proposed Security Lead

title: AI agent authorization boundaries
target_answer: An agent's effective authority is the intersection of its own agent role (tier ceiling from the authority matrix) and the delegating principal's authority; it can never exceed either. Agents call the same governed command handlers as humans; the tool broker exposes only tools whose command classes are within that intersection, and the authorization core re-checks every call. Content an agent reads (charity documents, emails, web pages) is treated as untrusted data: it cannot add tools, raise tier or change targets, and consequential actions proposed after processing untrusted content require human confirmation of the exact action. Reserved (A4) and prohibited (A5) actions, including grant approval, live payments, disabling logs and changing authority, are unavailable to any agent configuration.
intended_practice: Implement agent role ceilings, intersection semantics and the tool broker.
owner: Unassigned; proposed AI Governance owner

title: Data-level authorization for exports, reporting, analytics and sensitive fields
target_answer: Exports, scheduled reports and analytics are produced only through query handlers that apply the requester's scope and field-level permissions, never through direct database or warehouse access by users. Bulk exports require step-up, are logged with row counts and recipients, and above sponsor-set thresholds require a second approver. Sensitive fields (tax identifiers, bank details, dates of birth) are released only to roles that need them and are masked elsewhere. Any analytics store receives only data classes permitted by the isolation map and enforces the same tenant scope.
intended_practice: Implement export through governed handlers with field-level policy and approvals.
owner: Unassigned; proposed Security Lead

title: Availability commitment and definition
target_answer: Echelon publishes capability-level service levels rather than a single uptime figure: separate monthly targets for read access to records and statements, for submission of requests, and for approval and payment dispatch, measured with a stated methodology. A deliberate fail-closed refusal of a financial action because safety cannot be confirmed is reported transparently as unavailability of that capability, not excluded. Exclusions are limited and enumerated; scheduled maintenance counts against the target unless within a pre-announced window under a defined monthly cap.
intended_practice: Publish SLOs only after measurement exists in a production-like environment.
owner: Proposed: Unbound product owner

title: Availability measurement and reporting
target_answer: Availability is measured by synthetic probes from at least two external vantage points per capability and by server-side success ratios per tenant, so partial outages affecting some tenants or features are counted. Monthly per-tenant reports are generated automatically, and customers can obtain the raw measurement data to recompute them or compare with their own monitoring. Historical availability is published once a production record exists.
intended_practice: Implement measurement before any SLA is offered.
owner: Proposed: SRE Lead (role not yet staffed)

title: Status page, outage notification and post-incident reports
target_answer: A component-level status page hosted independently of production shows current status and history; customers can subscribe by email and webhook. Customers are notified of a material outage within 30 minutes of detection, which is designed to satisfy the bank service provider obligation to notify affected banking organizations as soon as possible when covered services are materially disrupted for four or more hours. A root-cause report follows within ten business days of a qualifying incident.
intended_practice: Stand up an independent status page before the first customer.
owner: Proposed: SRE Lead (role not yet staffed)

title: Maintenance windows and change-related downtime
target_answer: Deployments are zero-downtime by default and schema changes are applied online through Strata-managed migrations with expand-and-contract patterns. Any planned downtime is announced at least five business days ahead, scheduled outside customer business hours, capped monthly, and prohibited during declared freeze periods such as the last two weeks of December. Emergency maintenance is announced as soon as it is decided, with reason.
intended_practice: Design the release pipeline for zero downtime from the start.
owner: Proposed: SRE Lead (role not yet staffed)

title: Service credits and remedies
target_answer: Service credits are calculated automatically from the measurement stream and applied without a claim process; repeated misses (for example three months in any six) give the customer a termination right without penalty and transition assistance. Credits are not the exclusive remedy for failures caused by breach of security or data-integrity obligations.
intended_practice: Draft SLA schedule with counsel when SLOs are measurable.
owner: Proposed: Finance Lead (role not yet staffed)

title: Subprocessor dependency and its effect on availability
target_answer: Each capability is mapped to the subprocessors it depends on (cloud hosting, managed PostgreSQL, identity, email delivery, payment connectivity, custodian feeds, charity registries, AI providers). Echelon's SLA does not exclude outages of its own chosen subprocessors; it does distinguish outages of parties the customer chose, such as the sponsor's bank or custodian. Provider status is shown on the status page and in the product.
intended_practice: Build the register at provider selection.
owner: Proposed: Vendor Risk Lead (role not yet staffed)

title: Degraded modes and fail-closed financial actions
target_answer: Every dependency outage maps to an explicit degraded state. Read access, drafting and non-financial work continue; money movement, payee changes and authority changes fail closed when the system cannot confirm safety (for example the hold registry is stale beyond its freshness bound or database quorum is lost), and the user sees a distinct, honest status such as 'Outcome being confirmed' rather than a false success or a generic error. Platform-originated holds are time-bounded, notify the sponsor's designated officer, never move funds, and leave the sponsor able to pay through its own bank.
intended_practice: Implement degraded states as typed domain states with automated tests per dependency.
owner: Proposed: Unbound architecture owner

title: Business continuity management program and policy
target_answer: Echelon operates a business continuity management program aligned with ISO 22301 concepts. A board-approved policy covers every customer-facing service and the functions that support it, names an accountable executive, is reviewed at least annually and on material change, and its summary and change log are available to customers under NDA. Continuity evidence (BIA, plans, exercises, remediation) is generated in a governed repository with provenance so that customers can verify freshness rather than rely on an annual attestation.
intended_practice: Adopt a continuity policy before the first customer contract; record approvals in Praxis-governed repositories; publish a customer-facing summary.
owner: Proposed: Business Continuity Owner (role not yet staffed)

title: Business impact analysis and criticality
target_answer: Every capability has a BIA entry stating customer consequence over time (for example missed grant deadlines, unreceipted year-end contributions, blocked payroll-like disbursements to charities), maximum tolerable disruption, minimum acceptable service, and dependencies including cloud, identity, payment rails, custodians, charity data sources and AI model providers. Recovery objectives are derived from the BIA, and Echelon provides each financial customer with the information needed to classify Unbound in its own BIA and critical-vendor inventory.
intended_practice: Perform a BIA as part of architecture acceptance; gate capability activation on a reviewed BIA entry.
owner: Proposed: Business Continuity Owner (role not yet staffed)

title: Continuity plans, alternate communications and crisis notification
target_answer: Scenario plans exist for loss of people, technology, facilities and providers. Each plan names decision authority, customer and regulator-facing communication steps and alternate channels that do not depend on the production platform, its email domain or its identity provider. Current copies are held out of band and checked automatically for drift. Customers receive a designated contact list and the channels Echelon will use if its primary domain is compromised.
intended_practice: Draft plans with the BIA; store a signed out-of-band copy; register alternate channels with each customer at onboarding.
owner: Proposed: Business Continuity Owner (role not yet staffed)

title: Continuity exercises and testing
target_answer: Plans are exercised at least annually with scenario variety, including correlated conjunctions (year-end surge plus payment-provider outage plus custodian delay), and customers may observe or participate in a joint exercise annually. Each exercise produces a dated report with measured timings, findings and remediation closure evidence; summaries are shared under NDA.
intended_practice: Run a first tabletop before production; add functional exercises once a production-like environment exists.
owner: Proposed: Business Continuity Owner (role not yet staffed)

title: Key-person and founder dependence
target_answer: No capability, credential or decision depends on a single individual. A key-person register lists each capability with a named alternate; emergency credentials are held under dual control or split custody; the codebase, requirements, decisions and operating procedures are in governed repositories with provenance so a qualified successor can operate and change the system; and portability is proven by exercises in which the primary does not participate. Contracts give customers a verifiable exit package and transition assistance if Echelon cannot continue.
intended_practice: Build the key-person register at formation; place emergency credentials under dual control; run a portability test before the first production customer.
owner: Proposed: Chief Executive (role holder not established)

title: Workforce disruption and pandemic readiness
target_answer: All operational roles can be performed remotely on managed devices with no dependency on a single office or data center under Echelon's control. The plan defines minimum staffing per function, absenteeism triggers and which non-essential work is suspended, and identifies the share of operational work performed by AI agents under human supervision, including what happens if supervising staff are unavailable.
intended_practice: Document remote-operation and staffing thresholds with the continuity plan.
owner: Proposed: Business Continuity Owner (role not yet staffed)

title: Dependence on AI providers for engineering, operations and runtime
target_answer: AI is never in the authoritative path for money movement, authority, holds or records: deterministic policy evaluates first and AI is advisory, so a model-provider outage degrades throughput and convenience but not correctness. Each AI-dependent function has a named fallback (alternate model, human queue, or deferral) tested quarterly with the provider disabled. Engineering can continue at reduced velocity without AI agents because the codebase is conventional F#/.NET under human review. Model versions are pinned and provider deprecations are tracked as change events.
intended_practice: Inventory AI dependencies; implement rules-first routing; test with providers disabled.
owner: Proposed: Unbound architecture owner

title: Alternate processing for grants and payments during platform outage
target_answer: The sponsor, not Unbound, originates payments, so the sponsor can always pay an urgent grant through its own bank channel. Unbound provides a documented alternate procedure, an offline read-only archive of fund balances and pending grants, and an OutOfBandPaymentRecorded command that, after recovery, cancels the matching queued instruction and registers the expected bank debit, so no duplicate payment is sent. Manual processing preserves the sponsor's dual approval and sanctions screening through a checklist, and replay of queued requests occurs only after reconciliation and revalidation.
intended_practice: Implement the OutOfBandPaymentRecorded command and offline archive before payment features launch; drill annually with each sponsor.
owner: Proposed: Unbound payments owner

title: Subprocessor continuity and Echelon viability
target_answer: Critical subprocessors (cloud, managed PostgreSQL, payment connectivity, identity, AI providers) are inventoried with assurance reports, bridge letters and reviewed continuity commitments. If Echelon cannot continue, customers can take a verifiable exit package at any time, contracts provide transition assistance and notice, and source code escrow is available where a customer requires it.
intended_practice: Build the vendor register at provider selection; implement exit package before production; evaluate escrow providers.
owner: Proposed: Vendor Risk Lead (role not yet staffed)

title: Backup scope, frequency, retention and location
target_answer: All authoritative stores are backed up at frequencies meeting their data-class RPO: continuous write-ahead-log archiving plus daily snapshots for the ledger database, versioned object storage for issued documents, and daily backups of configuration and source repositories. Rebuildable projections, search indexes and embeddings are excluded by design and rebuilt from the journal. Backups are retained at least 35 days for operational recovery, with longer retention for financial records governed by the retention policy, and copies are kept in a second location within the tenant's residency jurisdiction. Customers may also take their own complete, verifiable export at any time.
intended_practice: Configure backups with the first production-like environment; generate the inventory from configuration.
owner: Proposed: SRE Lead (role not yet staffed)

title: Backup protection: immutability, separation, encryption and access
target_answer: Backups are written to a vault in a separate cloud account with separate credentials and a compliance-mode retention lock, so no production administrator, compromised credential or AI agent can delete or alter them during retention. Backups are encrypted with keys outside production key scope, with an escrowed recovery path tested annually. Restores into production require two authorized people and are logged as tamper-evident evidence; agents cannot initiate them.
intended_practice: Adopt a separate backup account and retention lock from the first environment.
owner: Proposed: SRE Lead (role not yet staffed)

title: Restore testing and integrity verification
target_answer: Restores of each data class run at least quarterly into isolated environments and are verified by hash-chain or signed-checkpoint verification, record counts and per-fund trial balances, not only by job success. Missing or failed backups raise monitored control exceptions. Results are retained as evidence and summarized for customers under NDA.
intended_practice: Implement integrity verification with the ledger; schedule restore tests from the first pre-production environment.
owner: Proposed: SRE Lead (role not yet staffed)

title: Point-in-time recovery and deterministic replay
target_answer: The authoritative ledger is strictly append-only; corrections are new linked records, never updates. Point-in-time recovery is available to the second within the retention window through write-ahead-log archiving, and every balance and projection can be reconstructed by deterministic replay of the journal to any prior point. Replay is side-effect free: it cannot send payments, emails or provider calls. Replay equivalence against live projections is tested monthly.
intended_practice: Build the ledger as append-only with typed separation of replay from effect dispatch.
owner: Proposed: Unbound architecture owner

title: Backups, retention, legal hold and deletion
target_answer: Backups honor the retention policy, including the seven-year minimum for financial records and legal holds. When personal data is deleted or a tenant exits, Echelon states which backups still contain the data and when they expire (no more than 35 days after the exit package is delivered for operational backups), and the destruction certificate lists residual copies and records retained by legal obligation. Echelon does not claim cryptographic erasure where plaintext remains in backups, logs or exports.
intended_practice: Implement retention policy engine and backup expiry tracking before production.
owner: Proposed: Privacy Lead (role not yet staffed)

title: Change approval and authorization
target_answer: Production changes are deployed only through one pipeline from reviewed, approved commits; the pipeline generates a change record linking work item, commits, author and approvers, check results, artifact digest and deployment; sponsors receive a per-release notice of changed control-relevant modules; change records are retained as service-organization evidence.
intended_practice: Production changes are deployed only through one pipeline from reviewed, approved commits; the pipeline generates a change record linking work item, commits, author and approvers, check results, artifact digest and deployment; sponsors receive a per-release notice of changed control-relevant modules; change records are retained as service-organization evidence.
owner: Engineering Lead (proposed role, unassigned)

title: Segregation of duties in development and deployment
target_answer: The pipeline enforces that no identity, human or agent, can author, approve and deploy the same change; control-relevant modules need two approvers other than the author; repository and pipeline administrative changes are themselves reviewed and alerted; exceptions are recorded with approver and expiry. Where headcount is insufficient for independent human approval, Echelon will disclose this and use an external reviewer rather than claim segregation it does not have.
intended_practice: The pipeline enforces that no identity, human or agent, can author, approve and deploy the same change; control-relevant modules need two approvers other than the author; repository and pipeline administrative changes are themselves reviewed and alerted; exceptions are recorded with approver and expiry. Where headcount is insufficient for independent human approval, Echelon will disclose this and use an external reviewer rather than claim segregation it does not have.
owner: Engineering Lead (proposed role, unassigned)

title: Production access and break-glass
target_answer: No human or agent has standing access to production data. Read diagnostics are scoped, expiring and pre-approved by the sponsor; writes need per-case approval; production database administrative roles are break-glass only with two-person activation; every session is recorded and reviewed after use.
intended_practice: No human or agent has standing access to production data. Read diagnostics are scoped, expiring and pre-approved by the sponsor; writes need per-case approval; production database administrative roles are break-glass only with two-person activation; every session is recorded and reviewed after use.
owner: Security Lead (proposed role, unassigned)

title: Emergency change
target_answer: Emergency changes use the same pipeline, artifacts and provenance as normal changes; only the approval timing differs. An emergency is declared with a reason and a named approver, and a retrospective review is completed within two business days; emergency frequency is reported as a metric.
intended_practice: Emergency changes use the same pipeline, artifacts and provenance as normal changes; only the approval timing differs. An emergency is declared with a reason and a named approver, and a retrospective review is completed within two business days; emergency frequency is reported as a metric.
owner: Engineering Lead (proposed role, unassigned)

title: Deployment, rollback and database migration safety
target_answer: Application releases are immutable artifacts that can be rolled back; database changes are deployed only as Strata plans that are compiled, diffed and judged for breaking effects, with destructive steps blocked by default; schema changes follow expand-and-contract so application rollback remains possible; rollback and restore are tested before release; after any restore, money movement stays blocked until reconciliation (CNV-ARC-001).
intended_practice: Application releases are immutable artifacts that can be rolled back; database changes are deployed only as Strata plans that are compiled, diffed and judged for breaking effects, with destructive steps blocked by default; schema changes follow expand-and-contract so application rollback remains possible; rollback and restore are tested before release; after any restore, money movement stays blocked until reconciliation (CNV-ARC-001).
owner: Engineering Lead (proposed role, unassigned)

title: Change evidence and infrastructure as code
target_answer: Infrastructure and database schema are declared as code and deployed only from declarations, with daily drift detection. Change evidence is generated by construction: Praxis records the work item, actor (human or agent with model and runtime) and content digests; the pipeline adds approvals, artifact digests and deployment records; records are signed and retained under the service-organization evidence class. Echelon distinguishes self-reported actor identity from authenticated identity and binds the two through the source control platform's authenticated accounts.
intended_practice: Infrastructure and database schema are declared as code and deployed only from declarations, with daily drift detection. Change evidence is generated by construction: Praxis records the work item, actor (human or agent with model and runtime) and content digests; the pipeline adds approvals, artifact digests and deployment records; records are signed and retained under the service-organization evidence class. Echelon distinguishes self-reported actor identity from authenticated identity and binds the two through the source control platform's authenticated accounts.
owner: Engineering Lead (proposed role, unassigned)

title: Eligibility verification against IRS primary data
target_answer: Recipient status is established from first-party ingestion of IRS primary sources (Tax Exempt Organization Search and Pub 78 data, the EO Business Master File, automatic revocation lists, Form 990 series and 990-N data, and determination letters where available), each observation stored with source, posting date, retrieval time and checksum. Public charity status under section 170(b)(1)(A) is distinguished from private foundation status, grants are made to the listed legal name, group-exemption subordinates are flagged for additional verification, and absence from a dataset is never treated by itself as proof of ineligibility.
intended_practice: First-party connectors per UNB-CHAR-010 and UNB-EXT-001, provenance per UNB-CHAR-008, approval and release checks per CNV-GRT-003.
owner: Unbound product owner (proposed role; not yet assigned)

title: Status freshness, reverification cadence and event-triggered reevaluation
target_answer: Status is checked at approval and again at release against the latest published IRS data, with each source's posting date recorded and a retrieval target of 24 hours from publication (an operational target, not a legal threshold). Deep reviews expire by default after 180 days (sponsors may tighten) with refresh 30 days before expiry, and any primary-source change, policy change or grant purpose change triggers reevaluation of only the impacted decisions. When a source is unavailable or stale beyond policy, release holds rather than proceeding.
intended_practice: Freshness rules per CNV-GRT-003, reevaluation per UNB-CHAR-024 and UNB-GEX-019, release recheck per UNB-GRANT-009.
owner: Unbound product owner (proposed role; not yet assigned)

title: Revocation and reinstatement handling
target_answer: When IRS data shows an automatic or other revocation or removal from Pub 78 data, the platform re-verifies the fact from the primary source, places a legally mandatory hold on pending and recurring grants to that organization, routes in-flight payments for recall where possible, notifies affected donors with neutral wording, and records reinstatement (including retroactive reinstatement) as a new linked fact without erasing history.
intended_practice: Revocation holds per CNV-GRT-004 and UNB-CHAR-015; hold propagation per CNV-ARC-003; cancellation rules per TVR-GR-004.
owner: Unbound product owner (proposed role; not yet assigned)

title: Foreign grantees, equivalency determinations and intermediaries
target_answer: Direct foreign grants are architecturally supported but disabled in release 1. When enabled, the routine path requires a current EquivalencyDetermination record (practitioner identity and Circular 230 standing, advice date, grantee taxable year, currency under the applicable regulation) or sponsor-exercised expenditure responsibility. Recommendations naming a foreign organization without either are redirected to the sponsor's catalog of domestic intermediaries whose outbound wording may name a program, country or cause but never the foreign organization. Foreign-related grants add OFAC general licence versioning, risk-based anti-corruption diligence, staged payments and use reporting.
intended_practice: Foreign path per CNV-GRT-002, CNV-GRT-007, CNV-GRT-008, UNB-GRANT-041, UNB-XIN-NPG-001/002.
owner: Unbound product owner (proposed role; not yet assigned)

title: Fiscal sponsors, churches, government units, supporting organizations and non-filers
target_answer: A counsel-approved entity-type evidence matrix defines accepted evidence for churches and conventions not required to file, government units, group-exemption subordinates, disregarded entities of an eligible parent and newly recognized organizations not yet in bulk files. Fiscally sponsored projects record arrangement type, evidence source and the fiscal sponsor's own eligibility, with the fiscal sponsor as legal payee. Supporting organizations are classified by type, and Type I or II and grants to Type III supporting organizations route to enhanced review under §4966 rules. Charity identity, legal payee, fiscal sponsor and project remain separate entities.
intended_practice: Entity evidence matrix per UNB-RCN-GRT-013, fiscal sponsorship evidence per UNB-XIN-NPG-003, separation per UNB-RULE-011 and UNB-KNOW-007.
owner: Unbound product owner (proposed role; not yet assigned)

title: Sanctions screening of grantees, donors and payment parties
target_answer: A counsel-approved screening scope matrix covers recipient legal entity, fiscal sponsor and project, payee account holder, intermediary and beneficiary banks for cross-border payments, destination country, donors, advisors and successors. Parties are screened at onboarding, delta-screened automatically on list updates and screened before each grant release against the current list version. Confirmed matches resolve to Block, Reject or Proceed under a licence or exemption, never automatically, and produce OFAC report data within required timelines. Licence reliance is versioned and re-verified at release.
intended_practice: Screening per CNV-GRT-006/007 and UNB-RCN-GRT-007; restricted lists per UNB-CHAR-031.
owner: Unbound product owner (proposed role; not yet assigned)

title: Adverse media, discretionary holds and explainable risk signals
target_answer: Discretionary holds are permitted only under a board-approved policy listing criteria (adjudicated findings, regulator actions, official pending matters; media allegations only with elevated approval and a shorter maximum). Each hold records reason, evidence, owner and review deadline (maximum 90 days, renewable once on new evidence) and auto-releases, while legally mandatory holds never auto-release. Monitoring alerts carry materiality, confidence, freshness and ownership; no black-box AI risk score decides eligibility.
intended_practice: Discretionary hold policy per CNV-GRT-005; alerting per UNB-CHAR-033; AI limits per UNB-CHAR-022.
owner: Unbound product owner (proposed role; not yet assigned)

title: Shared charity registry: public facts versus sponsor-private investigations
target_answer: The common charity registry shares only non-sensitive canonical identity facts and holds derived from verified public facts (IRS revocation, Pub 78 removal, OFAC listing, published judgments), each re-verified by the platform from the primary source. Sponsor-private investigation content, suspicions and decisions never propagate to other sponsors; sponsor-originated corrections are re-verified before updating the registry, and release 1 does not offer any cross-sponsor 'enhanced review' flag. Investigation cases are restricted to the sponsor's investigation role. Charities have a correction and right-of-response process.
intended_practice: Sharing rules per CNV-GRT-004, UNB-CHAR-036/037; investigation isolation per UNB-XIN-CLM-004; correction per UNB-CHAR-014/017.
owner: Unbound product owner (proposed role; not yet assigned)

title: Charity identity resolution, impersonation and data quality
target_answer: Each organization has an immutable internal identifier independent of EIN, name and address, with legal names, aliases, historic names, EIN changes, mergers and successor relationships modeled explicitly. Duplicate candidates are detected deterministically and probabilistically but merged only with confirmation. Impersonation signals (similar names, mismatched EIN and bank details, suspicious address or bank changes, charity hijacking) open cases. Legacy sponsor records are imported as unverified claims, and charities can submit evidence through a controlled verification workflow.
intended_practice: Identity model per UNB-CHAR-001..006, impersonation per UNB-CHAR-028, migration per UNB-CHAR-041, charity workflows per UNB-CHAR-014.
owner: Unbound product owner (proposed role; not yet assigned)

title: Sponsor-specific eligibility decisions, overrides and reproducibility
target_answer: Eligibility is a time-bound, evidence-backed decision for a specific sponsor, program, purpose and date, with results Eligible, Ineligible, NeedsReview or InsufficientEvidence plus reasons and rule versions. Factual organization status, sponsor-specific eligibility and payment beneficiary verification are separate. Sponsor overrides are permitted only within lawful policy boundaries with reason, evidence and approver. Historical decisions are reproducible from pinned evidence, and state registration status such as the California Attorney General Registry is shown as a recipient attribute with sponsor-selected hold or warn behavior.
intended_practice: Decision model per UNB-CHAR-018..021, overrides per UNB-CHAR-023, reproducibility per UNB-CHAR-025, state registry per CNV-GRT-015.
owner: Unbound product owner (proposed role; not yet assigned)

title: Cloud provider selection and due diligence
target_answer: Echelon selects Unbound's cloud provider through a recorded decision that compares candidates on: current SOC 1 and SOC 2 Type 2 reports and ISO/IEC 27001, 27017 and 27018 certificates covering the specific services used; availability of FIPS 140-3 validated key management; US regions with at least two availability zones for managed PostgreSQL 16 (Strata constraint); private networking for managed services; workload identity; data residency controls; financial stability; and exit feasibility. The decision, the provider's reports and the gaps found are retained and refreshed annually.
intended_practice: Write the provider selection ADR with explicit criteria before any production resource is created.
owner: unassigned

title: Review of the cloud provider's assurance reports
target_answer: Each year, and on each new report or bridge letter, Echelon obtains the provider's SOC 1 Type 2 (where the provider's services affect sponsors' financial reporting) and SOC 2 Type 2 reports, confirms the services Unbound uses are in scope, reviews exceptions and qualified opinions, and maps every complementary user entity control in the provider's report to an Echelon control with evidence. Gaps between report periods are covered by bridge letters. The review record is available to customers under NDA together with instructions for obtaining the provider's reports directly.
intended_practice: Create the CUEC mapping template now; complete it when the provider is selected.
owner: unassigned

title: Shared responsibility model
target_answer: Echelon publishes a three-way responsibility matrix (cloud provider, Echelon, sponsor customer) for every control family: physical, network, host, platform, application, identity, data, keys, backups, incident response, and payment origination (the sponsor originates payments; Unbound is a third-party service provider per CNV-PAY-001). Each Echelon row links to an ECTL control and evidence requirement; each sponsor row is a complementary user entity control in Echelon's future SOC 2 report. The matrix is generated from the control register so it cannot drift from the controls actually implemented.
intended_practice: Draft the matrix structure in the control register; populate provider rows from the chosen provider's documentation.
owner: unassigned

title: Subservice organizations in the SOC 2 report: carve-out versus inclusive method
target_answer: Echelon's SOC 2 report will use the carve-out method for its cloud provider and other infrastructure subservice organizations, which is standard practice because hyperscale providers do not participate in customers' audits. The report will list each carved-out subservice organization, the services it provides, and the complementary subservice organization controls (CSOCs) Echelon relies on, and Echelon will monitor those organizations through their own reports (ANS-CLD-002). Inclusive treatment would only be considered for a smaller subservice organization that agrees to it and whose controls are central to a customer commitment.
intended_practice: Choose method with the auditor during readiness; document CSOCs from the provider's report.
owner: unassigned

title: Cloud configuration security posture and guardrails
target_answer: Insecure cloud configurations are prevented rather than found: organization-level policies deny creation of public storage, unencrypted storage, resources in unapproved regions, long-lived access keys and disabling of audit logging. A cloud security posture assessment runs continuously against a benchmark (CIS for the chosen provider) across all accounts; findings are routed with severity-based targets and suppressions require approved, expiring exceptions. Combined with IaC review (ECTL-INF-005) and drift reconciliation (ECTL-INF-006), this gives three layers: prevent, review, detect.
intended_practice: Write organization guardrails before first workload; enable provider-native posture assessment at account creation.
owner: unassigned

title: Region selection and data residency
target_answer: All Unbound customer data, including backups, replicas, logs, search indexes, AI embeddings and caches, is stored and processed in United States regions only, enforced by an organization policy that denies resource creation elsewhere. A data location inventory lists every store and its region, including subservice organizations (email delivery, AI model providers, support tooling) and where their processing occurs. Support access from outside the United States is not permitted without customer agreement. If a sponsor requires a narrower residency (for example a specific region), its deployment cell is placed accordingly (UNB-TEN-008). Disaster recovery uses a second US region.
intended_practice: Decide region pair with the provider; enforce region allowlist by policy; inventory subprocessors' processing locations.
owner: unassigned

title: Cloud account structure and root credential protection
target_answer: The cloud organization has separate accounts for production, non-production, security logging, shared build infrastructure and break-glass, with dedicated-infrastructure sponsors in their own production accounts (isolation profile C). Root or owner credentials for the organization and each account are protected with hardware-backed MFA, held under two-person control, never used for daily work, and every use alerts the security owner. Human access is federated from the workforce IdP with no local users; workloads use platform-issued identities with no long-lived access keys. Security logging is written to an account that production administrators cannot modify.
intended_practice: Create account structure as the first IaC module.
owner: unassigned

title: Cloud concentration risk and exit strategy
target_answer: Unbound accepts single-provider concentration deliberately and manages it rather than running multi-cloud. Mitigations: the application is one portable .NET deployable in a standard container; the authoritative store is PostgreSQL (portable engine), managed by Strata's declarative schemas; infrastructure is codified; backups are exported in a provider-neutral format to storage under separate credentials; and an exit runbook is tested annually by restoring a representative tenant into an alternate environment and verifying ledger integrity. Provider-specific services (KMS, identity) are isolated behind adapters. Echelon discloses the provider concentration to customers so they can assess their own aggregate exposure.
intended_practice: Write exit runbook with the hosting decision; schedule first restore-elsewhere test before general availability.
owner: unassigned

title: Managed services and other subservice organizations inventory
target_answer: Echelon maintains a register of every managed cloud service and external provider that stores, processes or can access customer data, generated from the provider adapter registry and IaC: service, provider, data classes, region, whether it is a subservice organization for SOC 2 purposes, its assurance report status, contractual terms, and the CSOCs relied upon. The register drives the customer-facing subprocessor list and SOC 2 system description, and adding a provider requires a security and privacy design review (SOC2-030).
intended_practice: Create the register schema in the control register; populate from provider adapters as they are designed.
owner: unassigned

title: Cash contribution intake by ACH, wire and check with provisional status
target_answer: Contributions arrive by ACH, wire, check or securities transfer into sponsor-titled accounts or through the sponsor's existing payment provider. Each cash contribution is matched to a gift intent and fund, unmatched deposits go to an exception queue (never auto-assigned), and reversible-rail contributions remain Provisional and not grantable beyond a sponsor risk limit until the applicable return window passes. ACH authorizations are retained for their active life plus two years, and bank feeds use BAI2, ISO 20022 camt messages or bank APIs.
intended_practice: Rails per CNV-PAY-005 and CNV-PAY-007; provisional status per TVR-CON-001; status transparency per UNB-DON-002.
owner: Unbound product owner (proposed role; not yet assigned)

title: The four contribution dates and gift completion rules
target_answer: Every contribution records GiftCompletionDate (tax rule by instrument and rail from a counsel-approved, versioned rule table), AcceptanceDate (accounting recognition), AvailabilityDate (sponsor risk rule, explicitly not finality) and AcknowledgmentDate. Year-end cutoffs use the gift completion date, and contributions missing evidence required by the rule table are held rather than dated by default.
intended_practice: Date model per CNV-FIN-003, gift date rule table per UNB-RCN-FIN-012.
owner: Unbound product owner (proposed role; not yet assigned)

title: Publicly traded securities contributions
target_answer: Securities gifts start from a gift intent (donor, fund, security identifier, quantity, delivering DTC participant, expected date). Custody receipts are matched deterministically; exactly one match auto-links and zero or multiple matches go to a queue, so orphan deposits are never assigned by guess. Multi-lot intents close as partial after the sponsor window, and acknowledgments cover only received lots. Settled liquidation proceeds are distinguished from unsettled proceeds, and valuations record timestamp, convention and price source.
intended_practice: Securities intake per UNB-XIN-PAY-007, UNB-WF-002, UNB-RCN-WF-003; custody per UNB-CUST-008/015.
owner: Unbound product owner (proposed role; not yet assigned)

title: Non-cash valuation, qualified appraisals and Forms 8283 and 8282
target_answer: Sponsor accounting valuations, donor-provided valuations, qualified appraisals and tax basis are kept separate. Gifts above the qualified appraisal threshold (including crypto above counsel-configured thresholds) are flagged as requiring a donor-obtained qualified appraisal. The platform tracks the sponsor's signature on Form 8283 Section B (donee acknowledgment), and monitors dispositions within three years of receipt to prepare Form 8282 data. The donee of record for intermediary-handled assets is determined by the counsel-approved agreement structure.
intended_practice: Valuation separation per UNB-GAP-012; appraisal flags per UNB-RCN-FIN-011; donee model per UNB-RCN-WF-005 and CNV-GRT-013.
owner: Unbound product owner (proposed role; not yet assigned)

title: Cryptocurrency and complex asset contributions
target_answer: Acceptance of crypto, privately held stock, real estate, partnership interests and other complex assets is a sponsor policy decision, not presumed. Complex gifts expected to credit a DAF use a counsel-approved agent model in which the sponsor is donee of record and any intermediary is its contracted agent. Each asset class has its own acceptance diligence (source of funds and wallet screening for crypto; environmental, debt, unrelated business income and excess business holdings review for real estate and business interests), custody and disposition states, and disclosed, reasonable service charges never paid to donors, advisors or related parties.
intended_practice: Crypto per UNB-WF-004, complex assets per UNB-GAP-011, intermediary model per CNV-GRT-013.
owner: Unbound product owner (proposed role; not yet assigned)

title: Contribution reversals, returns and chargebacks
target_answer: A returned ACH debit, dishonored check or card chargeback reverses the contribution as never completed and voids or amends the acknowledgment. If a reversed contribution already funded disbursements, the platform creates a donor receivable and sponsor exposure case and never allows a silent negative fund. Return and claim windows drive per-donor exposure limits across all unmatured reversible amounts. Card acceptance is architecturally supported but disabled in release 1.
intended_practice: Reversal model per CNV-FIN-003, TVR-CON-001 and TVR-CON-003; ACH return handling per CNV-PAY-005; cards per CNV-PAY-008.
owner: Unbound product owner (proposed role; not yet assigned)

title: Contribution acknowledgments and substantiation
target_answer: Acknowledgments are issued only through a gated command that validates a counsel-approved, versioned sponsor template containing every mandatory element, including the statement that the sponsoring organization has exclusive legal control over the contributed assets and whether any goods or services were provided. Issued acknowledgments are immutable artifacts with content hashes, timely relative to the donor's filing needs, amended through linked corrections, available in annual summaries, and retained per the sponsor's schedule.
intended_practice: Gated issuance per UNB-RCN-FIN-001, content per CNV-GRT-014, artifact registry per REQ-X-034, retention per CNV-PLT-004.
owner: Unbound product owner (proposed role; not yet assigned)

title: Donor-covered processing fees and fee disclosure
target_answer: For each processor-settled contribution the platform records gross amount charged (including donor-elected fee coverage), processor fee and net settled. When fee coverage is voluntary and the sponsor is merchant of record, the acknowledgment and fund credit use the gross amount and the processing fee posts as an expense; amounts paid to a non-charity (platform or mandatory convenience fees) are excluded from the acknowledgment and shown separately. Donor-facing quotes are shown for charged operations, and any amount above the donor's accepted maximum requires consent.
intended_practice: Fee treatment per CNV-PAY-006 and UNB-XIN-PAY-006; quotes per CNV-ECO-002; fee schedules per CNV-FIN-002.
owner: Unbound product owner (proposed role; not yet assigned)

title: Contribution acceptance, payor verification and screening
target_answer: Contributors and third-party payors are identity-verified and screened at onboarding, delta-screened on list updates and screened on contribution. The funding account owner is matched to the donor, and third-party payments require an explicit acceptance rule. Release 1 supports only the standard DAF account type, so contributions carrying binding donor restrictions are refused or routed for sponsor decision. Embedded and public contribution endpoints enforce velocity limits and step-up challenges against card testing, and the sponsor can refuse any gift.
intended_practice: Screening per CNV-GRT-006; funding account owner match per CNV-PLT-003; standard type per CNV-FIN-008; card testing defenses per UNB-XIN-PAY-004.
owner: Unbound product owner (proposed role; not yet assigned)

title: Custodian integration architecture, data integrity and freshness
target_answer: Unbound defines a custodian-neutral, versioned adapter contract covering account registration, positions, cash, transactions, prices, tax lots where available, corporate actions, fees, transfers and statements. Each integration declares a verified capability matrix (read-only feed, file import, manager-managed execution or API execution are separate profiles) and the system never infers trading or transfer permission from read access. Feeds arrive by polling, webhook, SFTP batch or secure statement with verifiable origin, freshness, deduplication, ordering and replay protection; every provider fact is appended with source, as-of time, received time, normalization version and hash, and corrections append superseding facts. Raw feeds are preserved. Provider credentials are scoped, rotated and stored as managed secrets. Core fund accounting and grant workflows do not require any particular custodian.
intended_practice: Unbound defines a custodian-neutral, versioned adapter contract covering account registration, positions, cash, transactions, prices, tax lots where available, corporate actions, fees, transfers and statements. Each integration declares a verified capability matrix (read-only feed, file import, manager-managed execution or API execution are separate profiles) and the system never infers trading or transfer permission from read access. Feeds arrive by polling, webhook, SFTP batch or secure statement with verifiable origin, freshness, deduplication, ordering and replay protection; every provider fact is appended with source, as-of time, received time, normalization version and hash, and corrections append superseding facts. Raw feeds are preserved. Provider credentials are scoped, rotated and stored as managed secrets. Core fund accounting and grant workflows do not require any particular custodian.
owner: Unassigned (proposed: Unbound integrations owner; sponsor Treasury for entitlements)

title: Asset segregation, legal title and Unbound's non-custodial role
target_answer: Unbound never holds custody of donor or fund assets and never receives or holds donor or grant money; there are no operator, FBO or pooled accounts, and donor payments settle directly into sponsor-owned accounts through regulated processors. Assets are titled to the sponsoring organization at custodians the sponsor contracts. Each custody account records legal ownership, account title, restrictions and purpose; a DAF may map to segregated custody accounts, and an omnibus account supporting many DAFs must declare one attribution method (per-fund lot subaccounting or unitized) before accepting multi-fund allocations, with lot-owned positions reconciled per security to the custodian. Partner and sponsor isolation holds even when one custodian serves several partners; a provider account identifier is never a security boundary on its own. Unbound does not imply that a donor-specific account is donor-owned.
intended_practice: Unbound never holds custody of donor or fund assets and never receives or holds donor or grant money; there are no operator, FBO or pooled accounts, and donor payments settle directly into sponsor-owned accounts through regulated processors. Assets are titled to the sponsoring organization at custodians the sponsor contracts. Each custody account records legal ownership, account title, restrictions and purpose; a DAF may map to segregated custody accounts, and an omnibus account supporting many DAFs must declare one attribution method (per-fund lot subaccounting or unitized) before accepting multi-fund allocations, with lot-owned positions reconciled per security to the custodian. Partner and sponsor isolation holds even when one custodian serves several partners; a provider account identifier is never a security boundary on its own. Unbound does not imply that a donor-specific account is donor-owned.
owner: Unassigned (proposed: Unbound product owner; sponsor legal for titling)

title: Custodian statements and statement of record
target_answer: Custodian statements and positions are the statement of record for assets held at the custodian; Unbound's fund statements are derived views that must reconcile to them. Contracts document the boundaries for custody, valuation reliance and statement of record. Custodian cash, positions, transactions, valuations and fees reconcile to the investment subledger, GL, bank evidence and available-to-recommend calculation. Corporate actions, income, splits and fees have deterministic posting rules and independent reconciliation. Where values come from the sponsor's external manager, a missing or stale manager price blocks the affected statement rather than being estimated. Folio renders custody reconciliation packs and fund statements with provenance references.
intended_practice: Custodian statements and positions are the statement of record for assets held at the custodian; Unbound's fund statements are derived views that must reconcile to them. Contracts document the boundaries for custody, valuation reliance and statement of record. Custodian cash, positions, transactions, valuations and fees reconcile to the investment subledger, GL, bank evidence and available-to-recommend calculation. owner: Unassigned (proposed: sponsor Controller)

title: Custodian oversight: SOC 1 reliance and complementary user entity controls
target_answer: Unbound maintains a critical-vendor register recording each custodian's assurance type, legal entity, report period, scope, opinion, exceptions, subservice organizations and complementary user entity controls (CUECs). Every CUEC is mapped to an internal control owner (sponsor or Unbound) before the custodian is marked Assured. A bridge letter is required when the period end is more than 3 months old and assurance is marked Expired after 12 months (provisional defaults; the sponsor's auditor confirms reliance criteria); a bridge letter is never recorded as extending independent assurance. An adverse opinion or expired risk acceptance changes vendor status. AI may extract report metadata only for human confirmation. Unbound will in turn publish to each sponsor the CUECs derived from that sponsor's configuration.
intended_practice: Unbound maintains a critical-vendor register recording each custodian's assurance type, legal entity, report period, scope, opinion, exceptions, subservice organizations and complementary user entity controls (CUECs). Every CUEC is mapped to an internal control owner (sponsor or Unbound) before the custodian is marked Assured. An adverse opinion or expired risk acceptance changes vendor status. AI may extract report metadata only for human confirmation. owner: Unassigned (proposed: sponsor vendor risk owner with Unbound support)

title: Trade and cash instructions to custodians
target_answer: Unbound does not execute: it never moves funds or releases an irreversible instruction using authority the sponsor has not delegated for that instruction. Where a custodian or manager contract permits, Unbound may relay sponsor-authorized instructions. Recommendations, orders, approvals, submission, acceptance, execution, partial fill, cancellation, rejection and settlement are distinct states. Cash transfers, liquidations, wires and securities transfers require independent authorization, payee or beneficiary verification, separation of duties, limits, idempotent instruction keys and provider settlement evidence. Grant payment instructions require Funded status or an approved, limit-checked liquidity advance. AI may propose but never originate or approve an instruction. In the Unbound test and simulation phase, live rail invocation is denied.
intended_practice: Unbound does not execute: it never moves funds or releases an irreversible instruction using authority the sponsor has not delegated for that instruction. Where a custodian or manager contract permits, Unbound may relay sponsor-authorized instructions.
