owner: Unassigned (proposed: sponsor Treasury)

title: Custodian outage, degraded modes and custodian transition
target_answer: Custodian outages, delayed feeds, revoked permissions, malformed files and account freezes trigger defined degraded modes: freshness warnings, scoped holds on affected reservations and statements, escalation, and no invented balances or unsafe transfers. The sponsor can freeze trading or allocation changes for custodian outage or valuation uncertainty. Valuations remain on hold or clearly provisional when source facts are unavailable. Custodian migrations preserve complete immutable history, account mappings, tax lots, open orders, restrictions and settlements, with overlapping read-only periods across managers. Because original feeds and append-only records are kept, fund-level holdings can be reconstructed independently of the custodian's systems.

The sponsor can freeze trading or allocation changes for custodian outage or valuation uncertainty. Valuations remain on hold or clearly provisional when source facts are unavailable. owner: Unassigned (proposed: Unbound operations owner with sponsor Treasury)

title: DAF account lifecycle, fund agreement versioning and point-in-time history
target_answer: Every DAF account is an explicit state machine (Requested, Active, Restricted, Frozen, ClosureRequested, ObligationsResolved, FinalFeesPosted, ResidualDisposed, Closed, Archived) whose transitions occur only through authorized, typed commands recorded as append-only events. The governing fund agreement and sponsor program terms are immutable versions bound to the account with effective dates, so the sponsor can reconstruct the account, its participants, balances and governing terms as of any past date. Closure cannot complete while reservations, unsettled contributions or in-flight payments remain.
intended_practice: Model the account lifecycle as an F# discriminated-union state machine persisted append-only (Strata-managed PostgreSQL schema), with bitemporal queries and a closure state machine per UNB-RCN-ENT-006.
owner: Unbound product owner (proposed role; not yet assigned)

title: Fund type classification for section 4966(d)(2) and accounting treatment
target_answer: Each fund carries exactly one fund type (donor-advised, designated, agency, field-of-interest, scholarship, other excepted fund) and one accounting treatment derived from the instrument's terms, not marketing labels. The fund type selects the rule set the engine applies, so DAF rules are applied to every fund that meets the statutory definition and excepted-fund rules only where the sponsor's counsel-approved classification supports the exception.
intended_practice: Implement an account-type register with counsel- and CPA-approved classification and AccountingTreatment per CNV-FIN-008 and UNB-XIN-ACC-001; release 1 supports only the standard DAF type.
owner: Unbound product owner (proposed role; not yet assigned)

title: Advisory privilege grant, scope, revocation and point-in-time proof
target_answer: Advisory privileges (grant recommendation, investment recommendation, view-only, successor designation, participant management) are separate, explicitly scoped, effective-dated grants recorded as append-only authority facts. Every command is reauthorized server-side against current authority at execution time, so revocation takes effect at the next authorization check and no later than 60 seconds across sessions, widgets, API tokens and agent principals. No principal can grant privileges it does not hold.
intended_practice: Central server-side authorization (SEC-AUTH-001) over typed authority facts; revocation propagation per UNB-RCN-WF-013 and AUTH-I1.
owner: Unbound product owner (proposed role; not yet assigned)

title: Multi-participant accounts, joint instructions and conflict handling
target_answer: A fund supports any number of participant relationships, each with its own role, scope and effective period. Instruction authority comes from the recorded fund agreement (any-one, all-must-approve, or configured quorum), never from inferred family status. Conflicting instructions from different principals with the same conflict scope are detected in the same transaction and both are held for resolution; closure, succession and authority changes require joint approval unless the agreement says otherwise. Adding a participant does not grant access to history unless the grantor's scope includes it.
intended_practice: Relationship model per UNB-PART-001..009 with conflict scope keys (UNB-XIN-EVA-012) and CNV-GRT-016 authority rules.
owner: Unbound product owner (proposed role; not yet assigned)

title: Successor advisors, charitable beneficiaries and succession activation
target_answer: Each fund has a versioned succession plan with zero or more ordered successors, contingent successors and charitable beneficiaries or spend-down instructions. On credible notice of death or incapacity the platform holds that person's new actions; on verification it suspends that person's rights, sessions and delegated agents in one transaction. Succession starts only when no living qualified advisor remains, may split the fund into separate successor accounts by percentage using balanced append-only entries, and handles disputes, nonresponse and contingent paths explicitly. Approved unpaid grants proceed unless sponsor policy says otherwise.
intended_practice: Succession graph and activation per UNB-SUCC-001..014, CNV-ENT-001, UNB-RCN-ENT-004 and REQ-X-008, with preview simulation (UNB-SUCC-013).
owner: Unbound product owner (proposed role; not yet assigned)

title: Sponsor policy configuration, approval, simulation and version pinning
target_answer: Every sponsor-configurable policy (minimums, fees, grant limits, payout, inactivity, eligibility, approval delegation) is a declarative, versioned, effective-dated record that only authorized sponsor decision makers can approve. Material changes require affirmative sponsor adoption, can be simulated against historical data before activation, and are pinned to every decision they influence. Platform changes cannot alter sponsor policy outcomes without the sponsor's adoption, and feature flags cannot vary legal or financial semantics by tenant.
intended_practice: Policy packs per CNV-GOV-005 and REQ-X-045, configuration register per UNB-SMP-CFG-003, replay per UNB-GEX-024.
owner: Unbound product owner (proposed role; not yet assigned)

title: Sponsor exclusive legal control, vendor authority limits and independence
target_answer: The architecture preserves the sponsor's exclusive legal control: charitable assets are titled to the sponsor or its custodian; external writes express requests, never approvals or money movement; reserved authority (grant approval, policy adoption, payment release) can be held only by persons appointed by sponsor board resolution, and vendor staff and AI agents are structurally excluded from it. Vendor operator access to sponsor data is denied by default and requires sponsor-approved, scoped, expiring delegation or per-case approval, all evidenced. No partner, embedding host or vendor account appears in the funds flow.
intended_practice: AuthorityMatrix (CNV-GOV-010), A3+ authority rules (CNV-GOV-004), FundsFlow declaration (UNB-XIN-REG-001), operator access delegation (UNB-XIN-IAM-002, CNV-ARC-002).
owner: Unbound product owner (proposed role; not yet assigned)

title: Inactive accounts, account minimums and small-balance handling
target_answer: Inactivity is a sponsor-configured, versioned policy: the platform detects inactivity by defined criteria, runs evidenced outreach through every verified channel, applies holds, and executes the sponsor's approved charitable default (for example a grant to the sponsor's unrestricted fund or named charities) only through an approved disposition workflow. Minimum opening balances, minimum balances, minimum grants and minimum fees are fee-schedule policy versions disclosed to donors, each tied to a cost basis, and below-minimum handling follows the sponsor's disclosed policy rather than silent fee depletion.
intended_practice: Dormancy workflow per ADM-024 and UNB-WF-015, closure via UNB-RCN-ENT-006, minimums via UNB-SMP-ECN-001 and CNV-ECO-002.
owner: Unbound product owner (proposed role; not yet assigned)

title: Section 4966, 4967 and 4958 compliance support
target_answer: Deterministic gates block, before approval and again before release, distributions that would be taxable distributions under §4966 (natural persons, non-charitable purposes without expenditure responsibility), prohibited benefits under §4967, and automatic excess benefit transactions under §4958 (grants, loans, compensation or similar payments to donors, donor-advisors, family members and 35 percent controlled entities). Disqualified-person relationships are maintained as effective-dated facts. Each policy version records its fund managers for §4966(a)(2) purposes. When a completed payment is later identified as a possible violation, an ExciseTaxIncident captures affected grants, parties and approvers and supports correction and Form 4720 data.
intended_practice: Gates per UNB-GRANT-011, CNV-GRT-009 and TVR-GR-006; incident handling per UNB-XIN-NPG-008 and CNV-GRT-010; fund manager register per CNV-GRT-001.
owner: Unbound product owner (proposed role; not yet assigned)

title: Exposure to the 2023 IRS proposed DAF regulations and rule-change agility
target_answer: Legal interpretations are versioned data in a machine-checkable regulatory applicability register that distinguishes binding, proposed and disputed obligations. For the November 2023 proposed DAF regulations, the sponsor records its election (for example whether to treat personal investment advisers as donor-advisors, or to rely on the proposed definition for public-charity-only funds), the engine applies the elected rule set, and the impact of the proposed or final rule can be simulated against existing funds before activation.
intended_practice: Regulatory register per UNB-REGMAP-001..004 with versioned legal assertions (UNB-LEG-001) and policy simulation (UNB-GEX-024).
owner: Unbound product owner (proposed role; not yet assigned)

title: Data classification scheme and schema-level assignment
target_answer: Unbound uses a four-level scheme (Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted) plus orthogonal tags for tenant scope and regulated categories (financial account, government identifier, donor anonymity, sanctions screening). Every column, event field, document type, log field, API field and AI prompt template is classified in its definition; the build fails on unclassified elements; derived data inherits the highest classification of its inputs unless a reviewed declassification rule applies.
intended_practice: Adopt the scheme in the first data model; implement classification as schema metadata with a build gate.
owner: Data governance owner (proposed role; not appointed)

title: Labeling and handling rules by classification, including AI agents and egress
target_answer: Each classification has a handling standard covering storage encryption, transmission, display masking, export, printing, email and retention. Folio-rendered documents and exports carry visible classification labels and embedded metadata. Restricted data cannot be sent by email or placed in tickets; outbound channels carry tokens or secure links instead. AI agent tools declare which classifications they may read and return, and the tool gateway refuses calls that would exceed them.
intended_practice: Write the handling standard; implement labels in Folio templates and classification-aware tool permissions.
owner: Data governance owner (proposed role; not appointed)

title: Restricted data: bank account numbers, SSNs and TINs, government identifiers
target_answer: Bank account and routing numbers, SSNs, TINs and government ID numbers are stored only in a tokenization vault with field-level encryption under separately managed keys; application records and events hold tokens. Displays show masked values by default; unmasking requires a declared purpose, role and step-up authentication and is logged. SSN or TIN is collected only where a documented need exists (for example identity proofing or tax reporting) and is never written to logs, events, exports or prompts. Nacha's unreadable-at-rest expectation is met regardless of volume threshold.
intended_practice: Design the tokenization vault together with the identity vault (UNB-DATA-007); define the collection-need register.
owner: Data governance owner (proposed role; not appointed)

title: Donor anonymity and disclosure preferences
target_answer: Each grant carries an effective disclosure preference (full name, fund name only, anonymous) set by the advisor within sponsor policy. Every outbound channel that mentions a donor (grant letters, check stubs, ACH remittance addenda, networked grant-platform payloads, charity portal views, acknowledgments) renders donor identity only through one disclosure function that applies the preference; the type system prevents raw donor names reaching outbound templates. Overrides require sponsor authority and are logged. Preferences survive migration and succession.
intended_practice: Model disclosure preference as a typed value that outbound templates must consume.
owner: Data governance owner (proposed role; not appointed)

title: Data minimization in collection, storage and onward disclosure
target_answer: Every collected field is justified in a collection-need register linked to the schema; fields without a recorded purpose fail the build. Onward disclosures to subprocessors (identity proofing, sanctions screening, payment) send only fields the integration contract declares. Minimization is reviewed annually against actual field usage telemetry, and unused fields are retired.
intended_practice: Create the collection-need register as part of schema metadata.
owner: Data governance owner (proposed role; not appointed)

title: Donor and advisor identity proofing
target_answer: Identity proofing is risk-based: core attributes are validated against authoritative sources, the funding account owner is matched, and a validated address or phone is confirmed; failure or elevated risk steps up to document and selfie or a non-biometric live-video alternative. Entities are verified by registration and signatory authority. Knowledge-based verification is never used for proofing. Accessible alternatives (mailed code, outbound call to a verified number, assisted captioned video, in-person or notarized verification) each reach a defined assurance level.
intended_practice: Proofing per CNV-PLT-003, accessible assurance per CNV-PLT-011, onboarding per UNB-PART-007, recovery per REQ-X-072.
owner: Unbound product owner (proposed role; not yet assigned)

title: Donor account takeover protection and recovery
target_answer: Donor accounts support phishing-resistant authenticators (passkeys or security keys) with device-bound options; a synced passkey alone is insufficient to add a new grant recipient. Any change to a verified contact channel notifies the previous channel with a self-service revert link and, for a sponsor-set period (default 72 hours), holds successor, beneficiary and authority changes and grant recommendations above a threshold for confirmation. Phone and support interactions reach only defined contact assurance levels, recovery requires identity-proofed paths, and suspected takeover cases are handled as restricted investigations.
intended_practice: Contact change hold per CNV-PLT-011, recipient novelty per TVR-SEC-010, assurance levels per CNV-PLT-003, cases per UNB-XIN-CLM-004.
owner: Unbound product owner (proposed role; not yet assigned)

title: Donor anonymity and privacy preferences across channels
target_answer: Anonymity, recognition and communication elections are authority facts owned by the identity and delegation capability, stored append-only with effective and recorded times. Every outbound use (grant letters, sponsor annual reports, partner views, statements) derives disclosure from the current election, and notifications re-read the election immediately before external send. Other participants on a fund see only what the grantor's scope allows.
intended_practice: Authority facts per UNB-XIN-EVA-014, send-time re-check per UNB-XIN-EVA-015, naming per ADM-013, privacy gap per UNB-GAP-021.
owner: Unbound product owner (proposed role; not yet assigned)

title: Professional advisor access delegation and firm changes
target_answer: Donors may delegate scoped, revocable, effective-dated access to professional advisors (view, investment recommendation, or grant preparation without submission). A professional-advisor relationship is scoped to the pair of individual advisor and firm; when the firm or a verified HR or SCIM feed reports the advisor's departure, or the advisor reports a new firm, the delegated access is suspended pending donor reconfirmation. Partner identity mapping uses a permanent identifier, never an email, and mapping changes require dual control and donor notice. Agents under a power of attorney act only with verified authority.
intended_practice: Delegation per UNB-ADV-001, advisor-firm pair per UNB-XIN-CRM-007, identity mapping per AUTH-I8, POA per CNV-ENT-001.
owner: Unbound product owner (proposed role; not yet assigned)

title: Donor communications classification, consent and accuracy
target_answer: Every message template is classified (commercial, transactional or relationship, mandatory legal, security) before activation, with a declared sender legal entity; promotional email in white-label programs is sent with the sponsor as sender, opt-outs are honored within 10 business days across all platforms sending for that sender, and texts or automated calls require prior express written consent naming the sponsor. Each notification records the fact and version it describes and is re-validated against the current fact and the recipient's consent state immediately before sending. Statements are generated for every configured period.
intended_practice: Classification per CNV-PLT-001, UNB-XIN-CRM-003, UNB-XIN-REG-003; send-time validation per UNB-XIN-EVA-015; statements per CNV-PLT-005 and REQ-X-032.
owner: Unbound product owner (proposed role; not yet assigned)

title: Donor data use limits, secondary use, AI training and privacy rights
target_answer: Donor data is processed only to provide services for the sponsor that controls it. The vendor does not sell donor data, does not use it for its own marketing, and does not use one sponsor's donor data to train models or benefit other sponsors except as the sponsor contractually authorizes. Cross-sponsor personal data exposure is prevented by tenant boundaries, and shared data requires separate rights and provenance. Privacy requests are fulfilled through reviewed procedures compatible with append-only records (for example cryptographic erasure or redaction of personal fields while preserving financial integrity) and legal retention.
intended_practice: Purpose limitation per UNB-API-005, UNB-CHAR-035/037 and UNB-TEN-007; privacy procedures per UNB-DATA-007 and UNB-GAP-021.
owner: Unbound product owner (proposed role; not yet assigned)

title: Deceased and incapacitated donor handling
target_answer: On credible notice of a donor's death the platform holds new actions by that person; on verification it suspends, in one transaction, all rights, sessions and delegated agent principals deriving from that person. Valid sponsor-approved unpaid grants continue unless sponsor policy says otherwise, future instructions are suspended until successor authority is verified, marketing to the deceased stops, and executors or estate representatives receive only the information the sponsor's policy permits.
intended_practice: Death handling per CNV-ENT-001, UNB-RCN-ENT-004, REQ-X-008, ADM-022 and UNB-WF-013.
owner: Unbound product owner (proposed role; not yet assigned)

title: Recovery time and recovery point objectives
target_answer: Recovery objectives are defined per data class and per capability in one versioned table referenced by each contract: acknowledged authoritative financial and security commits (ledger, reservations, approvals, holds, payee versions, authority, payment intents) have RPO zero and RTO of four hours or less; issued documents RPO zero and RTO 24 hours; operational records RPO 15 minutes and RTO 24 hours; rebuildable projections are rebuilt rather than restored. The fault assumptions under which RPO zero holds are stated explicitly, and a tenant may buy stricter RTO with a matching isolation profile.
intended_practice: Approve objectives before architecture acceptance and verify by restore test before production use.
owner: Proposed: SRE Lead (role not yet staffed)

title: Failover, regional resilience and split-brain prevention
target_answer: Unbound runs one component monolith on managed PostgreSQL with quorum-durable synchronous replication across availability zones and a fenced single writer. Authoritative financial writes are suspended, not redirected, when safe quorum is lost, so availability is traded for correctness. Regional loss is handled by restore or promotion in a secondary region that honors the tenant's residency, with an RTO stated separately for regional events. Failback requires replica catch-up and reconciliation. Cloud-provider exit is addressed by portability of data and infrastructure definitions, not by active multi-cloud.
intended_practice: Select provider and topology; implement fencing and quorum tests before payment features launch.
owner: Proposed: SRE Lead (role not yet staffed)

title: DR testing and evidence
target_answer: Every data class is restored at least annually per isolation profile, and failover is exercised at least annually, with measured RTO and RPO compared to objectives. A fault-injection suite runs on each release in a production-like environment. Evidence is generated automatically, time-stamped and digest-protected, and test evidence is labeled distinct from production evidence. Customers receive exercise summaries under NDA.
intended_practice: Run first restore and failover exercises in a pre-production environment before production launch.
owner: Proposed: SRE Lead (role not yet staffed)

title: Recovery dependency mapping and clean rebuild
target_answer: A generated dependency map shows what each capability needs to recover and in which order, including DNS, identity provider, key management, secrets, CI/CD and payment connectivity. The whole environment can be rebuilt from source, infrastructure definitions and Strata-managed schema into a clean account, which is the recovery path for destructive cyber events such as ransomware or cloud-account compromise. Encryption keys have documented recovery procedures so that key loss cannot make backups unreadable.
intended_practice: Adopt infrastructure as code from the first environment; test clean rebuild twice a year.
owner: Proposed: SRE Lead (role not yet staffed)

title: Tenant-level restoration
target_answer: A single tenant can be restored to a chosen point in time without affecting other tenants, using tooling bound to one verified tenant context and verified by negative isolation tests. The capability depends on isolation profile: dedicated databases restore independently; shared physical backups do not by themselves guarantee independent tenant recovery, and Echelon discloses that limit. Tenants on dedicated profiles may have separately configured and tested objectives.
intended_practice: Default to dedicated database per tenant (Profile B) and test tenant-selective restore annually.
owner: Proposed: SRE Lead (role not yet staffed)

title: Financial integrity and payment safety after recovery
target_answer: After any restore or failover, payment release stays blocked until consistency checks across all C0 stores pass and external bank and custodian outcomes are reconciled; payments with Unknown outcomes cannot be re-sent until resolved through the rail's protocol. Protective holds and cancellations are replayed before anything else, and independent authorization is required to lift the lock. If a recovery would lose an acknowledged financial fact, an approved procedure defines compensating records and customer notice.
intended_practice: Implement the release lock and reconciliation gate as part of the payments component; include in every restore exercise.
owner: Proposed: Unbound payments owner

title: Disaster declaration, communication and customer responsibilities
target_answer: Named roles may declare a disaster; customers are notified through pre-registered alternate channels within one hour of declaration, receive status at defined intervals, and receive a post-event report within ten business days stating achieved RTO and RPO against commitments. Complementary customer responsibilities (verifying balances, resubmitting rejected requests, confirming out-of-band payments) are documented in advance.
intended_practice: Define declaration authority and notification procedure with the continuity plan.
owner: Proposed: SRE Lead (role not yet staffed)

title: Encryption of customer data at rest in production stores and backups
target_answer: Every production data store that holds customer data, including managed PostgreSQL storage, replicas, snapshots, backups, object storage for statements and documents, search indexes, AI embeddings, caches, queues and logs, is encrypted at rest with AES-256 under keys held in the cloud key management service (ANS-ENC-004). Encryption is not optional: an organization guardrail denies creating unencrypted storage (ECTL-CLD-004) and a daily check attests that every store in the data location inventory is encrypted with an approved key. Community PostgreSQL has no built-in transparent data encryption, so storage-level encryption is provided by the managed service; the most sensitive fields additionally receive application-level encryption (ANS-ENC-008) so that database administrators and backups do not expose them in plaintext.
intended_practice: Enable provider storage encryption with customer-managed provider keys from day one; add guardrail and daily attestation.
owner: unassigned

title: Encryption in transit over public networks
target_answer: All external connections to Unbound (browser, partner API, webhooks, file delivery) use TLS 1.3, with TLS 1.2 permitted only with forward-secret AEAD cipher suites (ECDHE with AES-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305); TLS 1.0 and 1.1, SSL, RC4, 3DES, CBC-mode and static RSA key exchange are disabled. HSTS is set with a long max-age and includeSubDomains. Certificates are issued by approved CAs (CAA-restricted), use RSA 2048+ or ECDSA P-256+, are renewed automatically and monitored for expiry. Outbound connections to providers (payment, custodian, identity, email, AI model endpoints) require TLS 1.2+ with certificate validation; disabling validation is prohibited in code and detected by analysis. A weekly external scan verifies the configuration (ECTL-NET-009).
intended_practice: Encode TLS policy in edge configuration and an outbound HTTP client wrapper; add external scan.
owner: unassigned

title: Encryption in transit inside the hosting environment
target_answer: Every internal hop that carries customer data is encrypted and authenticated: edge to application (re-encrypted TLS), application to PostgreSQL (TLS with full certificate and hostname verification, for example Npgsql SSL Mode VerifyFull with the provider's CA pinned in configuration), application to key service, object storage and other managed services (TLS via provider SDKs or private endpoints). Connection settings are produced by a typed configuration module so a non-verifying mode cannot be configured without a failing build check. Database server settings reject non-TLS connections.
intended_practice: Build the typed connection configuration in the persistence layer (ADR-003 in the persistence design).
owner: unassigned

title: Key management lifecycle and custody
target_answer: Keys are held in the cloud provider's key management service backed by FIPS 140-3 validated hardware security modules; key-encryption keys never leave the HSM boundary. Unbound uses envelope encryption: per-tenant key-encryption keys in KMS wrap data-encryption keys generated per tenant and per data class. Key policies separate duties: the application identity can encrypt and decrypt with its tenant keys but cannot change policies or schedule deletion; key administrators cannot use keys to decrypt data; deletion requires two-person approval and a waiting period. Every key use and administrative action is logged to the security log account. Keys rotate automatically at least annually (data keys more often), and a compromise procedure re-wraps or re-encrypts affected data. The key inventory, owners and policies are maintained as code.
intended_practice: Resolve ADR-006 with the hosting decision; codify key hierarchy and policies.
owner: unassigned

title: FIPS 140-3 validated cryptographic modules
target_answer: Data at rest is encrypted by cloud services whose key management uses FIPS 140-3 (or still-valid FIPS 140-2) validated HSMs, with certificate numbers recorded. In the application, cryptography goes through .NET APIs backed by the platform library; the container base image uses an OS distribution whose OpenSSL provider has a FIPS 140-3 validation, and Echelon records which certificate covers the deployed version and whether the module runs in its validated (FIPS) mode. Echelon states precisely which operations use validated modules and does not claim 'FIPS compliant' for the whole service. Where a customer contractually requires FIPS mode end to end, it is offered for a dedicated cell after testing that all dependencies operate correctly in that mode.
intended_practice: Choose base image and provider services with validated modules; maintain a certificate register.
owner: unassigned

title: Customer-managed keys and per-tenant key isolation
target_answer: Every sponsor tenant has its own key-encryption key, so keys and therefore cryptographic access are isolated per tenant even in shared databases. For sponsors who contract for it, the tenant key can be a customer-managed key in the sponsor's own cloud KMS account, granted to Unbound for encrypt and decrypt only; the sponsor can audit every use and revoke the grant, which renders its data unreadable to Unbound (with documented consequences for service, legal holds and records retention). Echelon does not offer hold-your-own-key arrangements where keys are outside any cloud KMS, because Unbound's authoritative ledger must remain available for payments and regulatory records.
intended_practice: Design per-tenant key hierarchy in ADR-006; offer customer-managed keys only after operational procedures and revocation consequences are tested.
owner: unassigned

title: Secrets management and prevention of hardcoded secrets
target_answer: Unbound holds no long-lived secrets where platform identity can replace them: workloads authenticate to the database, KMS and cloud services with platform-issued short-lived credentials. Remaining secrets (third-party API keys, webhook signing secrets, provider credentials) live in a managed secret store, are retrieved at runtime by the workload identity that needs them, are never written to source, configuration files, container images, IaC state, logs or AI agent context, and rotate on a defined schedule and on personnel change or suspected exposure. Secret scanning runs on every commit and on history, blocking merges; a found secret is treated as compromised and rotated, not just removed. Logging redacts secret-typed values by construction because secrets are wrapped in a type whose string rendering is masked.
intended_practice: Adopt secret store with hosting decision; enable secret scanning in Praxis CI workflow now for existing repositories.

title: Field-level encryption of donor PII and bank account numbers
target_answer: Restricted fields, including bank account and routing numbers, tax identifiers, dates of birth and government ID data, are encrypted at the application layer before reaching PostgreSQL, using AES-256-GCM with per-tenant data keys from KMS (ANS-ENC-004) and the record identifier bound as associated data so ciphertext cannot be moved between records. In F#, these fields are distinct types (for example an EncryptedBankAccountNumber) with private constructors, so a plaintext value cannot be stored, logged or serialized by mistake; plaintext exists only inside the narrow payment-preparation and verification paths that need it. Display uses masked values (last four digits). Equality search uses a keyed HMAC index, never the plaintext. Donor PII sits in a segregated identity store so the append-only event history refers to it by token rather than embedding it (UNB-DATA-007), which enables lawful erasure by key destruction (ANS-ENC-011). This also satisfies the Nacha requirement that account numbers used for ACH be rendered unreadable when stored electronically, to the extent that requirement applies to Unbound as a third-party service provider.
intended_practice: Build the typed encrypted-field module and identity vault as part of ADR-006 before any real bank data is accepted.
owner: unassigned

title: Approved cryptography only: no custom cryptography and restricted .NET cryptographic APIs
target_answer: Echelon code uses no custom cryptographic algorithms, protocols or constructions (SEC-CRYPTO-001). All cryptographic operations go through one small, reviewed F# module that exposes only purpose-level functions (encrypt field, sign evidence, hash for integrity, derive password verifier) built on .NET's System.Security.Cryptography types backed by the platform library: AES-GCM for authenticated encryption, SHA-256/384/512 for hashing, HMAC-SHA-256, ECDSA P-256/P-384 or RSA-PSS for signatures, RandomNumberGenerator for all randomness, and PBKDF2 with high iteration counts only where a password-based key is unavoidable (user passwords are handled by the identity provider). Direct use of System.Security.Cryptography elsewhere, of obsolete types (MD5, SHA-1 for security purposes, DES, TripleDES, RC2, ECB or CBC without authentication, System.Random for security values) and of certificate-validation overrides is blocked by an analyzer gate. Because Roslyn analyzers do not analyze F# code, the gate requires an F# analyzer (FSharp.Analyzers.SDK) or a compiled-assembly check; this is a known tooling gap. Cryptographic code changes require review by a second engineer with cryptography competence.
intended_practice: Write the crypto module and banned-API check before any cryptographic feature is built.
owner: unassigned

title: Cryptographic agility and post-quantum readiness
target_answer: Echelon maintains a cryptographic bill of materials generated from code and configuration for every release: algorithms, key sizes, protocols, libraries and where each is used. Because primitives are reached only through the purpose-level crypto module (ANS-ENC-009) and keys are versioned in KMS, an algorithm can be replaced by changing the module and re-wrapping or re-encrypting data under a new key version without touching business logic. Ciphertexts and signatures carry algorithm and key version identifiers. Echelon tracks NIST's post-quantum standards and the deprecation timeline for quantum-vulnerable public-key algorithms, enables hybrid post-quantum key exchange in TLS when the edge provider and .NET platform support it, prioritizing external connections that carry long-lived sensitive data, and plans migration of signing keys (evidence, statements, builds) to post-quantum signature schemes as KMS support becomes available. Symmetric encryption at AES-256 is considered adequate against known quantum attacks.
intended_practice: Generate a CBOM from the first build; record a PQC migration plan.

title: Cryptographic erasure and key destruction
target_answer: Where personal data must be erased but the authoritative event history is append-only, the data is held encrypted under a per-subject or per-tenant key in the identity vault, and erasure is performed by destroying that key in KMS after legal retention and holds are checked. Echelon only claims an erasure is complete when it has verified that no plaintext copy exists in backups, logs, exports, search indexes, AI embeddings or caches within their retention windows, consistent with UNB-IMM-008; otherwise it states the date by which remaining copies expire. Key destruction is two-person approved, logged and evidenced. At sponsor exit, the sponsor's tenant keys are destroyed after the exit package is delivered and retention obligations are confirmed, rendering residual ciphertext unreadable.
intended_practice: Design the identity vault and key-per-subject granularity in ADR-006; involve counsel on retention conflicts (UNB-DATA-007).

title: Signing keys for builds, evidence, statements and ledger integrity anchors
target_answer: Separate signing keys, each held non-exportably in KMS/HSM, sign: release artifacts and provenance (CNV-PLT-010); control evidence bundles; issued statement manifests (REQ-X-033); outbound webhook deliveries (UNB-XIN-SAS-004); and daily ledger digest anchors published externally (CNV-PLT-010). Each key has one purpose, a named owner, rotation schedule and published public key with validity periods so customers and auditors can verify signatures independently. title: Workforce device management and inventory
target_answer: Every device that accesses Echelon systems is enrolled in device management before it can authenticate: the workforce identity provider grants access only to compliant, enrolled devices (conditional access). Management enforces OS updates within defined windows, screen lock, firewall, full disk encryption, EDR presence and remote wipe. The device inventory is produced by the management system and reconciled to the personnel roster daily so that offboarded users' devices are wiped or returned. Access to customer data from devices is minimized by design (ANS-END-004).

title: Endpoint detection and response and malware protection
target_answer: All managed workforce devices run an EDR agent reporting to a monitored console, with tamper protection; alerts are triaged by a named function or managed detection provider within defined times. title: Device disk encryption, lock and lost device response
target_answer: Full disk encryption using the operating system's built-in encryption is enforced by device management on every managed laptop and desktop, with recovery keys escrowed to the management system and not to the user. Screen lock after a short idle period, firmware passwords or secure boot where supported, and remote lock and wipe are enforced. Lost or stolen devices are reported within one business day, wiped remotely and evaluated as a potential security incident; because devices do not hold customer data by design, loss is normally not a reportable data breach, and the encryption status record supports that determination.

title: Personal devices, contractor devices and data on endpoints
target_answer: Personal and contractor-owned devices may access only low-sensitivity collaboration tools through a managed browser profile or application protection policy that blocks download, copy and local storage of Echelon data. title: Developer workstation and AI coding agent sandbox security
target_answer: Software is developed in ephemeral, cloud-hosted workspaces rather than on laptops where possible. Agent-written changes pass the same review and release gates as human changes, and control-relevant modules require two human approvers (CNV-PLT-010). Secrets never enter agent context; secret scanning runs on every commit (ECTL-ENC-008). Package installs in sandboxes resolve only through the approved dependency policy (SEC-SUPPLY-001).

title: Engine-enforced segregation of duties across financial processes
target_answer: Segregation of duties is enforced by the Unbound command engine, not by procedure. For posting-rule version approval, manual journals, bank and payee master changes, reconciliation sign-off, close certification and payment release, the approver must be a different principal from the preparer, and the check runs inside the command transaction (RR-UNB-ACC-022-r2, CNV-GOV-003). The rule applies to humans, service accounts and AI agents alike, so one actor cannot control request, approval and reconciliation (GOV-AUTH-004); AI can never approve its own accounting actions. Until a deterministic release gate is accepted by the sponsor's auditor and board, payment release requires three distinct people. Reconciliation sits outside the payment chain. Every conflict evaluation emits a DutyConflictEvaluated event (UNB-SCTRL-002) so an auditor can test the full population rather than a sample.
intended_practice: Implement the SoD conflict matrix as a server-side policy evaluated in every consequential command; publish the matrix per sponsor; negative tests prove self-approval is denied.

title: Approval limits and delegation of authority with aggregation
target_answer: Every approval is checked against a versioned delegation-of-authority (DoA) register. Each entry declares the decision type, per-item limit, cumulative limit, aggregation window and key (approver by counterparty), the board or officer resolution that grants it and an expiry (UNB-XIN-ERP-005). An approval above the per-item limit, or one that would push the approver's cumulative approvals to the same counterparty over the window limit, is rejected and escalated, which defeats invoice or grant splitting. Entries become invalid at the next check when the holder is inactive in the workforce feed or the source resolution is superseded. Grant approvals route by role, amount, risk, relationship and exception, with dual control where policy requires (RR-UNB-GRANT-012-r1).
intended_practice: Build the DoA register and limit evaluator as a deterministic policy component; feed it from the sponsor's board resolutions and the workforce identity feed.

title: Change control over fee schedules, rates and fee computation
target_answer: Fees can only be charged under an approved, versioned fee schedule. Each version declares its basis, day count, accrual and settlement cadence, minimum and exactly one payer source; a schedule with a missing or ambiguous payer source cannot activate (CNV-FIN-002, UNB-XIN-ERP-002). Schedule publication is a high-risk policy change that requires dual control (UNB-RULE-020) and is effective-dated rather than edited in place, so fee computation segments at each version boundary (UNB-XIN-ERP-001). Fee runs are idempotent per fund, schedule, period and segment set and move through Accrued, Assessed and Posted; waivers are approved exceptions with expiry and corrections are compensating entries (RR-ADM-028-r1). Only the fee engine may emit authoritative fee events (UNB-XIN-ERP-007). Operator charges to a sponsor are billed from the operator's own system and never posted into a tenant ledger (UNB-XIN-ERP-003).
intended_practice: Implement fee schedules as immutable versions with an activation gate, independent recomputation and a monthly fee reconciliation.

title: SOC 1 relevance and plan for customers' financial statement audits

intended_practice: Begin SOC 1 Type 2 readiness, including the first observation period, before the first staffed-administration client goes live (CNV-GOV-001); engage a CPA firm to confirm scope.

title: Internal control framework, control register and control state honesty
target_answer: Unbound's financial controls are organized around a COSO-aligned control register in which every control has a unique ID, owner, objective, risk, trigger, evidence schema, source system, reviewer and failure behavior (SOC2-001, TVR-CMP-001). The register separates Proposed, Designed, Implemented, Operating, Tested, Deficient, Remediating and AuditorReviewed and never infers one state from another (SOC2-019). Today all 90 UNB-CTRL controls in the master matrix are Designed only, with no operating evidence, test execution or auditor review. Every material capability has exactly one accountable human role even when execution is automated (UNB-CTL-003).
intended_practice: Operate the register as data that generates customer answers, so a status can only advance with attached evidence.

title: Management review controls and reliability of information used in review
target_answer: Management review controls in Unbound operate on reports whose completeness and accuracy can be proven. Every financial report, statement and dashboard figure is computed from a sealed financial snapshot identified by sponsor entity, period or as-of instant and ledger commit watermark, so recomputation yields identical figures (UNB-XIN-EVA-003). Generated reports carry information-produced-by-entity support: query definition, parameters, population counts, hash and run log (CNV-GOV-001). Manual review is replaced by generated evidence only after the auditor confirms reliance.

title: Automation, AI and deterministic rules within financial controls
target_answer: Unbound classifies every decision as deterministic (D), probabilistic recommendation or flag (P) or human-authorized (H); a probabilistic output alone can never clear a control or move money (UNB-CTL-001). AI may propose journal drafts and classifications but cannot bypass posting, approval or reconciliation controls (UNB-ACC-029); state-changing events with financial consequences come only from approved deterministic rules or authorized people (UNB-EVT-005); model-only auto-clear designs are prohibited (UNB-CTL-005). A deterministic release gate counts as an approver only when it runs a published, independently approved policy version, the human approvers cannot author or deploy it, ITGCs are effective and the auditor and board have accepted the design (CNV-GOV-003). Changes to control-relevant modules need two approvers, neither the author, and signed builds (CNV-PLT-010).
intended_practice: Encode D/P/H classification in the command catalog; agent principals can write only to an AI observation store (UNB-XIN-EVA-016).

title: Exceptions, overrides, emergency access and compensating controls

Where a sponsor lacks staff for full SoD, enforced leave applies when two trained staff exist and anomaly analytics otherwise; each alternative control is documented with expiry (CNV-GOV-003, TVR-SEC-006). Any authoritative state change without a matching command event blocks affected payments until reviewed.

title: Fee schedule definition, versioning and cost basis
target_answer: Every fee schedule is an approved, effective-dated version that declares its FeeBase contract: measurement basis (end-of-day market value by default; average daily, period-end or quarter-average options), inclusions and exclusions, valuation version, tier method, day count, accrual and settlement cadence, minimums, waivers, payer source, recipient type, service identity and treatment of reserved-but-uncommunicated grants. title: Grant priority over fees and fee shortfall handling
target_answer: Recognized grants payable and, by default, reserved grants rank ahead of fees. title: Account takeover resistance for donor, advisor, charity and sponsor accounts
target_answer: Platform and sponsor privileged roles use AAL3-grade authenticators (hardware keys or device-bound non-exportable keys, two per user, no synced passkeys) with identity-proofed recovery; other workforce uses AAL2 phishing-resistant authenticators; knowledge-based verification is never used for proofing (CNV-PLT-003). A StepUpPolicy matrix maps high-risk actions (authenticator or recovery change, authority or delegation change, payee or destination change, data export, large grant recommendations, API credential creation) to required assurance and a maximum authentication age of five minutes by default, and the step-up event is bound to the command (UNB-XIN-IAM-003). Authority-relevant credential changes need step-up, a cooling-off period and notice to the prior channel, and grants to recipients added during cooling-off need sponsor-direct confirmation (AUTH-I7). Auto-approval ceilings depend on session assurance, aggregate thresholds defeat splitting, and a new recipient from a phishable or agent session needs step-up (TVR-SEC-004); recipient novelty is measured from the last confirmation through a pre-existing channel, so waiting out a window does not make a recipient known (TVR-SEC-010).
intended_practice: Implement the StepUpPolicy matrix and cooling-off rules in the authorization component; red-team phishable-session grant attempts before launch.

title: Payee and bank account change fraud controls
target_answer: Destination evidence must exist before the first electronic payment to a charity and after every bank-detail change. The accepted combinations are exactly: (a) a bank-originated account-owner match plus a cooling-off period plus notice on both the old and new verified channels, or (b) a charity document plus a callback to a contact sourced from the charity registry or a prior verified record (never from the change request) plus cooling-off plus notice; a charity-signed letter alone never suffices (CNV-PAY-002). The cooling-off default is three business days and cannot be shortened below one (UNB-RCN-WF-028). A callback contact must have been verified at least 30 days before the request by default, and any contact or signatory change inside that window disqualifies it. Charity users who submit bank changes must authenticate at CAL3. Treasury publishes a versioned DestinationEvidence table per rail and rails that cannot meet it are ineligible for automated release (UNB-RCN-GRT-017). For tokenized destinations, a per-payment fingerprint is compared with sponsor-held verified data and provider self-attestation alone is insufficient (TVR-PAY-005, REQ-X-005).
intended_practice: Implement destination evidence records and the release gate; integrate an account-owner validation service where available.
owner: Not assigned; proposed: Unbound fraud and payments risk owner (role not staffed) with each sponsor's fraud operations owner

title: Business email compromise and social engineering of payment staff
target_answer: Unbound removes the channel that business email compromise exploits: payment instructions, approvals and destination changes can only be created through authenticated platform commands, never from an email, phone call or uploaded letter, and ingestion of external files or messages never grants sponsor approval (UNB-EVT-003, UNB-CTL-002). No payment may originate outside the platform payment gate; manual fallback also runs through the gate with dual control and bank portal entitlements are limited so no one can release unilaterally outside it (TVR-PAY-004). Callback contacts are never sourced from the request (CNV-PAY-002). Grant-specific threats such as payment detail substitution, fake charity identity, insider override and social engineering are explicitly modeled (UNB-GRANT-044). Staff training is a supporting control, not the primary one.
intended_practice: Provide no API, import or UI path that creates a payee change or payment from unstructured inbound content; review bank portal entitlements quarterly.
owner: Not assigned; proposed: Unbound fraud and payments risk owner (role not staffed) with each sponsor's fraud operations owner

title: Check fraud controls and positive pay
target_answer: Every check account uses positive pay with daily issue files that include voids (CNV-PAY-002). A check cannot move from Printed to Released-for-mail until the bank acknowledges an issue file with its number, amount, issue date and, where supported, payee name (payee positive pay). Positive-pay exception decisions default to Return; a Pay decision needs an authorized human who did not issue the check and recorded evidence. Voids are transmitted and acknowledged before any reissue (UNB-XIN-BNK-006, UNB-RCN-GRT-005). Disbursement accounts carry debit blocks that allow only named bank-fee company IDs, and unmatched debits trigger incidents and holds (UNB-XIN-BNK-003). Positive pay is a sponsor bank service; Unbound produces and transmits the issue data and records acknowledgments.
intended_practice: Implement the check state machine and issue-file generation per the sponsor bank's positive pay format.
owner: Not assigned; proposed: Unbound fraud and payments risk owner (role not staffed) with each sponsor's fraud operations owner

title: Insider fraud and collusion resistance
target_answer: Insider fraud is addressed structurally first: SoD is engine-enforced, AI cannot approve, payment release needs three distinct people until an accepted deterministic gate exists, and reconciliation sits outside the payment chain (CNV-GOV-003). Every business day each linked sponsor account's debits must match exactly one authorized instruction or an expected-debit class; an unmatched debit opens a high-severity incident within an hour, notifies two independent sponsor roles and holds further releases (UNB-XIN-BNK-003). The standing-data rule extends to external registers: daily custody movement match, identity-provider admin action match and bank portal entitlement review (TVR-SEC-008). Collusion-resistant analytics and enforced leave or rotation apply to payment and reconciliation roles (TVR-SEC-006). Grants whose recipient matches a sponsor operating vendor or a vendor of a party with privileges on the fund route to related-party review (UNB-XIN-ERP-004). Echelon engineers and agents cannot change control-relevant modules without two approvers who are not the author, and production database administration is break-glass only (CNV-PLT-010, UNB-XIN-IAM-005).
intended_practice: Implement daily unmatched-debit control and cross-role analytics; operate quarterly access recertification including bank portal users.
owner: Not assigned; proposed: Unbound fraud and payments risk owner (role not staffed) with each sponsor's fraud operations owner

title: Synthetic identities, contribution fraud and reversible funding
target_answer: Donor and advisor identity proofing is risk-based: core attributes are validated against authoritative sources, the funding account owner is matched and an address or phone is validated, stepping up to document and selfie or a non-biometric live-video alternative when validation fails or risk is elevated; entities are verified by registration and signatory authority (CNV-PLT-003). Sanctions screening, identity proofing, any customer due diligence and contact assurance are recorded as separate obligations (RR-UNB-PART-007-r1). Contributions on reversible rails remain Provisional until the rail's return window passes, per a versioned ReversalWindow table, and per-donor exposure caps weight un-matured reversible amounts (CNV-FIN-003, RR-TVR-CON-001-r1), so a synthetic donor cannot fund grants with money that is later returned. A reversed contribution reduces capacity immediately and opens an exposure case (RR-REQ-X-009-r1). Card contribution endpoints enforce velocity limits, minimum amounts and automatic channel suspension (UNB-XIN-PAY-004).
intended_practice: Integrate an identity verification provider behind a provider-neutral interface; implement provisional availability and exposure caps.
owner: Not assigned; proposed: Unbound fraud and payments risk owner (role not staffed) with each sponsor's fraud operations owner

title: Grant diversion, fake charities and prohibited benefits
target_answer: Unbound detects impersonation, suspicious address or bank changes, duplicate entities, charity hijacking, mismatched EIN and name and anomalous grant patterns, presented as evidence-based signals rather than automatic findings of guilt (UNB-CHAR-028, UNB-GEX-033). Identity confidence, grant eligibility, fraud risk and payment beneficiary verification are kept separate so a confident identity match never substitutes for destination verification (UNB-CHAR-006). Duplicate or split grants are detected by recommendation fingerprint while legitimate recurring installments are preserved (EXC-10, UNB-GRANT-029). Grant purpose rules block restricted purposes and prohibited benefits (UNB-SCTRL-016), and grants to recipients linked to sponsor vendors or fund privilege holders route to related-party review (UNB-XIN-ERP-004). Only holds derived from verified public facts propagate across sponsors; private suspicions do not (CNV-GRT-004).
intended_practice: Implement fraud signals as P-class outputs that route to human review and holds, never auto-clear or auto-deny (UNB-CTL-001).
owner: Not assigned; proposed: Unbound fraud and payments risk owner (role not staffed) with each sponsor's fraud operations owner

title: Fraud monitoring program, anomaly detection and Nacha 2026 amendments
target_answer: For each sponsor that originates ACH entries, Unbound maintains a documented FraudMonitoringProgram covering at least destination-change after-the-fact review, first payment to a new destination, amount anomalies against the recipient's history, request-channel provenance for bank-detail changes and debit-origination anomalies; each rule has a version, owner, risk rationale and outcome metrics, and new ACH origination is blocked if the last completed program review is older than 12 months plus a grace period (UNB-XIN-BNK-002). As a Third-Party Service Provider, Unbound accepts by contract the Nacha risk-based fraud monitoring obligations that apply to it, alongside security and audit cooperation (CNV-PAY-001); a documented program is a precondition of the RailGoLive gate (RR-UNB-PAY-008-r1). Anomaly and AI signals are independently reviewable and cannot clear controls alone (UNB-ACC-035, UNB-CTL-005). Suspected fraud and account takeover cases use a restricted-investigation access class, are excluded from general search and AI context, and the investigator does not make the sponsor decision on the subject transaction (UNB-XIN-CLM-004).
intended_practice: Build the rule registry and review gate; confirm the applicable Nacha phase and obligations with counsel and each sponsor's ODFI.

title: Financial statements and financial transparency package
target_answer: Because an audit is disproportionate at our stage, we offer a financial transparency package under NDA: annual financial statements reviewed by an independent CPA (moving to audited statements once revenue or customer requirements justify the cost), quarterly management accounts, and a quarterly runway attestation signed by the managing member and supported by a bank balance confirmation. Business and personal finances are fully separated. We state plainly whether any statement is audited, reviewed, compiled or internally prepared.

title: Funding, runway, concentration and financial notification covenants
target_answer: We disclose under NDA our funding sources, cash on hand, monthly net burn, runway, committed funding and revenue concentration, and the decision rules we will apply if funding or revenue falls short. We contractually commit to notify customers within 10 business days if runway falls below 12 months, if a funding commitment fails, or if we lose a customer representing more than a stated share of revenue, and such notice triggers the customer's transition rights and an escrow verification. Our pricing is set to cover cost to serve without subsidy, with cost attribution evidence.

title: Insolvency and cessation protection: escrow, wind-down and customer-controlled data
target_answer: A vendor failure cannot trap customer data or money. Unbound never holds, controls or executes movement of donor or grant funds (CNV-LEG-001). Customers can export their complete records at any time in a documented open format without Echelon involvement, verified by a per-release round-trip test. Source code, build scripts, infrastructure definitions and runbooks for the customer's deployment are deposited with an independent escrow agent at every release, with release conditions including insolvency, cessation of business, failure to support and assignment for benefit of creditors, and the agent performs a build verification at least annually. The license survives bankruptcy and grants the customer a right to host and maintain the software for its own use. A written wind-down plan and a reserve sized to fund an orderly transition period are maintained and tested.
intended_practice: Select an escrow agent; implement export tooling with a release gate; write wind-down plan before first production customer.

title: Vendor internal financial controls, banking authority and tax standing
target_answer: Company bank accounts require dual authorization above a stated threshold using the bank's own approval workflow, with a second authorized person or an outside accountant; bank statements are reconciled monthly by someone other than the payment initiator, or reviewed by an outside accountant where staff is insufficient. Federal, state and payroll tax filings are current, with no liens. Customer billing is computed from the versioned fee schedule (UNB-SMP-ECN-004) with an auditable calculation trail.
intended_practice: Open business accounts with dual control; engage outside accountant for monthly review.

title: External financial signals and ongoing financial monitoring
target_answer: We authorize customers to obtain a business credit report and provide bank and trade references on request. During the term we notify customers of defined financial events: loss of funding, default on material debt, material litigation, loss of a major customer, and change of control. Our capacity model states how many sponsors of a given size we can onboard and support concurrently, and we decline commitments beyond it.

title: Legal entity identity, formation status and contracting entity
target_answer: Echelon Foundry, LLC is an Indiana limited liability company in good standing. We provide, on request and before signature, a current certificate of existence, the filed articles of organization, our EIN on a signed W-9, and our registered agent. The same entity owns the intellectual property, engages all personnel and contractors, holds the cloud and code-hosting accounts and signs the customer agreement. title: Beneficial ownership, control persons and change of control
target_answer: We disclose under NDA every beneficial owner holding 25 percent or more and every individual with significant managerial control, any foreign ownership or control rights, and investor rights that affect product, pricing or data use. Owners and officers are screened against sanctions lists at onboarding and on list updates. The customer agreement gives the customer written notice of a change of control within a defined period and a right to terminate without penalty.

title: Governing body, officers, decision authority and oversight of risk
target_answer: Authority is written down: the operating agreement names the manager(s), a delegation-of-authority matrix states who may sign contracts, accept risk, approve policy and approve security exceptions, and every material decision is recorded as a decision record with owner, rationale, alternatives, evidence and review date. An advisory board including at least one person independent of ownership with security or financial-services control experience reviews risk and security at least quarterly and its review is minuted. AI agents may draft governance material but cannot approve it; approval is attributed to a named human.

title: Key-person dependence and succession
target_answer: We treat key-person dependence as a primary risk and mitigate it with mechanisms that work without the principal: (1) the operating agreement designates a successor manager with springing authority on death or incapacity; (2) break-glass credentials for cloud, domain, code hosting and signing keys are held in sealed custody by a named second party, with access logged and tested annually; (3) source code, infrastructure definitions, deployment runbooks and data export tooling are deposited with an escrow agent and verified by an independent build test; (4) customer data is always exportable by the customer without Echelon involvement; (5) Praxis records keep decisions, research and handoffs durable outside any person's memory or an AI conversation; (6) key-person life and disability insurance funds an orderly transition. We report the number of people holding each critical capability.
intended_practice: Implement the six mechanisms before the first production customer, prioritizing credential custody, escrow and customer-controlled export.

title: Policy governance: adoption, review, publication and enforceability
target_answer: Every policy is a versioned record with owner, approver, approval date, effective date, next review date and the controls and checks that enforce each rule. Policies are adopted by the managing member and reviewed at least annually or on material change. Each mandatory rule maps to an enforcing check or a recorded manual procedure; a rule with neither fails the policy build. The customer-facing copy is generated from the approved version and carries its hash and approval date.
intended_practice: Adopt the Secure Construction Standard and a minimum policy set; maintain them as machine-readable records under Praxis.

title: Conflicts of interest and related-party relationships with sponsors
target_answer: Echelon maintains a conflict-of-interest policy covering owners, personnel and contractors, with annual and event-driven disclosure, and a register of every role an Echelon person holds at a customer, grantee, investment manager, custodian or competitor. We disclose to each sponsor any relationship that could make an Echelon person an interested person for Form 990 Schedule L or a disqualified person for section 4958, and provide the information the sponsor needs for its own analysis. Echelon receives no referral fees, revenue share or other compensation from investment managers, custodians, payment providers or charities connected to the service, and contracts say so.

title: Regulatory status, registrations and regulatory change management
target_answer: Echelon states its regulatory perimeter precisely: it is not a bank, money transmitter, investment adviser or broker-dealer because the platform never holds, controls or executes movement of customer funds, which is enforced by architecture (CNV-LEG-001). It holds the registrations its activities actually require, such as California charitable fundraising platform registration where applicable, and accepts examination by a customer's regulator where law provides for it. A regulatory change log, reviewed by counsel, records changes that affect Echelon or customers and the resulting requirement changes.

title: Grant recommendation intake, affirmation and duplicate detection
target_answer: A grant recommendation is a typed request that captures recommender, fund, recipient identity, purpose, amount, timing, restrictions and recognition preference, together with an affirmation evidence record (presented disclosure text and hash, the donor's no-benefit and no-pledge certifications, channel, time and idempotency key). Submission never creates an entitlement or moves money. Duplicate and replayed submissions are handled idempotently, and suspicious repeated or split recommendations are flagged across channels.
intended_practice: Recommendation command per UNB-GRANT-001/002/029 with AffirmationEvidence per UNB-RCN-GRT-010.
owner: Unbound product owner (proposed role; not yet assigned)

title: Grant approval workflow, board-delegated policy approval and segregation of duties
target_answer: Approval authority derives from a recorded sponsor board or committee resolution. Until such a resolution adopts a version-pinned policy and names a delegate, deterministic policy only recommends and an accountable person decides. Once delegated, conforming items may be approved by policy under the delegate's authority, while exceptions and enhanced-review triggers route to qualified humans by amount, risk and relationship. The engine enforces segregation of duties, vendor staff and AI agents cannot hold approval authority, decision quality is checked by risk-stratified sampling, and approval atomically reserves the approved amount.
intended_practice: Policy-delegation model per CNV-GRT-001, routing per UNB-GRANT-012 and CNV-GRT-011, authority per CNV-GOV-003/004/010, reservation per CNV-FIN-001.
owner: Unbound product owner (proposed role; not yet assigned)

title: Grant purpose, restrictions, agreements and post-approval modification
target_answer: Grant purposes and restrictions are structured data evaluated against sponsor, program and fund policy in explicit precedence order. Restrictions that would deliver a benefit to the donor or name a foreign organization through an intermediary are blocked or routed for review. Grant agreements, milestones and reporting obligations are supported for conditional grants. Material modifications after approval (recipient, amount, purpose, timing, restrictions) require re-evaluation and human approval.
intended_practice: Restriction evaluation per UNB-GRANT-010 and UNB-GRANT-024; modification control per UNB-GRANT-048; intermediary wording per CNV-GRT-008.
owner: Unbound product owner (proposed role; not yet assigned)

title: Recurring and scheduled grants with per-instance re-evaluation
target_answer: Each instance of a recurring or scheduled grant re-checks the template author's current authority, the recipient's eligibility and sanctions status, fund availability and current sponsor policy at execution, and reserves individually. Series are paused, not silently skipped, on failure; changes in purpose, class or eligibility require reconfirmation, and series affected by a recipient merger carry a notice-and-opt-out window.
intended_practice: Per-instance checks per TVR-GR-005, TVR-GR-008 and UNB-GRANT-027; notice rules per CNV-GRT-010.
owner: Unbound product owner (proposed role; not yet assigned)

title: Pledges, event benefits and other prohibited benefit scenarios
target_answer: Pledge handling is an explicit sponsor policy choice (Prohibited, NonBindingOnly, or conditions consistent with IRS Notice 2017-73 section 7). Embedded and API giving requests declare a typed host context (donation, event ticket, sponsorship, auction, membership with benefits), and benefit-bearing contexts are rejected or routed to the benefit gate. Grants are blocked to purposes that provide tuition, memberships with more than incidental benefits, or tickets, and bifurcated grants (DAF pays the charitable portion, donor pays the benefit) follow sponsor policy.
intended_practice: Pledge policy per CNV-GRT-010; host context per UNB-RCN-GRT-012; benefit evaluation per UNB-GRANT-011.
owner: Unbound product owner (proposed role; not yet assigned)

title: Neutral decline reasons and independent reconsideration
target_answer: Declines use a sponsor-configurable neutral catalog: donor-facing text describes the policy outcome, never facts about a charity; sanctions, investigation and law-enforcement reasons map to a generic compliance review code; charity-facing communication is limited to status codes. Reconsideration defaults to a 60-day filing window and a 30-day response target, is decided by a reviewer independent of the original decision, and both records survive with outcomes Upheld, Reversed, Modified, Withdrawn or Referred.
intended_practice: Decline catalog and reconsideration per CNV-GRT-012; explanations per UNB-GRANT-037.
owner: Unbound product owner (proposed role; not yet assigned)

title: Payee substitution, payment destination integrity and partner exclusion from funds flow
target_answer: Canonical charity identity, legal payee, fiscal sponsor, project and payment destination are resolved separately. Payee substitution to a merger successor requires a verified legal successor passing eligibility on its own EIN in the same recipient class, sponsor approval and donor notice. Bank-detail changes require independent verification (bank-originated account owner match, cooling-off, notice to old and new verified channels) and dual control, and unverified changes cannot propagate into approved payment instructions. No partner, host or vendor account ever appears in the payment path.
intended_practice: Payee resolution per UNB-GRANT-007, substitution per CNV-GRT-010, bank change controls per UNB-GEX-018 and CNV-PAY-002, propagation block per UNB-CHAR-032.

title: Returned, uncashed and refunded grant payments
target_answer: Payment states distinguish prepared, approved, submitted, accepted, rejected, settled, returned and reconciled. Returns after disbursement are accepted and restore the fund through linked reversal entries, uncashed checks follow a sponsor-approved aging and reissue or redirect policy that considers state unclaimed property rules, and grantee refunds are recorded as linked corrections with donor notice. Unknown payment outcomes are never treated as failures without proof.
intended_practice: Payment state model per UNB-GRANT-022, returns per TVR-GR-002, exceptions per UNB-PAY-006 and CNV-PAY-003/004.

Letters name the sponsor as grantor, state that no goods or services may be provided to the donor, reflect the donor's recognition preference, and distinguish award, accounting recognition, payment, settlement and grantee receipt dates.

title: Grant anonymity and recognition preferences
target_answer: Each grant carries a recognition election (full name, name only, custom attribution, fund name only, anonymous), stored as an authority fact with effective time. Correspondence, remittance data and payment references are derived from the election at send time; immediately before external send the delivery worker re-reads the current election and suppresses or regenerates the message if it changed. title: Background screening of personnel
target_answer: Every person (founder, employee or contractor) who will have access to customer data or production systems completes a background check before access is granted, conducted through an FCRA-compliant consumer reporting agency with applicable state fair-chance procedures: identity verification, criminal history in jurisdictions of residence for seven years, sanctions and exclusion lists, and employment and education verification; enhanced checks (credit history where lawful, fingerprint-based checks where a bank customer requires them) apply to roles with financial-system or privileged access. Checks are repeated every three years and on promotion to privileged roles. Founders are screened like everyone else and results are available to customers in summary under NDA. Access provisioning requires a screening record.

title: Security, privacy and role-specific training

title: Joiner, mover and leaver access lifecycle across all systems

title: AI agents as workforce: scope, permissions, accountability and revocation

title: Security leadership, staffing adequacy and segregation of duties in a small team
target_answer: A named individual is accountable for information security, with qualifications disclosed, supported by an external security advisor (virtual CISO) under contract until a dedicated hire is justified. Privileged production access is held by at least two named people, with no standing access for routine work. Where one person would otherwise control request, approval and execution, segregation is achieved through independent gates and a second approver (CNV-PLT-010 requires two approvers on control-relevant modules). title: Workforce joiner, mover and leaver lifecycle
target_answer: All workforce access derives from a single authoritative identity provider tied to an engagement record (employee or contractor, with end date). Access is granted only through approved role bundles; there is no direct grant on target systems. Termination disables the identity provider account immediately (same business day for voluntary departures, immediately for involuntary), which cascades through federation to every connected system; systems that cannot federate are listed and deprovisioned by an automated task with evidence. Role changes revoke old access before new access is granted. Dormant accounts are disabled after a defined inactivity period. A daily match of identity-provider administrative actions against approved requests detects unapproved grants (TVR-SEC-008).

title: Periodic access recertification and continuous entitlement hygiene
target_answer: Access recertification runs quarterly for privileged and workforce roles and at least annually for delegated customer roles (advisors, authorized viewers, agents), and covers third-party authority registers such as bank-portal users and custodian trading authorities. Reviewers cannot certify their own access. Uncertified access is suspended automatically 14 days after the due date and the suspension is recorded and notified. Between reviews, grants carry expiry dates and are revoked by events (termination, role change, death or incapacity, partner exit), so the review confirms a mostly self-cleaning population rather than discovering it. Review evidence includes the complete population with counts reconciled to the system of record.
intended_practice: Implement the recertification campaign engine with automatic suspension and population reconciliation.

title: Privileged access to production infrastructure and databases
target_answer: There is no standing administrative access to production. Privileged access uses a dedicated PlatformWorkforce principal distinct from any customer or everyday identity, authenticated with AAL3-grade hardware or device-bound keys, elevated just in time for a bounded task with approval by a second person, and recorded in logs that the elevated principal cannot alter. Production database administrative roles are break-glass only with two-person activation. Application identities hold INSERT and constrained SELECT on authoritative tables and no UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE or DDL. The number of people eligible for elevation is published to customers.
