title: Break-glass emergency access
target_answer: Break-glass credentials are sealed and independent of the workforce identity provider, require two-person activation, expire automatically within four hours, page the security owner, and notify affected tenants' administrators within one hour. Break-glass sessions are limited to reading, protective actions (payment freeze, hold, credential revocation) and infrastructure recovery; they cannot approve grants, change payees, change authority, post ledger entries or remove holds. Any authoritative state change without a matching command event blocks affected payments until reviewed. Procedures are tested at least annually without using real customer data.
intended_practice: Implement sealed credential storage, activation workflow and post-use review before production.
owner: Unassigned; proposed Security Lead

title: Vendor staff access to customer tenant data and access transparency
target_answer: Vendor staff have no access to a customer's non-public data by default. Read diagnostics require an OperatorAccessDelegation pre-approved by the sponsor for listed task classes, scopes and maximum duration; writes require per-case approval by an authorized sponsor approver. Staff cannot perform sponsor decisions (grant approval, payee change, authority change, fund closure) unless the sponsor's delegation names that command class. Revocation takes effect on the next request. Every operator session appears to the customer's administrators within 15 minutes with who, when, scope, reason, case and records touched. Support 'view as' is a distinct low-assurance command kind that cannot add recipients without sponsor-direct confirmation. Support personnel locations and subcontractors are disclosed.
intended_practice: Implement OperatorAccessDelegation, per-case approval and the transparency view as part of the authorization core.
owner: Unassigned; proposed Security Lead

title: Service accounts, workload identities and machine credentials
target_answer: Every workload (service, job, CI pipeline, agent) has its own identity in the Workload realm, registered in an inventory with owner and purpose. Credentials are short-lived and obtained by workload identity federation (for example OIDC from CI) rather than stored static secrets; any unavoidable static secret is held in a managed secret store and rotated automatically. Workload identities cannot log in interactively. Each component uses a distinct least-privilege database role; no application identity can UPDATE or DELETE authoritative event or journal tables. CI can deploy only artifacts that passed gates and only with approval for control-relevant modules.
intended_practice: Adopt workload identity federation and a secret manager for all Unbound workloads; generate service account inventory from infrastructure code.
owner: Unassigned; proposed Security Lead

title: AI agent identities, authority bounds and suspension
target_answer: Each product agent is a distinct Workload principal with a named human owner, a declared capability manifest and an authority tier. When an agent acts for a user, it holds a delegated grant derived from that user's authority that can never exceed it and ends when the parent ends; the delegation chain is recorded on every action. Agents cannot grant themselves permissions, approve their own consequential actions, change their own policy or clear their own alerts. Prohibited tools are removed by the tool broker rather than forbidden by prompt. A global and per-tenant emergency stop suspends agents and safely parks queued actions. Engineering agents never hold production customer-data credentials; their CI identity is authenticated workload identity rather than self-declared. Agent identities are included in access reviews and deprovisioned when retired.
intended_practice: Implement agent principals, delegation chains, tool broker and emergency stop; bind engineering agent CI runs to authenticated workload identity.
owner: Unassigned; proposed AI Governance owner with Security Lead

title: Customer administrator delegation and customer-side user management
target_answer: Sponsor administrators manage their own users within the SponsorWorkforce realm and may delegate administration of defined scopes (program, partner, function) to sub-administrators. No administrator can grant a permission they do not hold or assign sponsor-reserved authority. Distribution-partner administrators manage only PartnerWorkforce users for their partner and cannot administer sponsor-reserved functions. Changes to administrator roles require step-up authentication and, for the top administrative tier, a second sponsor approver. Delegated roles expire and are recertified. If a customer loses all administrators, recovery requires verified authorization from the customer's designated officers through an out-of-band, identity-proofed procedure with a waiting period and notification to all prior administrators; vendor staff cannot grant administrative rights on their own.
intended_practice: Implement delegated administration with subset-only grants and an administrator recovery procedure.

title: Identity lifecycle for donors, advisors and partner-federated users
target_answer: Donors and advisors are identity-proofed by a risk-based process that validates core attributes against authoritative sources, matches the funding account owner, and steps up to document verification or a non-biometric alternative when needed; knowledge-based questions are never used for proofing. Each person has one principal per sponsor and per realm; a staff member who is also a donor has two principals linked only by an audited link that confers no privilege. On verified death or incapacity, all rights, sessions and delegated agent principals derived from that person are suspended in one transaction; an unverified notice only holds new actions. Users federated through a distribution partner are offered a sponsor-direct authenticator at first login so they keep access to their funds if the partner relationship ends.
intended_practice: Implement realms, proofing workflow, lifecycle events and sponsor-direct enrollment.

title: Hosting model and deployment topology
target_answer: Unbound is hosted on a major public cloud provider selected through a documented decision (open), using managed platform services rather than self-operated servers wherever available: a managed container or application platform for the single F# deployable (REQ-X-020) and managed PostgreSQL for the authoritative store (CNV-ARC-001, CNV-ARC-004). Each sponsor is placed in a deployment cell according to its isolation profile (UNB-TEN-002). Echelon operates no data centers or physical servers. The topology, providers and regions are published in the system description and subservice organization list.
intended_practice: Record a hosting ADR covering provider, compute model, managed PostgreSQL service and regions, satisfying ADR-001 and ADR-008 in the persistence design.

title: Hardening baselines for hosts, images and managed services
target_answer: Unbound runs on minimal container images built from an approved base (distroless or minimal OS with only the .NET runtime and required native libraries), rebuilt in the pipeline on every release and at least weekly. Images run as non-root with no shell or package manager. Where hosts are visible to Echelon, they follow CIS Benchmark-aligned settings applied by the platform; for managed services, Echelon applies the provider's security configuration baseline and records deviations. Hardening settings are expressed as policy-as-code and verified at build and at admission, not by periodic manual review.
intended_practice: Define base image and managed-service baselines once the provider is chosen; add image policy checks to the release gate.
owner: unassigned

title: Infrastructure patching and vulnerability remediation
target_answer: Infrastructure is patched by rebuilding, not by patching in place. Every release rebuilds images from current base images and dependencies; an automated weekly rebuild runs even without code changes. Vulnerabilities in images, the .NET runtime, NuGet packages and managed service versions are scanned on each build and daily against the deployed inventory. Remediation targets are tied to exploitability: actively exploited (CISA KEV listed) issues reachable in Unbound within days, other critical issues within 14 days, high within 30 days, with exceptions time-limited and approved (SOC2-033). Managed PostgreSQL minor versions follow the provider's maintenance window; major upgrades are gated by Strata compatibility (CNV-ARC-004).
intended_practice: Adopt scanning with the release pipeline; define SLA with exploitability weighting; record exceptions as data.
owner: unassigned

title: Container and runtime isolation
target_answer: Workloads run as containers on a managed orchestrator or platform where Echelon does not operate the control plane. Admission policy enforces: images only from Echelon's registry with verified signatures and provenance; non-root user; read-only root filesystem; no privileged mode, host networking, host path mounts or added capabilities; resource limits set. Each image has an SBOM (CycloneDX) generated at build. Tenant data isolation does not depend on container boundaries, since all tenants in a cell share the same application release (RR-UNB-PLAT-008-r1); dedicated-infrastructure tenants run in separate clusters or cells.
intended_practice: Select platform; write admission policies; generate SBOM and signed provenance in the build.

title: Immutable infrastructure and pipeline-only change
target_answer: Production is never modified interactively. Every change to application or infrastructure is a reviewed commit, built by the pipeline into a signed artifact with recorded provenance (CNV-PLT-010; SLSA build provenance), and deployed by replacing running instances. Workloads have no shell access in production; diagnostic access is through logs and the brokered process in ANS-NET-005. Emergency changes use the same pipeline with an expedited approval path, never a console edit. Rollback is a redeploy of a prior signed artifact.
intended_practice: Make the pipeline the only identity with production write permissions; record each deployment as an evidence event.

title: Infrastructure as code and policy as code
target_answer: All cloud resources, network rules, identities, key policies and managed service settings are defined in version-controlled infrastructure as code, reviewed like application code, with policy-as-code checks (no public data stores, encryption required, approved regions only, logging enabled) run on every change before apply. Control-relevant infrastructure (network boundary, key policies, identity) requires two approvers, neither the author (CNV-PLT-010). Plans and applied changes are retained as evidence. AI agents may propose infrastructure changes but cannot approve or apply them.
intended_practice: Choose IaC tool compatible with the provider and Echelon's .NET/F# toolchain; codify guardrails before first resource is created.

title: Configuration drift detection and baseline evidence
target_answer: The IaC definition is the baseline. A scheduled reconciliation compares live cloud configuration to IaC state at least daily and on every provider configuration change event; any drift raises a control exception and is either reverted automatically (for guardrail settings) or reviewed within one business day. Provider configuration change logs are retained in the security log account. Evidence is the continuous drift report, not a periodic screenshot.
intended_practice: Implement drift detection with IaC; classify which drift is auto-reverted.

title: Production access and environment separation
target_answer: Production is a separate cloud account with no human standing write access. Engineers and AI agents work only in non-production environments that contain synthetic data; production data is never copied to non-production (SOC2-031 requires production and synthetic evidence to be kept distinct). Read diagnostics in production are scoped, expiring and sponsor pre-approved; writes require per-case approval (CNV-ARC-002). Production database administrative roles are break-glass with two-person activation (CNV-PLT-010). Access grants and every use are evidence events, and quarterly access reviews are generated from those events.
intended_practice: Implement account separation and access broker with the hosting decision.

title: Supported component lifecycle and end-of-life management

For PostgreSQL, the upgrade path is gated by Strata support for the target version (CNV-ARC-004) so the platform cannot be stranded on an unsupported database version. Unbound targets the current .NET long-term support release.

title: Investment authority, regulatory boundary and adviser involvement
target_answer: Unbound is not an investment adviser and does not provide investment advice. It does not author fund- or donor-specific securities or allocation recommendations, construct models, select managers, route orders for others' accounts, take compensation varying with assets, trades or liquidations, or hold custody. title: Allocation elections and rebalancing

title: Unitization, valuation inputs and NAV publication
target_answer: Under the adopted operating model, unit values and positions come from the sponsor's external manager or custodian and are reconciled to the custodian; Unbound derives fund-level valuations from those inputs and a missing or stale manager price blocks the affected statement rather than being estimated. In-tolerance fund-level valuations publish by deterministic policy only under a recorded investment-committee delegation that approves tolerances and pricing sources, reviewed at least annually; out-of-tolerance, stale, missing or overridden prices route to a human approver before publication, and a risk-based independent sample is reviewed the next business day. Without a delegation every valuation requires a human checker. Valuation states (Draft, InputsValidated, Calculated, ExceptionHold, IndependentlyReviewed, Approved, Published, Superseded, Rejected) make publication a controlled act. Authoritative monetary and unit arithmetic uses fixed-precision decimal with specified rounding and residual allocation, never binary floating point; F# decimal types make this the default. Subscriptions and redemptions use forward pricing with explicit trade, valuation and settlement dates so no participant or agent can select a known historical price.

title: Valuation errors, corrections and remediation
target_answer: Corrected valuations are new approved publications linked to the original, recording cause class (source price error, missed position, late trade, corporate action, FX, fee accrual, cutoff, unit allocation, fraud or unauthorized override), affected period, funds, materiality, reviewer and remediation plan. Counterfactual unit and money impacts are calculated for every affected fund, transaction, grant, fee and statement; a sponsor-approved materiality and remediation policy decides compensation, restatement, unit adjustment, corrected statements and escalation to auditor. Settled transfers and historical unit issuance are never overwritten; corrective events are appended. Closed-period corrections require separate restatement authority and the originally issued reports remain reproducible. Propagation is idempotent, bounded and approval-gated.

title: Investment policy compliance, liquidity and concentration
target_answer: Sponsor investment policies and exceptions are versioned, effective-dated and linked to decisions and reporting evidence. Policy defines menus, prohibited investments, concentration limits, liquidity thresholds, rebalancing tolerance, manager eligibility and escalation. Pre-trade and post-trade compliance checks run against holdings reported by the manager. Each fund's external investments are backed by a sponsor-approved liquidity buffer at the custodian derived from a documented stress model (net outflow over the settlement horizon including the December peak); a fixed percentage is allowed only as a labeled placeholder until twelve months of outflow data exist. No display implies unsettled or illiquid assets are spendable. Business-enterprise holdings are computed with related persons before accepting a business interest and on later transactions to track excess business holdings disposal periods. The sponsor can freeze trading for compliance holds, valuation uncertainty or liquidity stress.

title: Prudent investment governance support (UPMIFA) and performance and cost reporting
target_answer: Unbound supports, but does not perform, the sponsor board's prudence duties. Under CNV-LEG-001 the board selects the external manager, sets scope and investment policy and monitors performance and cost; Unbound provides decision records (delegations, policy versions, manager reviews, exceptions) and reports with explicit methodology: time-weighted versus money-weighted returns, benchmarks, gross and net of fees, cash-flow timing and as-of dates, and never presents accounting gains as performance. Manager fees, pool fees and fund charges are shown without double counting so the board can assess cost reasonableness. Whether UPMIFA applies to a sponsor's DAF assets, and whether any fund is an endowment fund subject to its spending provisions, is a counsel determination per state; Unbound requirements contain no explicit UPMIFA requirement.

title: Valuation of illiquid and non-cash assets
target_answer: Valuation methodology is defined per asset class and structure. A pricing hierarchy (independent market feed, custodian mark, approved valuation service, documented manual appraisal, or explicit hold) has policy-controlled precedence and freshness limits. Illiquid valuations require appraisal methodology, approval, uncertainty range where meaningful, age limits and valuation-event triggers, marked provisional where policy permits. Stale, conflicting, missing or outlier prices create exceptions with severity and reviewer decision; prices are never silently forward-filled, and provider observations are evidence, not automatically approved marks. Continuously traded assets record exact UTC timestamp, valuation convention and source; contributed crypto above counsel-set thresholds is flagged for donor qualified appraisal. The donor's tax appraisal, the sponsor's book value and proceeds are separate typed values. In-kind workflows record asset classification, completed-gift rule, acceptance decision, holdings test and liquidation policy before acceptance.
