title: Incident response roles, on-call coverage and external support
target_answer: A named incident commander and at least one trained deputy, 24x7 paging with escalation, a retained incident response and forensics firm, outside breach counsel, and a verified customer contact registry; AI agents may gather evidence and draft communications but may not send regulatory or customer notices, release holds or destroy evidence without human approval.
intended_practice: Assign roles and contract a retainer before production.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)

title: Incident response testing and exercises
target_answer: Annual tabletop exercises covering ransomware, insider misuse, compromised AI agent, cross-tenant exposure and an incident during year-end giving peaks, with customer participation offered; semiannual automated technical drills measuring time to retrieve logs, disable accounts, place a sponsor-policy hold, revoke agent credentials and rotate keys; corrective actions tracked to closure and summaries shared.
intended_practice: Hold the first tabletop when the plan is approved.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)

title: Customer incident notification commitments
target_answer: Initial notice to affected customers within 24 hours of reasonable suspicion that customer data or covered services are affected, with updates at least every 24 hours until containment and a final report; the clock starts at reasonable suspicion, not confirmation; notices include what is known, affected data and tenants, actions taken, recommended customer actions and contact; notices are sent to registered contacts and confirmed over a second authenticated channel; subprocessor incidents and incidents affecting shared infrastructure or the same release are included.
intended_practice: Adopt in the security addendum after counsel review.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)

title: Bank service provider notification under the 2021 Computer-Security Incident Notification rule
target_answer: Where Echelon provides services to a banking organization subject to the Bank Service Company Act, it notifies each affected bank customer's designated contacts as soon as possible after determining that a computer-security incident has materially disrupted or degraded, or is reasonably likely to materially disrupt or degrade, covered services for four or more hours, and supports the bank's own 36-hour determination and notification to its primary federal regulator with rapid, structured facts. Scheduled maintenance previously communicated is excluded as the rule provides. Designated contacts are collected at onboarding and verified.
intended_practice: Determine applicability with counsel and build into the obligation matrix.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)

title: Service provider notice under amended SEC Regulation S-P (2024)
target_answer: For covered-institution customers, Echelon contractually agrees to take appropriate measures to protect against unauthorized access to customer information and to notify the covered institution as soon as possible and no later than 72 hours after becoming aware of a breach resulting in unauthorized access to a customer information system Echelon maintains; provides structured facts on sensitive customer information affected so the customer can meet its 30-day individual notification deadline; and supports the customer's service provider due diligence and monitoring.
intended_practice: Determine customer types and adopt contract terms with counsel.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)

title: Support for state breach laws and other regulatory notification obligations
target_answer: An obligation matrix reviewed by counsel maps each customer type and jurisdiction to its deadlines; Echelon notifies data owners as state laws require of service providers, and provides structured incident data (affected individuals by state of residence, data elements, timeline, containment) quickly enough for customers to meet NYDFS 72-hour, GDPR 72-hour, FTC 30-day and SEC four-business-day materiality-based deadlines.
intended_practice: Build the matrix with counsel before production.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)

title: Forensics, evidence preservation and regulator cooperation
target_answer: On declaration, logs, snapshots, images and agent ledgers in scope are preserved with hashes and chain of custody under legal hold for at least the longer of seven years or the applicable hold; customers' forensic firms may participate under coordination; Echelon cooperates with customers' regulators, auditors and law enforcement and provides records within agreed timeframes; forensic summaries are shared with affected customers.
intended_practice: Define preservation procedures with the logging architecture.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)

title: Post-incident review and lessons learned
target_answer: Every significant incident yields a blameless root cause analysis within 10 business days, a customer-facing post-incident report within 15 business days, corrective actions tracked to verified completion, and updates to threat models, invariants, regression tests and detections.
intended_practice: Apply Tutela incident ingestion once Unbound operates.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)

title: Ransomware preparedness and ransom payment policy
target_answer: Backups are immutable or logically isolated from production and administrative credentials and are restore-tested quarterly; the plan assumes no ransom payment, and any extortion decision requires counsel, insurer (if any) and sanctions screening against OFAC lists, with law enforcement engagement; customers are informed promptly of any data theft or extortion threat involving their data.
intended_practice: Implement with backup architecture (see BKP).
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)

title: Containment: credential revocation, tenant isolation, platform holds and AI agent kill switch
target_answer: Pre-authorized containment actions execute within minutes: revoke workforce, service and agent credentials; isolate a tenant; place platform holds under the sponsor's adopted hold policy that never move, reverse or redirect funds and leave the sponsor able to pay through its own bank; stop all or specific AI agents and review every action they took in the affected window from the agent ledger.
intended_practice: Implement with identity, hold policy and agent runtime.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)

title: Incident history disclosure
target_answer: Echelon discloses, under NDA, all security incidents in the last three years that required notification to customers or regulators, with summaries of root cause and corrective actions, and any related litigation or regulatory action.
intended_practice: Maintain an incident register from formation onward.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)

title: Written information security program, scope and governance
target_answer: Echelon maintains a written information security program approved by its managing member(s) or board, scoped to Echelon Foundry, LLC, all Echelon products (including Unbound), all personnel, contractors and the AI agents that perform engineering and operations work. The program is aligned primarily to NIST CSF 2.0 with control mappings to SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria and ISO/IEC 27001 Annex A, is reviewed at least annually and on material change, and tracks regulatory change for the customer segments served (GLBA Safeguards, NYDFS Part 500 for New York covered entities, FFIEC guidance for banks). Program records, control register and evidence are machine-readable and versioned.
intended_practice: Adopt a program charter and policy set by formal resolution of the LLC's governing body, then operate the Unbound control register as the program's control inventory.
owner: Unassigned; proposed Echelon managing member

title: Security leadership: CISO or qualified individual, independence and succession
target_answer: Echelon designates a qualified individual (CISO or equivalent, which may be a contracted fractional CISO with documented oversight) who owns the program, reports in writing at least annually to the governing body, has direct access to the governing body and to sponsor audit and risk committees where contracts require it, can block a release on security grounds through the mandatory release gates, and has a documented deputy for incident periods.
intended_practice: Appoint a qualified individual before onboarding any customer data; record the appointment, qualifications, reporting line and deputy; give the role release-blocking authority through Praxis gates.
owner: Unassigned; proposed Echelon managing member

title: Security policy set: content, approval, review and communication
target_answer: Echelon maintains a complete, versioned policy set (information security, acceptable use, access control, secure construction, cryptography, change management, incident response, vendor management, data classification and retention, business continuity, AI agent operations), each with an owner, approval record, effective date and annual review. Policies are written as stable rule identifiers (for example SEC-AUTH-001) so that each rule maps to an enforcement mechanism, negative tests and evidence. Mandatory rules are enforced by fail-closed build and release gates; agent operating instructions (AGENTS.md) reference the same rule identifiers. Personnel and contractors acknowledge policies at onboarding and on material change.
intended_practice: Formally adopt the standard and author the remaining policies with rule identifiers mapped to enforcement and evidence.
owner: Unassigned; proposed CISO or qualified individual

title: Policy exceptions and risk acceptance
target_answer: Every exception to a mandatory rule is a recorded, versioned object with scope, rationale, compensating controls, approver (who cannot be the requester), expiry and linked evidence. Build and release gates read the exception register; an expired exception fails the gate automatically. Risk acceptance authority is defined by risk tier. There is no mechanism, for humans or AI agents, to bypass a mandatory gate without creating such a record, and the count and age of open exceptions are reported to leadership and, in summary, to customers.
intended_practice: Implement an exception register consumed by Praxis gates; report exception counts in program metrics.
owner: Unassigned; proposed CISO or qualified individual

title: Security metrics and control effectiveness reporting
target_answer: Echelon reports control effectiveness metrics generated from the control register and evidence stream: controls with owners, evidence emitted on schedule, missed runs, evidence integrity failures, overdue access reviews, open exceptions and their age, remediation aging by severity, negative-test pass rates for mandatory rules and tested effectiveness. Each metric carries its population definition, query, run log and hash (information produced by entity support) so a reviewer can verify completeness. A customer-facing summary is published monthly; detail is available under NDA.
intended_practice: Build the metric set from the control register once controls operate; publish a monthly continuous assurance summary as the Secure Construction Standard proposes.
owner: Unassigned; proposed Security Lead

title: Security awareness and role-based training
target_answer: All personnel and contractors complete security awareness training at onboarding and annually, with completion tracked and access suspended automatically when overdue. Role-based training covers secure construction for engineers, privileged access for administrators, and social engineering of support staff, including fraudulent payee, contact-detail and authenticator-reset requests and business email compromise patterns common in DAF and wealth-management operations. Because phishing-resistant authentication and structural controls remove many click-to-compromise paths, simulations focus on support-channel manipulation and approval fraud rather than credential capture.
intended_practice: Select a training provider or build role-specific modules; integrate completion with access provisioning.
owner: Unassigned; proposed CISO or qualified individual

title: AI agents within the security program (agentic engineering and operations)
target_answer: Echelon discloses that AI agents perform engineering and some operations work. Agents are treated as workload identities under a named human owner; they operate only within repositories and environments whose mandatory rules are enforced by fail-closed gates rather than by prompt instructions; their contributions are attributed by execution identity and reviewed under the same two-approver rules as human changes for control-relevant modules (CNV-PLT-010). Agents never hold production credentials for customer data. Echelon discloses the model providers used in development and in the product, and agent instructions reference the same security rule identifiers as human policy.
intended_practice: Bind agent executions to authenticated workload identities in CI; enforce rules through gates; publish a model-provider disclosure.
owner: Unassigned; proposed CISO with AI governance owner

title: Independent review of the security program and assurance labeling
target_answer: Echelon obtains independent assurance appropriate to customer reliance: a SOC 2 Type 2 (and SOC 1 Type 2 where a sponsor's auditor relies on Unbound controls, per CNV-GOV-001) and periodic independent program assessment. All first-party assessments and automated evidence are labeled first-party and never presented as independent. Customers and their examiners may assess the program under contractual audit rights with reasonable notice.
intended_practice: Plan assurance scope from actual customer reliance; label all internal evidence as first-party.
owner: Unassigned; proposed CISO or qualified individual

title: Contract framework, order of precedence and negotiation authority
target_answer: Echelon offers a counsel-drafted master services agreement with order forms, a security addendum, a data processing addendum and a service level schedule. The signed agreement takes precedence over any online terms, which cannot change the customer's obligations without written amendment. We will review customer paper; deviations from our standard positions are approved by the managing member after counsel review and recorded in a contract exceptions register (BP 14.08), and every accepted obligation is extracted into an obligations register with an owner.
intended_practice: Engage counsel to draft a standard agreement set before the first paid engagement.
owner: Managing member of Echelon Foundry, LLC (role not yet formally assigned)

title: Information security addendum and flow-down of safeguards
target_answer: We sign a security addendum committing to specific, verifiable safeguards rather than only 'reasonable security': encryption in transit and at rest with managed keys (SEC-CRYPTO-001), phishing-resistant MFA for administrative access, deny-by-default authorization with tenant isolation (SEC-AUTH-001), logging and retention periods, vulnerability remediation timelines and secure development rules. We contractually maintain safeguards consistent with the GLBA Safeguards requirements applicable to our customers, flow equivalent obligations down to subcontractors with access to customer data, and accept termination for uncured material security breach.
intended_practice: Draft security addendum aligned to the Secure Construction Standard once adopted.
owner: Managing member of Echelon Foundry, LLC (role not yet formally assigned)

title: Incident and breach notification obligations
target_answer: We commit to notify affected customers without undue delay and in any case within 24 hours of determining that a security incident has affected or is reasonably likely to affect their data or services, and within the shorter of any period required by law applicable to the customer: for bank customers, as soon as possible when an incident has materially disrupted or degraded services for four hours or more (bank service provider notification rule); for SEC-regulated customers, within 72 hours of becoming aware of a breach of customer information (Regulation S-P). Notices state what is known, affected data, actions taken and a contact, and are updated as facts develop. Incident clocks are computed per customer from a register of each customer's notification obligations. We bear the reasonable cost of notification, forensic investigation and credit monitoring caused by our breach.
intended_practice: Build notification obligation register and incident runbook before production.
owner: Managing member of Echelon Foundry, LLC (role not yet formally assigned)

title: Limitation of liability, indemnities and ability to pay
target_answer: Our standard cap is the greater of fees paid in the prior 12 months or a fixed amount, with a higher super-cap for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, set no higher than the insurance limits we actually carry so the commitment is fundable. Fraud, willful misconduct and our IP infringement indemnity are uncapped or separately capped. We indemnify customers against third-party IP infringement claims, including claims arising from code produced with AI tools, and against third-party claims and regulatory penalties arising from our breach where legally insurable and permissible. Loss of or corruption of customer data caused by our breach is treated as direct damages. We disclose our insurance limits so customers can judge whether the cap is backed.
intended_practice: Set caps after insurance is placed; align with LEG-004 control.
owner: Managing member of Echelon Foundry, LLC (role not yet formally assigned)

title: Data protection terms: DPA, service provider terms, location, deletion and legal hold
target_answer: We sign a DPA that meets GDPR Article 28 where EU personal data is processed and that includes CCPA service provider terms (use only for the specified business purposes, no sale or sharing, no combining with other data) for US customers. Data is hosted and supported in the United States unless the customer agrees otherwise, and any transfer uses a recognized mechanism. At termination we return data in an open format and delete it, including from backups on their normal expiry, within a stated period, and certify deletion in writing. Legal hold notices from customers suspend deletion for the identified scope and are acknowledged.
intended_practice: DPA template drafted with counsel; deletion and legal hold supported by Unbound data lifecycle design.
owner: Managing member of Echelon Foundry, LLC (role not yet formally assigned)

title: Termination, transition assistance, assignment and subcontracting
target_answer: Customers may terminate for convenience on notice, for cause, on our change of control, on our insolvency and when directed by their regulator, without penalty in the last three cases. On any termination we provide transition assistance for up to 12 months at contracted rates, including full data export, continued operation during migration and cooperation with the successor. We may not assign the agreement without consent except to a successor that assumes all obligations, with notice and a customer termination right. New subcontractors with access to customer data are notified 30 days in advance through the subprocessor register, and customers may object and terminate if the objection cannot be resolved.
intended_practice: Include in standard agreement.
owner: Managing member of Echelon Foundry, LLC (role not yet formally assigned)

title: Litigation, claims history and compliance representations
target_answer: We provide an annual officer's certificate disclosing pending or threatened litigation, regulatory investigations, judgments and claims relating to data breach, IP or professional negligence against the company and its principals, and update it within 30 days of a new material matter. We represent compliance with anti-bribery, sanctions and anti-corruption laws and accept the customer's vendor code of conduct where consistent with law.
intended_practice: Prepare disclosure certificate template; run court records search before first contract.
owner: Managing member of Echelon Foundry, LLC (role not yet formally assigned)

title: Governing law, dispute resolution, notices and service level remedies
target_answer: We propose Indiana law and venue but accept the customer's home state law for regulated customers where counsel finds no material issue. Disputes follow executive escalation then mediation before litigation, except for injunctive relief. Legal notices go to the registered legal address and a monitored legal mailbox, with a second named recipient so that notices are received when the principal is unavailable. Service levels for availability and support response carry service credits, which are not the sole remedy for chronic failure, and chronic failure gives a termination right.
intended_practice: Include in standard agreement once entity address and registered agent are set.
owner: Managing member of Echelon Foundry, LLC (role not yet formally assigned)

title: Contract terms for AI use, automated decisions and model change
target_answer: The agreement discloses where AI systems are used in delivering the service, commits that AI agents only recommend or prepare and that consequential decisions (grant approval, payment release, fund changes) are made by authorized humans or by deterministic policies the customer's board has adopted, prohibits training on customer data (see IPR), and requires notice before changing AI model providers that process customer data. Where a customer's use falls within state or EU AI laws, we support its compliance obligations.
intended_practice: Draft AI addendum aligned to Unbound requirements.
owner: Managing member of Echelon Foundry, LLC (role not yet formally assigned)

title: Security event logging scope and content
target_answer: Unbound emits a versioned catalog of security events covering authentication, MFA changes, authorization denials, privilege and role changes, reads and exports of sensitive data, configuration and integration changes, administrative and break-glass actions, database-level activity outside the application and AI agent actions. Each record carries actor, authority used, action, resource, decision, result, occurredAt and recordedAt, correlation id and policy version. Automated tests prove every catalog event is emitted.
intended_practice: Implement the event catalog in Unbound's governed APIs and persistence layer.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)

title: Log integrity and tamper evidence
target_answer: Authoritative audit history is append-only below the application API; update and delete are denied to all application, administrator and agent roles; logs are stored in a separate trust domain; hash chains or signed checkpoints are verified daily and after any restore; customers and auditors can verify exported trails independently; access to logs is itself logged.
intended_practice: Benchmark the integrity mechanism and verify Strata and PostgreSQL permission model.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)

title: Log retention and privacy-aware logging
target_answer: Security logs are retained at least 12 months online-searchable and longer in archive per a counsel-approved schedule by log class, with tenant-specific extension and legal hold; typed log schemas exclude secrets and restrict personal data at emission; personal data in append-only logs is handled by field-level redaction or key destruction so lawful deletion is possible.
intended_practice: Set retention schedule with counsel and auditor (SOC2-023).
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)

title: SIEM, alerting, after-hours coverage and response
target_answer: Security events are centralized in an analysis platform with correlation across API, agent, persistence and cloud control plane sources; high-severity alerts page an on-call responder 24x7 with a 15-minute acknowledgment target; pre-approved automated protective actions (account disablement, agent credential revocation, tenant payment hold under the sponsor-adopted hold policy) execute on high-confidence signals; detection and response times are measured and reported.
intended_practice: Select a monitoring platform and staffing model before production.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)

title: Detection engineering
target_answer: Detections are maintained as versioned code mapped to MITRE ATT&CK and to domain abuse cases (payee change followed by disbursement request, unusual grant velocity, bulk export, cross-tenant probing, account takeover indicators, agent scope violations); each detection is tested with seeded events on change and monthly; false positive rates are tracked.
intended_practice: Build the detection catalog alongside the event catalog.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)

title: Customer administrator audit trail
target_answer: Customer administrators can view, search, export and stream (near real time, in a documented JSON schema) all audit events for their tenant, including actions by Echelon personnel, support and break-glass sessions; tenant-visible logs are retained for the contract term plus an agreed period and are exportable at termination; integrity proofs let the customer verify completeness independently; events are tenant-scoped so no tenant can see another's events.
intended_practice: Implement with the event catalog and tenant isolation model.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)

title: Missing heartbeat and log pipeline failure detection
target_answer: An independent expectation engine schedules expected evidence by control, source and period; missing or late sources raise preserved deficiencies within one hour; monitoring failure is a degraded-assurance incident; consequential grant and payment actions follow sponsor-approved fail-closed or manual-continuity policies while safety-critical monitoring is down; zero activity requires validated zero-activity evidence.
intended_practice: Implement per the continuous control monitoring architecture.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)

title: AI agent activity logging and scope monitoring
target_answer: Every AI agent action in engineering and operations is attributable to a distinct agent identity, model and version, authorizing human or policy, and task; tool invocations and results are logged with classification-based redaction of prompts and outputs; out-of-scope actions are denied, logged and alerted, and agents can be interrupted with a kill switch.
intended_practice: Extend to Unbound runtime agents per SOC2-017.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)

title: Time synchronization
target_answer: All components synchronize to the hosting provider's authoritative time service; offsets are monitored and alert beyond 100 ms; records use UTC with millisecond precision and carry both occurredAt and recordedAt.
intended_practice: Configure with hosting selection.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)

title: Privileged, break-glass and pipeline monitoring
target_answer: Break-glass and privileged production access are recorded at session level, page the security owner, notify affected tenant administrators within 1 hour and are reviewed after each use; changes to CI workflows, deploy credentials and signing keys are alerted and reviewed.
intended_practice: Implement with identity platform selection.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)

title: Network architecture, segmentation and tenant cell isolation
target_answer: Unbound runs as one deployable component monolith (REQ-X-020) per deployment cell. Each cell has three network zones defined in infrastructure as code: a public edge zone that only terminates client traffic, a private application zone with no inbound route from the internet, and a private data zone holding managed PostgreSQL that accepts connections only from that cell's application identities. Production, non-production and security logging environments live in separate cloud accounts with no network path between production and non-production. Dedicated-infrastructure tenants (isolation profile C) receive their own cell and network. Segmentation is enforced by policy-as-code checks that fail the release if any data-tier resource receives a public address or an unapproved route, and an external exposure test after each deployment confirms that only the edge answers.
intended_practice: Define the zone model in infrastructure as code once the provider is selected; make segmentation a release gate rather than a review item.
owner: unassigned

title: Public ingress control and web application firewall
target_answer: All client and partner traffic enters through one managed edge per environment. The edge accepts only HTTPS on 443, enforces the TLS policy in ECTL-ENC-002, and forwards to the application zone over re-encrypted connections. A managed WAF runs in blocking mode with a maintained rule set and Unbound-specific rules for API schema size limits; findings are logged to the security log account. Because Unbound is F# with Strata-only database access (SEC-DB-001), no user-supplied HTML (SEC-UI-001) and no application JavaScript outside Limen (SEC-UI-002), the WAF is a defense-in-depth and virtual-patching layer, not the primary control for injection or XSS. Every exposed hostname and port is declared in a reviewed ingress register; the post-deployment exposure test fails the release on any undeclared listener.
intended_practice: Select an edge and WAF capability with the hosting decision; register ingress declaratively; run WAF in detect mode during pre-production testing, then blocking mode before first customer.
owner: unassigned

title: Egress control and outbound connection allowlisting
target_answer: Production workloads have no default route to the internet. Outbound traffic leaves only through a controlled egress point that permits a reviewed allowlist of destinations: payment and banking providers, custodians, charity data sources, identity provider, email delivery, AI model endpoints approved for the tenant, and cloud service endpoints (preferably via private endpoints). At the application layer, outbound calls are only possible through registered provider adapters that bind each external host to a named integration (UNB-CUST-017), so a server-side request forgery cannot target arbitrary hosts or the cloud metadata service. Denied egress attempts are logged and alerted. AI agents operating on production data inherit the same egress policy and cannot add destinations.
intended_practice: Specify the egress allowlist as data with an owner per entry; generate it from the provider adapter registry so the network rule and the code integration stay in sync.
owner: unassigned

title: Denial-of-service resilience and rate limiting
target_answer: Volumetric and protocol attacks are absorbed by the cloud provider's or edge provider's DDoS protection in front of the single ingress. Application-layer abuse is controlled by per-principal, per-tenant and per-endpoint rate limits enforced at the edge and again in the application for expensive operations (search, statement generation, AI-assisted features). Payment and grant submissions are idempotent (UNB-IMM-006), so retries under load cannot duplicate money movement, and the system fails closed for authoritative financial writes when it cannot commit safely (REQ-X-006). DDoS response steps are part of the incident runbook and exercised once a year.
intended_practice: Choose a DDoS-protected edge with the hosting decision; define tenant-fair rate limits so one sponsor's traffic spike cannot starve another (noisy-neighbor test in the persistence design).
owner: unassigned

title: Remote administrative access to production
target_answer: There is no standing network path for administrators. No SSH, RDP or database ports are exposed to the internet or to a corporate VPN. Administrative actions on infrastructure happen through the deployment pipeline. Diagnostic access to a tenant is denied by default, granted per case with sponsor pre-approval, scoped and expiring (CNV-ARC-002), and goes through an identity-aware access broker that requires phishing-resistant MFA from a managed device, records the session and attributes it to a named person. Production database administrative roles are break-glass only with two-person activation (CNV-PLT-010); break-glass credentials are sealed, independent of the workforce IdP, expire within 4 hours and page the security owner (UNB-XIN-IAM-005). AI agents never receive interactive production access.
intended_practice: Select an identity-aware access mechanism with the hosting decision; avoid introducing a VPN unless a provider constraint requires one.
owner: unassigned

title: Zero trust posture and service-to-service authentication
target_answer: Unbound does not rely on network location for trust. Every request is authenticated and authorized server-side inside the command transaction (CNV-PLT-010, SEC-AUTH-001), bound to exactly one VerifiedTenantContext (RR-UNB-PLAT-008-r1). Because Unbound is a component monolith (REQ-X-020) rather than microservices, internal east-west traffic is limited to the application, PostgreSQL, the key service and a few managed services; each of those connections uses a workload identity issued by the platform (no shared static passwords), TLS with certificate verification (ECTL-ENC-003), and least-privilege database roles. Device posture and user identity are evaluated for workforce access (END). This maps to the NIST SP 800-207 tenets without requiring a service mesh.
intended_practice: Implement workload identity for database and provider access once the hosting platform is chosen; document how each SP 800-207 tenet is satisfied.
owner: unassigned

title: DNS, domain and certificate authority hygiene
target_answer: All Echelon and Unbound domains are held in one registrar account with registrar lock, phishing-resistant MFA and at least two administrators. DNS zones are managed as code with review; DNSSEC is enabled where the registrar and DNS provider support it; CAA records restrict certificate issuance to the approved certificate authorities; dangling records pointing to released cloud resources are detected daily to prevent subdomain takeover. Workloads use the provider's resolver with query logging, and resolution of unapproved external domains from production is blocked in line with the egress allowlist. Domain expiry and certificate expiry are monitored.
intended_practice: Inventory domains, move them to a managed registrar account, and put zones under code review.
owner: unassigned

title: TLS termination points and visibility of decrypted traffic
target_answer: TLS from clients terminates at the managed edge, which is operated by the hosting or edge provider and listed as a subservice organization. Traffic from the edge to the application is re-encrypted with TLS and certificate verification; no hop carries donor PII or credentials in cleartext. The set of parties that can observe decrypted request content (edge provider, WAF, the application) is documented in the system description. Bank account numbers and other restricted fields are additionally protected by field-level encryption at the application (ANS-ENC-008), so edge logging cannot capture them in reusable form if request logging is disabled for those paths. Edge request body logging is off by default.
intended_practice: Decide edge provider and whether any CDN that decrypts traffic is acceptable for authenticated donor traffic.
owner: unassigned

title: Network traffic visibility, flow logging and intrusion detection
target_answer: Flow logs are enabled for every network in every production account and delivered to a separate security logging account that production administrators cannot alter. Detection rules alert on denied egress, connections from the application zone to unexpected destinations, database connections from any non-application identity, and traffic to known-malicious addresses using the provider's threat detection service. Missing flow log delivery is itself an alert (SOC2-027). Because most attack traffic to Unbound is encrypted application traffic, network detection complements, and does not replace, application-level security events.
intended_practice: Select provider-native flow logging and threat detection with the hosting decision; route alerts to the incident process.
owner: unassigned

title: Nacha roles: sponsor as Originator, Unbound as Third-Party Service Provider holding no funds
target_answer: Each program records a role table naming the Originator (the sponsor), the ODFI, Third-Party Service Providers (Unbound), any Third-Party Sender or grant-rail partner, and the authorization holder (CNV-PAY-001). By default the sponsor is Originator of record on sponsor-titled accounts under its own ODFI agreement; the platform operator is a Third-Party Service Provider, never a Third-Party Sender, and holds no funds (UNB-XIN-BNK-001). Unbound does not sign an origination agreement, hold or pool donor or grant money, or execute or block a payment on its own authority; any configuration that would do so is rejected, and a funds-flow conformance check blocks activation of any deployment that fails (CNV-PAY-001, CNV-LEG-001, UNB-XIN-REG-001). Unbound accepts TPSP obligations by contract, including Nacha risk-based fraud monitoring, data security and audit cooperation. A versioned RailObligation register maps every binding obligation for each rail and role to a control, and production enablement of any rail must pass a RailGoLive gate (RR-UNB-PAY-008-r1). Outbound payments are deliberately deferred: no rail, bank or provider is selected and no live payment is authorized (PAY-DEF-001 in DEFERRED-PAYMENTS-AND-REMAINING-GAPS.md).
intended_practice: Complete funds-flow legal review and ODFI engagement per sponsor before any rail is enabled; publish the role table to each sponsor's ODFI.
owner: Not assigned; proposed: Unbound payments product owner (role not staffed); the sponsor remains Originator and payment authority

title: ACH debit authorizations, retention, account validation and return-rate monitoring
target_answer: Release 1 does not originate ACH debits from donors; contributions arrive by ACH credit, wire, check, securities transfer or the sponsor's existing processor (CNV-PAY-005). When donor debit origination is enabled, the system captures a signed or similarly authenticated authorization stating amount or range, frequency, start date, debiting entity and revocation method, delivers a copy, gives at least 10 days' notice of out-of-range amounts and honors revocation for entries not yet sent (UNB-XIN-PAY-001). Authorizations are retained for their active life plus two years after termination or revocation and are not deleted while warranty claims may arise (CNV-PAY-005). The first WEB debit to an account, and the first after any change, requires account validation by prenote, micro-entry or a third-party service (UNB-XIN-PAY-002). Rolling 60-day unauthorized, administrative and overall return rates are computed per Originator with alerts at configurable fractions of the Nacha thresholds and automatic suspension above a sponsor hard limit; reinitiation is allowed only for R01 and R09 (and R02 to R04 after correction), at most twice within 180 days, with 'RETRY PYMT' and identical company name, ID and amount (UNB-XIN-PAY-005).
intended_practice: Keep donor debit origination disabled until the RailGoLive gate passes for a sponsor; implement authorization records under a retention class that cannot expire during warranty windows.
owner: Not assigned; proposed: Unbound payments product owner (role not staffed); the sponsor remains Originator and payment authority

title: ACH returns and notifications of change
target_answer: Returns match on original entry trace number, return reason code and return trace; NOCs match on original trace, change code and COR trace. When addenda are missing a fallback match (amount, effective date, company ID, account last four, individual ID) routes to a queue and never auto-posts (CNV-PAY-005). These keys are the registered business idempotency keys, so redelivered files have no second effect (UNB-XIN-EVA-005). NOC corrections apply within six banking days or before the next entry, whichever is later, under change control; a matched bank-originated NOC counts as destination evidence without cooling-off but notifies the charity's verified channels, while any charity-requested change triggered by an NOC follows the full destination-change rule (CNV-PAY-002). Returns are accepted even after a grant is Disbursed or Final where the rail permits (TVR-GR-002); returned grant funds re-credit the originating fund by linked compensating entry, generate no acknowledgment, and restore capacity only after reconciliation (UNB-RCN-GRT-015). Return and NOC matching apply to grant payments from release 1.
intended_practice: Build return and NOC ingestion with deterministic matching, an exception queue and an NOC application timer.
owner: Not assigned; proposed: Unbound payments product owner (role not staffed); the sponsor remains Originator and payment authority

title: Wire transfers, UCC Article 4A security procedures and irrevocable rails
target_answer: Rails are governed by a versioned RailEligibility matrix keyed by payment class, rail and direction, with per-payment and daily limits and an irreversibility class; Irrevocable and RequestOnly rails such as wires require independent destination confirmation for each payment above a threshold, and instant rails default to not allowed for grants until a sponsor enables them (UNB-XIN-BNK-004). Domestic wires are sent with no-deduction instructions and international wires default to OUR charges, with any pass-through disclosed (CNV-PAY-007). Wire outcomes are confirmed by Fedwire IMAD/OMAD and beneficiary-bank confirmation before final aging (CNV-PAY-004). An adverse sanctions or status event on a dispatched but unsettled payment automatically triggers a recall request recorded as externally uncertain (UNB-RCN-GRT-016). Because the sponsor is the bank's customer under Article 4A, the commercially reasonable security procedure is agreed between the sponsor and its bank; Unbound's role is to deliver only independently approved instructions through an authenticated channel the sponsor's bank recognizes.
intended_practice: Document, per sponsor, how Unbound-delivered wire instructions interact with the sponsor's Article 4A security procedure, and keep account-number and beneficiary-name consistency checks before release.
owner: Not assigned; proposed: Unbound payments product owner (role not staffed); the sponsor remains Originator and payment authority

title: Check issuance, void handling, stale dating and reissue
target_answer: The check rail models Issued, Outstanding, AgedOutreach, StaleDated, VoidRequested, VoidConfirmed, Cleared and UnclaimedPropertyReportable, each with a defined grant, reservation and ledger effect (UNB-RCN-GRT-005). Positive pay with daily issue files including voids is mandatory, and a check is mailed only after the bank acknowledges its issue record (CNV-PAY-002, UNB-XIN-BNK-006). Checks void by default at 90 days, configurable but never later than the shortest applicable state window, with a recorded reason; voiding does not extinguish the grant obligation and does not automatically re-credit the fund (CNV-PAY-002). A reissue requires a confirmed stop or void, verified recipient eligibility and destination, and a linked replacement chain (UNB-RCN-GRT-005, CNV-PAY-004). Every program keeps a check fallback and stored verified destination so charities outside partner networks can be paid (CNV-PAY-001).
intended_practice: Implement the check state machine with void acknowledgment and reissue chain; print and mail through a vendor or the sponsor's bank (not selected).
owner: Not assigned; proposed: Unbound payments product owner (role not staffed); the sponsor remains Originator and payment authority

title: Unclaimed property for uncashed grant and refund checks
target_answer: Unbound maintains a counsel-approved UnclaimedPropertyRule table per state covering owner type, property type, dormancy period, business-to-business or charitable exemption flags, due-diligence notice window and content, and report and remittance dates; the state is determined by the payee's last known address with the sponsor's state of incorporation as fallback per counsel (UNB-XIN-BNK-007). Outstanding uncashed grant checks are presumed reportable property owed to the payee charity; before dormancy the system makes two outreach attempts including an offer to reissue by ACH. Void-and-re-credit to the fund is permitted only if the grant was cancelled before cashing with notice to the charity and the state row records that cancellation defeats the holder obligation. A VoidDisposition record decides re-credit, hold as payable or report; unknown inputs default to Hold and report at dormancy, and business-to-business exemptions default to not applicable to grants (CNV-PAY-003). Items with no applicable rule stay in review and are never re-credited.
intended_practice: Populate state rule rows from statute text starting with states where sponsors concentrate; generate report and remittance data for the sponsor as holder.
owner: Not assigned; proposed: Unbound payments product owner (role not staffed); the sponsor remains Originator and payment authority

title: Payment file security and bank integration authentication
target_answer: Every bank, payment-partner and custodian integration documents its authentication method, credential rotation, least privilege, webhook signature verification, replay defense, partner context binding and outage behavior (UNB-API-STD-005, UNB-CUST-017). Inbound files and callbacks require verifiable origin, freshness, deduplication, ordering and replay protection (UNB-CUST-009, RR-REQ-X-083-r1). Credentials are scoped per sponsor; secrets are never hardcoded and are managed with approved libraries, managed keys, scanning and rotation (SEC-CRYPTO-001). Sandbox tenants are bound to mock adapters and cannot resolve or authenticate to any production bank, payment or custody endpoint, and the simulated adapter never calls a real rail (UNB-XIN-SAS-010, UNB-SCTRL-030). Payment data, including account numbers, is classified and encrypted under the platform data policy (SOC2-014), and Unbound would accept Nacha data security obligations as a TPSP (CNV-PAY-001).
intended_practice: Select per-bank transport (bank API with mutual TLS or signed requests, or SFTP with file-level encryption and signing as the bank supports); keep integration credentials in a managed secret store with per-sponsor scope.
owner: Not assigned; proposed: Unbound payments product owner (role not staffed); the sponsor remains Originator and payment authority

title: Dual control on payment release, limits and no out-of-band origination
target_answer: No grant recommendation, AI proposal or internal journal authorizes outbound funds; release requires sponsor reserved authority, independent release control, payee verification and least privilege (UNB-PAY-003). Until a deterministic release gate is accepted by the sponsor's auditor and board, release requires three distinct people (CNV-GOV-003). Approvals are checked against delegation-of-authority limits, and rail eligibility carries per-payment and daily limits (UNB-XIN-ERP-005, UNB-XIN-BNK-004). A batch carries no approval or release authority itself; each item is released and re-checked against holds immediately before transmission (UNB-XIN-EVA-011, CNV-ARC-003). No payment may originate outside the platform gate, manual fallback runs through the gate with dual control, and bank portal entitlements give no unilateral release rights outside it (TVR-PAY-004). When bank feeds are stale, releases of already-reserved grants may proceed only on a balance attestation by two treasury staff distinct from the releasing approvers, valid one business day (CNV-PAY-007). Any platform hold leaves the sponsor able to pay through its own bank channel (CNV-PLT-007).
intended_practice: Implement the release gate with distinct-person enforcement and limit checks; document each sponsor's bank portal entitlement configuration and review it quarterly.
owner: Not assigned; proposed: Unbound payments product owner (role not staffed); the sponsor remains Originator and payment authority

title: Independent penetration testing: existence, frequency and triggers
target_answer: An independent, accredited firm tests Unbound before any customer production data is loaded, at least every 12 months thereafter, and after material changes (new hosting, authentication redesign, new payment or custodian integration, new AI agent authority). Results are shared as a letter of attestation and, under NDA, the full report.
intended_practice: Engage an accredited firm and complete an architecture-informed test before the first customer production data load.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)

title: Penetration test scope and methodology
target_answer: Scope covers external attack surface, web application and APIs, every user and administrative role, cross-tenant access attempts, business logic of grant approval, payee change, disbursement and fee workflows, the Limen browser boundary, Strata-backed data access, AI agent interfaces and tool authority, cloud configuration, assumed-breach internal perspective (compromised workforce, CI or agent credential) and environment segregation. Testing is architecture-informed with explicit objectives to bypass claimed structural controls. Methodology references OWASP WSTG, NIST SP 800-115 and PTES.
intended_practice: Define scope and rules of engagement during firm selection.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)

title: Tester qualifications, firm accreditation and independence
target_answer: Testing is performed by a firm independent of Echelon engineering, holding a recognized accreditation such as CREST (or NCSC CHECK where a UK customer requires it), with testers holding certifications such as OSCP or GIAC GPEN or GWAPT and demonstrable web and API testing experience; testers are under confidentiality, background-checked by their firm, and do not access real customer data. Firms or lead testers rotate at least every three engagements.
intended_practice: Apply these criteria in firm selection.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)

title: Sharing penetration test reports and letters of attestation
target_answer: Prospects receive a letter of attestation under NDA; customers, their auditors and regulators may review the full report under NDA in a controlled viewer; all first-party assessment material is labeled first-party and distinguished from independent tests.
intended_practice: Adopt sharing terms in the security addendum.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)

title: Remediation and retest of penetration test findings
target_answer: Findings enter the vulnerability register under VUL SLAs; each fix adds a regression test or structural change preventing recurrence of the class; the testing firm retests and issues an updated letter showing remediation status.
intended_practice: Implement with the vulnerability register.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)

title: Customer-initiated penetration testing rights
target_answer: Customers may test a dedicated tenant seeded with synthetic data, at no charge, with 10 business days' notice, under published rules of engagement that exclude denial-of-service and social engineering of Echelon staff, and that respect hosting provider policies; findings are triaged under VUL SLAs and results shared back with the customer.
intended_practice: Define in the security addendum once a test tenant capability exists.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)

title: First-party continuous adversarial testing between independent tests
target_answer: Every release runs adversarial, negative and property-based tests of financial invariants, authorization and tenant isolation, authored independently of the code author, with results recorded as first-party evidence and made available for sampling by independent testers and auditors.
intended_practice: Apply Tutela and Praxis gates to Unbound once implementation begins.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)

title: Threat-led and red team testing, including regulator-mandated programs
target_answer: If an EU financial entity designates Unbound as supporting a critical or important function, Echelon will participate in its threat-led penetration testing under DORA on agreed terms; red team exercises covering social engineering and supply chain are considered after production maturity.
intended_practice: Revisit if EU or UK financial customers are pursued.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)

title: Reliance on cloud provider data centers and shared responsibility
target_answer: Echelon operates no data centers or server rooms. Customer data is hosted with a major cloud provider in United States regions, including backups and disaster recovery copies, enforced by infrastructure-as-code region pinning and an organization policy that denies resource creation elsewhere. Production spans multiple availability zones, with a documented regional recovery approach. Physical and environmental controls are inherited from the provider and evidenced by its SOC 2 Type II and ISO/IEC 27001 reports, which we review annually, mapping provider complementary user entity controls to our own controls. We publish the shared responsibility split.
intended_practice: Select provider and regions as part of Unbound deployment architecture.
owner: Managing member of Echelon Foundry, LLC (role not yet formally assigned)

title: Offices, physical records and on-premises processing
target_answer: Echelon has no office that stores or processes customer data; any office or coworking space is used for work on company-managed devices only. No customer data is stored on local servers. Paper records with customer information are not created; if received, they are digitized to the controlled system and cross-cut shredded, with the disposal recorded.
intended_practice: Adopt a no-paper, no-local-server rule.
owner: Managing member of Echelon Foundry, LLC (role not yet formally assigned)

title: Remote work security
target_answer: All work is remote by design. Customer data is accessed only inside managed cloud environments through phishing-resistant authentication from company-managed devices; it is not stored on endpoints. Remote workers follow a remote work standard covering private workspace, screen privacy, home network hygiene and use of trusted networks or the company VPN or zero-trust access path. Access from outside approved jurisdictions is blocked by conditional access.
intended_practice: Adopt remote work standard and conditional access.
owner: Managing member of Echelon Foundry, LLC (role not yet formally assigned)

title: Endpoints, authenticators and media sanitization
target_answer: Only company-managed endpoints with full-disk encryption, automatic updates, screen lock, endpoint protection and remote wipe may access company systems, enforced by device posture checks at sign-in; personal devices are not permitted for administrative or customer-data access. Lost or stolen devices are reported within 24 hours and wiped. Administrative accounts require hardware-backed phishing-resistant authenticators, with registered backup authenticators held separately so loss of one key does not lock out or force weaker recovery. Retired devices and media are sanitized per NIST SP 800-88 with a certificate.
intended_practice: Adopt device management and authenticator standard.
owner: Managing member of Echelon Foundry, LLC (role not yet formally assigned)

title: Physical concentration risk of a small, co-located team
target_answer: We document where personnel are located and plan for a regional event that disables all of them: at least two people able to perform critical operations from different regions or a contracted backup operator, no critical operation that depends on a single physical device or location (backup authenticators and credential custody held separately), and the ability to operate from any managed device with internet access. Any equipment we operate ourselves has power, fire and flood protection appropriate to its role, though the target is to operate none. We explain to customers that a site inspection adds little for a cloud-hosted service and offer provider reports and configuration evidence instead, while permitting an inspection on request.
intended_practice: Document locations and backup operator arrangements in continuity plan.
owner: Managing member of Echelon Foundry, LLC (role not yet formally assigned)

title: Capacity planning and tenant resource isolation
target_answer: Capacity is planned from documented volume drivers (accounts per sponsor, activity segments, grant volume, document generation, AI-assisted case volume) and monitored against benchmarked sustainable capacity of the largest sponsor database; action is taken before peak commit rate reaches 50 percent of that capacity. Each sponsor has its own database by default, and quotas bound connections, API rates, fan-out and agent usage per tenant so no tenant can degrade another. When demand exceeds capacity, the system applies backpressure and queues deferrable work rather than failing, and never queues approvals or payments in a way that bypasses revalidation.
intended_practice: Build the capacity model alongside the first load test.
owner: Proposed: SRE Lead (role not yet staffed)

title: Load testing and peak-event readiness
target_answer: Load tests on the selected managed PostgreSQL model the year-end peak of the largest expected sponsor at ten times normal grant volume, plus historical replay and projection rebuild at production scale, and run as a release gate for high-volume paths. Year-end readiness includes a documented plan, conjunction drills (surge plus market plus provider plus regulatory change) and a staffing surge playbook. Results with thresholds and pass/fail are shared under NDA.
intended_practice: Run the first surge benchmark before choosing to add any second store or broker, as UNB-XIN-EVA-013 requires.
owner: Proposed: SRE Lead (role not yet staffed)

title: Performance service levels and reporting
target_answer: Echelon publishes performance SLOs per capability (for example interactive page response and command acknowledgment at the 95th percentile on mid-range phones over constrained networks, and maximum time from approval to payment file generation), measured with real-user monitoring segmented by device and network class and by server metrics, and reports them monthly per tenant. Performance SLOs are published only after a measured baseline exists.
intended_practice: Establish baselines in a production-like environment before offering performance commitments.
owner: Proposed: SRE Lead (role not yet staffed)

title: Batch windows and processing deadlines
target_answer: Batch work (payment file generation, reconciliation, statements, year-end acknowledgments) is scheduled against rail cut-offs and business deadlines and isolated from interactive load, so batches do not cause online slowdowns. Requests approved before a published internal cut-off are included in the next rail submission, with alerts raised before a deadline is at risk. Year-end acknowledgment and statement generation are capacity-tested for full-volume completion well before donors need them for tax filing, and Folio rendering throughput is measured before Folio is relied on for statements.
intended_practice: Define cut-off schedules per rail with the payments component; measure document throughput in a rendering spike.
owner: Proposed: Unbound payments owner

title: Export formats, documented schema and self-service export
target_answer: Customers can, without Echelon involvement, export their complete tenant dataset as versioned, documented open formats: JSON Lines or Parquet for records and events with a published JSON Schema per record type, CSV views for common tables, original-format documents with a manifest, and PDF/A renderings of statements and letters. The export schema is versioned with change notes and backward-compatibility rules, and the same schema is published to prospects before contract.
intended_practice: Specify the logical export schema alongside the domain model; build self-service export early, since it also serves backup verification and migration.
owner: Product owner, Unbound (proposed role; not appointed)

title: Export completeness: full history, audit trail, decisions and vendor-generated records
target_answer: The export contains everything the sponsor needs to continue operating and defend past decisions: the full append-only event history including corrections and reversals, current and historical balances and unit values, all grants with approvals, reviewer rationale, eligibility and sanctions screening snapshots, policy versions in force, overrides with authority, payment instructions and confirmations, communications, documents, consents and preferences, AI agent recommendations and the human decisions on them, and audit logs. Each export carries a manifest with record counts, control totals and hashes so the customer can verify completeness and reconcile balances independently. Exports are strictly tenant-scoped.
intended_practice: Define completeness as the full event stream plus documents; contractually commit that vendor-generated records are customer data for export purposes.
owner: Product owner, Unbound (proposed role; not appointed)

title: APIs and bulk programmatic access for data retrieval
target_answer: Customers have documented APIs to retrieve all data incrementally (by event sequence) and in bulk, with rate limits that permit a full extraction within a defined window, and no extraction fees. API access for export continues through the termination assistance period even after other access ends.
intended_practice: Design an incremental event-feed API from the start; set extraction-grade rate limits for export endpoints.
owner: Product owner, Unbound (proposed role; not appointed)

title: Migration assistance into and out of the platform
target_answer: Echelon runs migrations in both directions with the same method: a governed plan, a consistent cutover point, verifiable source and destination equivalence, independent ledger reconciliation, mapping tables for fund, grant and party identifiers, and a reconciliation report signed off by the sponsor. Parallel run is supported for a defined period without two authoritative writers. Outbound migration assistance is priced in advance in the contract.
intended_practice: Build the inbound importer first (it is required to win customers) and reuse it as the specification for outbound assistance.
owner: Product owner, Unbound (proposed role; not appointed)

title: Interoperability with other DAF platforms, grant networks and donor-level portability
target_answer: Echelon publishes its export and interchange schemas openly under a license that lets customers and competing platforms implement them, supports exchange with networked grant-payment partners in their published formats, and gives donors a portable statement of their fund history when a fund transfers to another sponsor. Contracts do not restrict customers from sharing schemas or exports with competing vendors.
intended_practice: Survey whether any DAF data interchange standard exists; publish the Unbound export schema.
owner: Product owner, Unbound (proposed role; not appointed)

title: Privacy program governance, accountable owner, inventory and notice
target_answer: Echelon operates a written privacy program owned by a named Privacy Officer who reports to the managing member at least quarterly. A machine-readable record of processing is generated from the Strata schema catalog, in which every column carries a data category and purpose tag, so the inventory cannot drift from the deployed schema. The platform privacy notice is versioned in Praxis-governed records, and privacy training is role-based and tracked. Program effectiveness is examined in a SOC 2 Type II report that includes the Privacy or Confidentiality criteria once the service is in production.
intended_practice: Adopt a privacy program before the first customer contract; derive the processing inventory from schema metadata; scope Privacy criteria into the first SOC 2 examination if customers require it.
owner: Managing member (interim) until a Privacy Officer is appointed

title: Processing role (processor, service provider) and applicability of CCPA/CPRA and state privacy laws
target_answer: For the Unbound service Echelon acts only as a processor, service provider or contractor on the sponsor's documented instructions. Echelon's own uses are limited to an enumerated list (security, fraud prevention, debugging, service improvement without cross-customer data combination) that the contract names. The DPA carries the CCPA service-provider terms where the customer is a covered business, and the equivalent processor terms required by state laws that cover nonprofits (for example Colorado and Oregon). Role determinations per data flow are recorded and reviewed by counsel.
intended_practice: Commission a counsel memo on Echelon's role by customer type (nonprofit sponsor, bank, RIA, broker-dealer, for-profit partner) and adopt a DPA that satisfies the strictest applicable regime.
owner: Privacy Officer (proposed role; not appointed)

title: GLBA, Regulation P, Safeguards Rule and Regulation S-P obligations flowing to Echelon
target_answer: Echelon treats donor financial data as if it were nonpublic personal information regardless of the unsettled GLBA status of a particular sponsor, so one control set serves banks, RIAs, broker-dealers and nonprofit sponsors. It accepts service-provider safeguards terms that bank customers need under the Interagency Guidelines, notifies covered institutions under amended Regulation S-P of a breach of customer information no later than 72 hours after becoming aware of it, limits reuse and redisclosure of NPI to the purposes for which it was received, and maintains a written information security program meeting the FTC Safeguards Rule elements whether or not Echelon is itself determined to be a financial institution.
intended_practice: Obtain counsel analysis per customer type; adopt the Safeguards Rule element set as the internal baseline; build a 72-hour customer notification runbook.
owner: Privacy Officer (proposed role; not appointed)

title: Data processing agreement terms: subprocessors, instructions, audit and flow-down
target_answer: Echelon offers a standard DPA before contract that covers processing on documented instructions, confidentiality, security measures, subprocessor authorization with advance notice and a right to object, assistance with rights requests and assessments, breach notification, return and deletion at end of service, and audit rights satisfied first by independent reports and, where required, by on-site or remote audit. A machine-readable subprocessor register (including AI model providers) is published with change history, and every subprocessor contract carries equivalent obligations.
intended_practice: Draft a DPA meeting GDPR Article 28 and CCPA service-provider requirements as the strictest common denominator; publish a versioned subprocessor register.
owner: Privacy Officer (proposed role; not appointed)

title: Data subject rights handling and the append-only record conflict
target_answer: Rights requests reach the sponsor, which decides; Echelon provides tooling that locates every record about a person across funds, successor and joint-advisor relationships, events, documents, logs and exports, and executes the decision within contractual timelines. Deletion is fulfilled by erasing the person's entry in a segregated encrypted identity vault (cryptographic erasure of the per-person key) while legally required financial records remain with pseudonymous references, and the customer receives a statement of exactly what was erased and what was retained and why. Requests reaching Echelon directly are forwarded to the sponsor within two business days.
intended_practice: Build identity vault and per-person key design (UNB-DATA-007) before first production data; define rights workflow with sponsor decision step.
owner: Privacy Officer (proposed role; not appointed)

title: No sale, sharing, advertising use or monetization of customer data
target_answer: Echelon does not sell or share customer personal data, does not use it for targeted or cross-context behavioral advertising, receives no third-party compensation tied to donor data, and does not create cross-customer benchmarks or data products from customer data. Any aggregate statistics are produced only with written sponsor opt-in and a published de-identification method. The platform has no advertising or data-broker integrations, which is checkable from the egress allowlist and subprocessor register.
intended_practice: Commit in contract and design; enforce cross-tenant prohibitions under UNB-TEN-007.
owner: Privacy Officer (proposed role; not appointed)

title: Data location, residency and international transfers
target_answer: All Unbound production data, backups and AI inference run in United States regions of named providers, and support or engineering access, including by AI agents, originates from approved US locations and is logged with origin. A residency commitment is enforced by infrastructure policy that rejects resources outside approved regions. Where personal data of EU or UK residents is processed (for example donors living abroad or foreign grantee signatories), Echelon offers the 2021 SCCs (Module 2 or 3) and the UK addendum, with a transfer impact assessment; Echelon does not currently claim Data Privacy Framework certification.
intended_practice: Select US regions; encode region restrictions as deploy-time policy; decide whether DPF certification is worth its cost given expected EU data volume.
owner: Engineering lead (proposed role)

title: Privacy by design, privacy impact assessment and production data in development
target_answer: Every change that introduces a data category, external API, AI agent permission or financial workflow requires a recorded privacy impact assessment linked to the change in Praxis; the release gate blocks merges that touch tagged schema elements without a linked assessment. Defaults favor privacy: donor names hidden from grantees unless chosen, minimal fields visible to charities and partners. Production personal data is never used in development or by AI coding agents; synthetic data is generated from schema definitions.
intended_practice: Define the PIA template and gate; build synthetic data generation from schema.
owner: Privacy Officer (proposed role; not appointed)

title: Cookies, tracking technologies and third-party scripts in donor portals
target_answer: Donor, advisor and charity portals load no third-party scripts, advertising pixels, session replay or cross-site trackers. Only strictly necessary first-party cookies for authentication and security are set, so no consent banner is needed in most US states; any optional first-party analytics is aggregate, cookieless and server-side. Content Security Policy forbids third-party script origins, and a CI check fails the build when one is introduced. Identifiers never appear in URLs.
intended_practice: Adopt a no-third-party-script rule enforced by CSP and CI; document the cookie inventory.
owner: Engineering lead (proposed role)

title: Children's and minors' data
target_answer: The service is not directed to children and does not permit accounts for users under 18. Minors named as successors or beneficiaries are recorded with the minimum data needed (name and relationship), visible only to the sponsor and the advising donor, and cannot log in until they reach majority and are verified. Any future youth philanthropy feature requires a PIA and counsel review against COPPA and state minors' privacy laws before design.
intended_practice: Add an explicit requirement for minors in succession records; decide whether any youth feature is in scope.
owner: Privacy Officer (proposed role; not appointed)

title: Use of customer data for AI training, model providers and AI agent access
target_answer: Echelon does not use customer data to train, fine-tune or evaluate models, and contracts with model providers prohibit training on and retention of prompts and outputs beyond the minimum needed for abuse monitoring, with zero-retention options used where available. AI agents performing engineering and operations work have no standing access to production customer data; any access is break-glass, purpose-declared, scoped to one tenant and logged. Customers can disable all AI processing of their tenant's data, which is enforced in the authorization layer rather than by configuration of individual features.
intended_practice: Write the no-training commitment into the DPA; select model providers with contractual no-training and limited retention; implement tenant AI opt-out in authorization.
owner: AI governance owner (proposed role)

title: De-identification and aggregation standards
target_answer: Any de-identified or aggregate output meets a documented standard: minimum cohort sizes and suppression appropriate to small DAF populations, removal of rare grant combinations, and, where statistical release is frequent, formal privacy methods. Echelon publicly commits not to re-identify, contractually binds recipients not to re-identify, and keeps de-identified sets technically separate. Support artifacts and AI evaluation sets are built from synthetic data, not de-identified production data.
intended_practice: Define aggregate reporting rules under UNB-GAP-017 before any reporting feature.
owner: Privacy Officer (proposed role; not appointed)

title: Reconciliation scope, sources and cadence (bank, custodian, payment rail, subledger, GL)
target_answer: Unbound is designed to reconcile continuously, not only at month end. Every authoritative balance has an independent external counterpart: sponsor-owned bank accounts (BAI2/BTRS and ISO 20022 camt.052/053/054 feeds, prior-day mandatory) to the cash subledger; custodian positions, cash and transactions to the investment subledger per security and per custody account; payment-rail settlement and returns to grants payable; and the sum of fund-level balances to the sponsor GL control accounts by entity, fund, restriction and currency. Where the sponsor's GL is kept in an external book of record, Unbound reconciles to it and is never a second authoritative book. Exact matches auto-pass, residual items route to an exception queue, and spendable capacity is derived from internal reservations against the last verified balance, never from a feed balance alone; releases fail closed when feeds are stale beyond the approved window. Because Unbound holds no donor money (CNV-LEG-001), all cash reconciled is in sponsor-owned accounts.

title: Matching rules, tolerances and auto-clear governance
target_answer: Match rules and tolerances are versioned policy objects. Tolerances are absolute and relative per source, currency and asset class, calibrated from observed feeds. A new source starts in ProvisionalCalibration: exact match only, every non-exact item to human review and 100 percent review for at least one full close cycle of parallel run, after which the controller approves tolerances. Differences are classified against RoundingTolerance (auto-clear with evidence), Materiality and AgingLimit thresholds; loosening any threshold requires a second approver. There are no balancing plugs or silent write-offs. External observations carry registered business idempotency keys so duplicates cannot match twice. AI may propose a match or explanation but cannot apply a manual match, change a tolerance or approve its own proposal.

title: Break management: ownership, aging, escalation and fund impact
target_answer: Every unmatched item becomes a break case with owner, fund attribution, amount, age and evidence. Breaks above Materiality block close certification, NAV publication and new reservations for the affected scope only; immaterial unexplained differences escalate when the AgingLimit expires regardless of amount. A break is attributed to funds through its unmatched items; an unattributable break opens a controller decision due within a sponsor-set number of business days to either publish affected statements marked provisional (reconciliation pending) or withhold them. Breaks found after close open a post-close adjustment case that preserves the original close package. Break counts, aging and materiality are reported to the sponsor.

title: Segregation of duties and independence of reconciliation from payment initiation

title: Deletion and media sanitization in a cloud service
target_answer: Logical deletion is completed by cryptographic erasure of per-tenant and per-person keys, which NIST SP 800-88 recognizes as a sanitization technique when keys are strong and fully destroyed. Physical media sanitization is the hosting provider's responsibility, covered by its independent attestation that Echelon reviews annually. Endpoints that may hold customer data are full-disk encrypted and sanitized by crypto erase plus device reset on retirement. Deletion completes in primary systems within 30 days of the triggering event and in backups by expiry (see ANS-RET-004).
intended_practice: Select provider and key service; document the sanitization approach per storage type.
