title: Deletion from backups
target_answer: Backups are encrypted under per-tenant keys and expire on a fixed, published cycle (for example 35 days). Deleted data is not surgically removed from backups but becomes unrecoverable when the tenant or person key is destroyed or when the backup expires, whichever is first. If a backup is restored, a replay of erasure and disposition events runs before the restored data is served, so previously deleted records are not reinstated.
intended_practice: Define backup retention; implement post-restore erasure replay and test it in the annual restore test.

title: Append-only ledgers and audit logs versus deletion obligations
target_answer: Authoritative events and audit records hold pseudonymous references and ciphertext for personal fields, never plaintext identifiers. Erasure destroys the relevant key; the event chain stays intact because integrity hashes are computed over ciphertext; projections, search indexes and caches are rebuilt and lose the erased values. Echelon reports exactly which classes of personal data remain in retained records (for example pseudonymous fund IDs and amounts) and the legal basis for retaining them.
intended_practice: Decide the hash-over-ciphertext design and the rebuild procedure before the first event schema is frozen.

title: OFAC blocked property and rejected transaction reporting

title: Unclaimed property reporting for uncashed grants and dormant accounts

Outstanding uncashed grant checks are presumed reportable property owed to the payee charity. The reporting state is the payee's last known address state, else the sponsor's state of incorporation (fixed rule XID-BNK-003). A counsel-approved, statute-derived UnclaimedPropertyRule table per state gives dormancy period, exemptions, due-diligence notice window and content, and report and remittance dates. Two outreach attempts, including an offer to reissue by ACH, precede dormancy. Void and re-credit to the fund is permitted only if the grant was cancelled before cashing with notice to the charity and the state rule allows; an item with no rule row stays in review and is never re-credited. Unknown inputs default to hold and report at dormancy. Dormant DAF accounts follow a sponsor dormancy policy with charitable default disposition; escheat processing is limited to payment instruments unless counsel records otherwise.

Reports are reproducible exactly as filed. Audit adjustments post only in a period 13 linked to audit findings. Preparation, review and sign-off are separate principals and AI cannot sign or file. Package integrity is verified before release. None of this replaces the sponsor's external audit or an independent SOC report, which do not yet exist for Unbound.

title: Enterprise and security risk management framework and method
target_answer: Our risk method follows ISO/IEC 27005-style assessment within an ISO/IEC 27001 and NIST CSF 2.0 structure: assets, threats, vulnerabilities, likelihood and impact are scored on a documented scale, including fraud and AI-agent misuse scenarios. A full assessment runs at least annually and is re-run on defined triggers (new data category, new integration, new autonomous permission, material incident, new regulated customer type). Threat models produced with Tutela for each product feed the enterprise register. The managing member owns the process; an independent advisor reviews results.
intended_practice: Adopt method and perform first assessment before first production customer.
owner: Managing member of Echelon Foundry, LLC (role not yet formally assigned)

title: Risk register, treatment tracking and effectiveness
target_answer: We maintain a machine-readable risk register in which each risk has an owner, inherent and residual rating, treatment decision, linked controls (ECTL-, UNB-CTRL-) and linked evidence requirements. Treatment actions have due dates; overdue actions raise an exception automatically. Effectiveness is judged from control evidence and incident data, not from completion of tasks. Risks arising from our own size and stage (key-person dependence, limited runway, customer concentration) are in the register and summarized to customers under NDA.
intended_practice: Create register as records under Praxis with validation that every high risk links to at least one control and evidence requirement.
owner: Managing member of Echelon Foundry, LLC (role not yet formally assigned)

title: Risk appetite, tolerance and risk acceptance authority
target_answer: The managing member has approved a risk appetite statement with measurable tolerances for security, availability, data integrity and compliance. Residual risks above tolerance can be accepted only by the managing member and only with a recorded decision; any acceptance that affects a customer's data or obligations is disclosed to that customer, who can object. Because one person may both propose and accept a risk, every acceptance above a defined rating is reviewed by an independent advisor within 30 days and the review is recorded. Risks to sponsor operations remain the sponsor board's to accept (UNB-GOV-001).
intended_practice: Adopt appetite statement and acceptance workflow using Praxis decision records.
owner: Managing member of Echelon Foundry, LLC (role not yet formally assigned)

title: Policy and standard exceptions with enforced expiry
target_answer: Every exception to a mandatory rule is a record naming the rule, scope (repository, path, environment), justification, compensating controls, approver and expiry. The build and release gates read the exception records: an expired exception makes the gate fail again, and a suppression without a matching record fails the build. Mandatory checks run in CI under branch protection that neither a human nor an AI agent can bypass without leaving an audit record; any bypass raises an alert. Open exception counts and the oldest exception age are reported monthly.
intended_practice: Implement exception records and gate integration in Praxis/CI as part of Secure Construction Standard adoption.
owner: Managing member of Echelon Foundry, LLC (role not yet formally assigned)

title: Echelon's own third-party and fourth-party risk management
target_answer: We maintain an inventory of critical vendors, derived where possible from infrastructure-as-code, SBOM and billing data so it cannot silently drift, covering cloud hosting, code hosting, CI, AI model providers, email and support tooling. Each critical vendor has a criticality rating, assessment (SOC report review including complementary user entity controls we must operate, financial check, contract review), data classes received, AI training terms, incident notice terms and an exit plan. Reviews are annual and on change. Vendor incidents affecting customers are relayed within our contractual notice period.
intended_practice: Build inventory and assess the cloud, code hosting and AI providers first.
owner: Managing member of Echelon Foundry, LLC (role not yet formally assigned)

title: Risk assessment of AI agent use, new capabilities and model provider change
target_answer: Before an AI agent receives a new tool, permission, data class or production pathway, a recorded risk assessment covers misuse, prompt injection, data leakage, unreviewed change and loss of attribution, mapped to NIST AI RMF and the OWASP agentic threat list, and names the controls (tool brokering, least privilege, human approval, provenance). Model or provider changes are treated as changes: pinned model identifiers, evaluation against regression suites before switching, and notice to customers where processing of their data changes.
intended_practice: Add AI-specific triggers to the risk method and a change record for model/provider changes.
owner: Managing member of Echelon Foundry, LLC (role not yet formally assigned)

title: Risk reporting to customers and scenario analysis
target_answer: Customers receive a periodic risk and control status report generated from the live register and control evidence, so it cannot drift from the internal view, with each statement tagged by status (operating, designed, planned). We run and record at least annually severe-but-plausible scenarios: loss of the founder, loss or suspension of the cloud account, ransomware or credential compromise in CI, loss of a major customer, and AI agent misuse, with the resulting actions.
intended_practice: Generate customer reports from records with Folio once the register exists.

title: Static application security testing, including F# coverage
target_answer: Every merge runs available .NET analyzers, F# analyzers built on FSharp.Analyzers.SDK, and Echelon custom semantic rules that detect use or bypass of prohibited constructs (dynamic SQL outside Strata, dynamic code loading, unsafe interop, unrestricted deserialization, application JavaScript outside Limen); generated JavaScript bundles are scanned with a JavaScript-capable engine; coverage limits are stated per weakness class.
intended_practice: Select and build F# analyzers, assign an owner (not Aegis), and integrate into Praxis gates.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)

title: Software composition analysis
target_answer: Every build generates an SBOM and runs SCA against OSV and GitHub advisory data for NuGet and npm, including transitive dependencies, with license policy; deployed SBOMs are rescanned daily so new advisories against released artifacts are detected.
intended_practice: Implement in CI with SEC-SUPPLY-001.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)

title: Secret scanning and response
target_answer: Pre-commit and push-time scanning blocks secrets; scheduled scans cover full history, CI logs, container images and persisted AI agent transcripts; any detected secret is treated as compromised, rotated and revoked, and its use investigated; scanning applies to all Echelon repositories.
intended_practice: Enable push-time blocking and history scans across Echelon repositories.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)

title: Dynamic testing (DAST, API testing, IAST, ASV)
target_answer: Each release candidate deployed to a test cell is scanned with authenticated DAST and schema-driven API tests across all roles, including cross-tenant object access attempts; Limen boundary messages and other serialized inputs are fuzzed. IAST is not used unless a tool demonstrably supports F# on .NET. ASV scans are performed only if PCI DSS scope is ever introduced.
intended_practice: Implement once a deployable test environment exists.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)

title: Infrastructure-as-code, container, configuration and schema scanning

title: Scanner validation and false negative measurement
target_answer: Each scanner and rule set release is validated against public suites where applicable and Echelon F# vulnerable and safe fixtures with independently constructed holdouts; precision, recall, false positive and false negative rates are reported by weakness class; recall regressions block adoption; vulnerabilities that escaped scanners become new fixtures; methodology, fixtures and limitations are published, and benchmarking is never represented as accreditation.
intended_practice: Build the fixture corpus and validation harness as part of the scanner program.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)

title: Scan frequency, coverage, gating and suppression governance
target_answer: SAST, SCA and secret scans run on every merge; DAST and IaC scans on every release candidate; deployed artifacts rescanned daily; scan evidence older than the release commit blocks release. Gates fail closed on missing evidence. Scanner configuration lives outside the repository under change control. Suppressions need a non-author human approver, expire and are re-reviewed; AI agents cannot alter scanner configuration, gates or suppressions. Coverage is reported against the full inventory.

title: Sharing scan results with customers

title: Dependency approval and intake

title: Development environment separation, secrets and test data
target_answer: Development, test and production use separate accounts, credentials and networks; production data is never copied to non-production unless masked through an approved, logged process; secrets are injected at runtime from a managed store and blocked from source by scanning on every push; access to source repositories requires MFA and is reviewed.

title: Published subprocessor register generated from the vendor inventory
target_answer: Echelon publishes a subprocessor register per tenant, generated from the vendor inventory and from integration configuration, listing each subprocessor's legal entity, function, data categories, processing and support locations and transfer mechanism. Vendors without access to customer data are excluded and the distinction is documented. Because the register is generated from the configuration that actually routes data, an integration that sends customer data to an unlisted party fails a release check.
intended_practice: Generate the register from the vendor inventory (TPR) and a data-flow declaration checked at release.
owner: Not assigned (proposed: Echelon privacy owner)

title: Advance notice of subprocessor changes and customer objection rights
target_answer: Echelon notifies subscribed customer contacts at least 30 days before adding or replacing a subprocessor, or changing a subprocessor's location or processing scope, with the register diff. Emergency replacements are notified within 72 hours with the reason. Customers may object on reasonable data protection grounds; Echelon then offers an alternative configuration that avoids the subprocessor for that tenant where technically possible, or a termination right with pro-rated refund. Notices are generated from the register diff so none can be skipped.
intended_practice: Implement per UNB-XIN-SAS-011 with objection handling defined in the customer agreement.
owner: Not assigned (proposed: Echelon privacy owner)

title: Flow-down terms and oversight of subprocessors
target_answer: Each subprocessor is bound by written terms at least as protective as Echelon's commitments to the customer: confidentiality, security measures, purpose limitation including no AI training on customer data, breach notice, assistance with data subject requests, deletion at end of service, audit rights and approval of further sub-subprocessors. Echelon remains responsible to the customer for subprocessor performance. Subprocessors are monitored under the TPR program at the tier their data access implies.
intended_practice: Create a DPA template and flow-down checklist; record each subprocessor's terms in the vendor register.
owner: Not assigned (proposed: Echelon counsel)

title: Data location, processing location and cross-border transfers
target_answer: Customer data, backups, logs, AI inference and support access are confined to documented regions, by default the United States, enforced by infrastructure configuration and provider region settings and verified by automated configuration checks. Any processing outside the region, including AI inference and follow-the-sun support, is listed in the register with its transfer mechanism (for EU or UK personal data, Standard Contractual Clauses or the Data Privacy Framework where the recipient is certified).
intended_practice: Decide hosting region and AI inference region before production and encode them as checked configuration.
owner: Not assigned (proposed: Echelon engineering owner)

title: AI providers as subprocessors
target_answer: Every AI provider that receives customer content is a listed subprocessor, naming the contracting entity that processes the data (for example the cloud platform hosting a model rather than the model developer, where that is the case), its region and its retention terms. Switching to a new AI provider, or to a different hosting route for a model, triggers the subprocessor notice process; changing model version within the same provider and route does not, but is recorded in the AI inventory. Engineering AI tools never receive customer data, enforced by keeping customer data out of engineering environments; if that ever changes, those providers become subprocessors and are listed.
intended_practice: Add AI provider fields to the subprocessor register and a rule keeping customer data out of engineering environments.
owner: Not assigned (proposed: Echelon privacy owner)

title: Support hours, channels and peak coverage
target_answer: Support is available during US business hours in all continental time zones for sponsor staff, with critical-severity coverage at all times. Channels include an in-product case system, email and phone, plus an out-of-band channel that works when the platform is down. Coverage increases in the final weeks of December according to a seasonal capacity plan. Echelon supports sponsor staff; donor-facing support is the sponsor's choice and Unbound provides tools for it.

owner: Proposed: Customer Support Lead (role not yet staffed)

title: Severity definitions and response targets
target_answer: Four severity levels are defined with examples tied to customer consequence (Severity 1 includes inability to approve or release grants, suspected data exposure, or incorrect balances). Response targets are contractual (for example 30 minutes for Severity 1 at any hour) and resolution targets are stated as objectives. Performance is measured from ticket timestamps and reported monthly. Customer commitments made in support cases are recorded with owners and due times.
intended_practice: Draft severity matrix with the support offering.
owner: Proposed: Customer Support Lead (role not yet staffed)

title: Escalation, named contacts and coverage despite small team
target_answer: Each customer has a named primary and backup contact and a documented escalation path to executive level; every level resolves to a reachable person with a named backup, enforced the same way control ownership is (owner plus backup always resolvable).
intended_practice: Assign named contacts and backups per customer at onboarding.
owner: Proposed: Customer Support Lead (role not yet staffed)

title: Support access to customer data
target_answer: Support staff and support agents have no standing access to tenant data. Access requires a case-linked request approved by the customer, is limited in scope and time, is read-only unless the customer explicitly authorizes a specific change, and is logged with every action visible in the customer's access view. Support can never move money, change payees or change authority on a customer's behalf. Emergency access is two-person break-glass, limited to read and protective actions, auto-expiring within four hours and notified to the customer immediately.
intended_practice: Implement support access as a first-class authorization feature before production.
owner: Proposed: Security Lead (role not yet staffed)

title: AI support agents
target_answer: Where AI agents answer support questions, users are told they are interacting with AI, can reach a human at any point, and are routed to a human automatically for financial, security, accessibility-accommodation or complaint matters. Agents can read only public documentation and the requesting user's own authorized data, cannot take financial, authority or configuration actions, and their model and prompt versions are recorded per conversation. Support conversations are not used to train third-party models, and evaluation of accuracy and escalation behavior runs on a schedule.
intended_practice: Decide whether to use AI support agents; if so, build to this design.
owner: Proposed: Customer Support Lead (role not yet staffed)

title: Problem management, case visibility and support workforce
target_answer: Recurring incidents are managed as problems with root cause and fix tracking; known errors and workarounds are published to affected customers. Customers see all their cases, history and commitments, and can export them. Support is provided by Echelon employees located in the United States unless a customer agrees otherwise; any subcontracted support is disclosed with its data access.
intended_practice: Select a case system integrated with Unbound's case kernel; decide support workforce model.
owner: Proposed: Customer Support Lead (role not yet staffed)

title: Multi-tenant architecture, tenant unit and isolation profiles
target_answer: Unbound's tenant unit is the legal sponsor. Each sponsor is a cell: by default a dedicated schema and database role in a shared managed PostgreSQL cluster (profile A), with dedicated database (B) or dedicated infrastructure (C) available when risk or contract requires; business logic does not fork by profile. Inside a cell, distribution partners and programs are separated by typed partitioning in code, row-level security in the database, and negative tests. Isolation never relies on a tenant_id filter in application code alone. Shared services (identity, charity reference registry, orchestration, telemetry, model services) are listed in a SharedStoreRegister with permitted fields and classification; donor and advisor personal data never enters a shared store except as a keyed token. The isolation profile and controls in effect for each tenant at any time are recorded as append-only events.
intended_practice: Resolve the open architecture decisions (database engine and provider, key hierarchy, row-level security role), then build the sponsor cell model.
owner: Unassigned; proposed Unbound architecture owner

title: Tenant context derivation, routing and connection hygiene
target_answer: The tenant for every request, job and message is derived from the authenticated principal's server-held entitlement set; a user entitled to several tenants selects one through an opaque, server-issued, session-bound token that is revalidated on every request. Headers, parameters, subdomains, schema hints and partner API fields cannot select a tenant. The connection broker binds an allowlisted schema and tenant-specific database role per transaction, never interpolates identifiers, never relies on a mutable default search path, and resets role, session settings and search path before returning a connection to the pool. Background jobs and message consumers carry a signed tenant context in the message envelope and open tenant-bound units of work; there is no cross-tenant job identity except governed platform maintenance under break-glass rules.
intended_practice: Implement the broker and pooled-connection reset with negative tests (spoofed tenant, pooled leakage).
owner: Unassigned; proposed Engineering Lead

title: Tenant isolation by construction: verified tenant context as a required type
target_answer: Application code cannot obtain a database connection or issue a query without a VerifiedTenantContext value, and that value can be constructed only by the trusted tenant resolver after authentication and entitlement checks. All repository and query functions take the context as a required parameter and bind tenant schema and role from it, so a query that spans tenants or omits the tenant cannot be written in application code and fails to compile. Within a sponsor cell, partner and program scope are typed the same way. The guarantee is scoped and stated: it covers application command and query code in the governed modules; it does not cover migrations, platform maintenance, break-glass, the database engine itself, or code that uses reflection or unsafe interop, each of which is controlled separately (Strata-declared grants and RLS, break-glass rules, SEC-EXEC-001 and SEC-LANG-001 analysis). Build provenance links the deployed binary to the checked source, and database-level enforcement remains as an independent second layer.
intended_practice: Build the tenant-bound unit-of-work and query layer, prohibit raw connections in governed modules by analyzer, and keep database roles and RLS as an independent layer.
owner: Unassigned; proposed Unbound architecture owner

title: Database-enforced tenant separation: roles, schema privileges, row-level security and catalog exposure
target_answer: Each sponsor cell has its own schema and database roles; tenant roles have no privileges on other cells' schemas and none are granted to PUBLIC. Every tenant table in a cell has row-level security enabled and forced, so table owners cannot bypass it, with policies keyed to partner and program scope; no application role has BYPASSRLS or superuser. Grants and policies are declared in Strata and checked before each deployment, and a release check fails if any tenant table lacks enabled and forced RLS or if any tenant role holds privileges outside its cell. SECURITY DEFINER routines are prohibited in tenant schemas unless reviewed with a pinned search path. Because PostgreSQL system catalogs are readable across schemas and some catalogs (roles, databases) are cluster-wide, schema, role and object names contain no customer-identifying information, and customers needing metadata confidentiality use the dedicated-database profile.
intended_practice: Add Strata invariants (or a separate check) for forced RLS on tenant tables and for cell-confined grants; adopt opaque naming; test UNB-TEN-005 scenarios.
owner: Unassigned; proposed Engineering Lead

title: Cross-tenant isolation testing and continuous verification
target_answer: Every build runs the full isolation test matrix for each supported profile against real PostgreSQL: cross-tenant reads and writes, spoofed routing hints, pooled connection reuse, background job context, cache and index isolation, and AI retrieval. In production, synthetic canary tenants continuously attempt cross-tenant access through public interfaces and every denial is recorded and alerted. An independent penetration test focused on tenant isolation is performed before production and annually, and customers may test isolation themselves using two provisioned test tenants under agreed rules.
intended_practice: Build the matrix with the persistence layer; commission independent testing before production.
owner: Unassigned; proposed Security Lead

title: Isolation beyond the database: caches, queues, search, files, logs, backups and AI context
target_answer: Every secondary store is listed in the isolation map with its tenant key: cache keys and queue topics are tenant-prefixed by the same typed context; search and vector indexes are partitioned per sponsor cell; object storage uses per-cell prefixes or buckets with cell-scoped credentials; logs and traces carry tenant identifiers and redact personal data. AI features retrieve context only through the governed query layer under the user's tenant context, log retrieved resource identifiers, and never use one tenant's data to train, fine-tune or evaluate models serving another tenant without documented sharing rights. Backups are per cell where the profile allows; for shared-cluster backups the limitations of single-tenant restore are documented and tested. Support and observability tools show tenant-scoped views by default.
intended_practice: Extend the typed tenant context to cache, queue, index and storage clients; partition AI retrieval; document backup limitations.
owner: Unassigned; proposed Unbound architecture owner

title: Tenant-scoped encryption keys, customer-managed keys and cryptographic erasure
target_answer: Each sponsor cell has its own data encryption keys under a key hierarchy in a managed key service, with sensitive fields additionally encrypted at the application layer under cell-specific keys so that database-level access alone does not reveal them. Customers that require it can supply or hold their own root key; revoking it renders their data unavailable, and the service behavior on revocation is documented. On exit, cell keys are destroyed under dual control after retention and legal-hold checks, and a destruction certificate states what persists (for example immutable backups until expiry) and when. Compromise of one cell's keys does not expose another cell.
intended_practice: Decide the key hierarchy (ADR-006); implement per-cell keys and application-layer encryption for sensitive fields.
owner: Unassigned; proposed Security Lead

title: Noisy neighbor and per-tenant resource isolation
target_answer: Each tenant has rate limits, query timeouts, connection pool quotas and job concurrency limits enforced at the API gateway, connection broker and job scheduler. Time-critical work (grant disbursement windows, year-end receipting) runs in priority queues with per-tenant fairness so one tenant's surge cannot delay another's deadlines. Per-tenant latency and error rates are monitored with alerts on cross-tenant contention. Schema migrations are applied per cell with independent failure handling, so one cell's failed migration leaves others unaffected. Tenants whose load or contract requires it move to a dedicated profile without changing identifiers.
intended_practice: Benchmark per UNB-TEN-018; implement quotas and per-cell migration.
owner: Unassigned; proposed Unbound operations owner

title: White-label, embedded and distribution-partner isolation and partner exit
target_answer: Distribution partners are typed partitions inside the sponsor cell. A partner's users, APIs and widgets can reach only donors and funds in that partner's channel and only the data classes the sponsor authorizes for that partner; cross-partner movement of a donor or fund requires an approved transfer, never a data copy. Embedded components run in an isolated origin with scoped tokens and cannot be scripted by the host page. Branding, templates and sender identity are versioned per program and validated so a communication cannot be sent under another partner's brand. On partner exit, partner access, API clients and subscriptions end at the effective time, donors retain access through pre-provisioned sponsor-direct credentials, and the exit case reconciles every fund.
intended_practice: Implement partner partitions with the same typed context and RLS policies as programs; implement the PartnerExit case.
owner: Unassigned; proposed Product Owner

title: Tenant lifecycle: provisioning, profile migration, export and offboarding evidence
target_answer: Tenants move through a governed lifecycle state machine. Go-live requires a ReadinessValidated state that includes passing the isolation test matrix for that tenant's profile. Migration between profiles uses a consistent event high-water mark, record-by-record equivalence verification, independent ledger reconciliation and fencing so there is never more than one authoritative writer, and preserves all identifiers and history. On exit, the sponsor receives within 30 days an ExitPackage with full event history, projections, documents, policies, audit records and a signed manifest with digests, counts and reconciled trial balances that it can verify independently; the tenant then enters read-only retention before key destruction. The profile and controls in effect at any past time are queryable.
intended_practice: Implement the lifecycle state machine with isolation readiness checks and the export package.
owner: Unassigned; proposed Unbound operations owner

title: Third-party inventory and criticality tiering
target_answer: Echelon keeps one vendor inventory that is the source for the subprocessor register, the SBOM-linked open-source inventory and the AI provider list. Each entry records service, data classes accessed, integration points, contract, owner, inherent risk tier and criticality to each customer-facing service. Tiering criteria are documented (data sensitivity, operational criticality, substitutability, regulatory relevance) and applied consistently. The inventory is reconciled quarterly against spend, contracts, identity provider integrations, network egress destinations and code dependencies, so unrecorded vendors surface automatically.
intended_practice: Create the inventory before any production deployment and generate the subprocessor register from it.
owner: Not assigned (proposed: Echelon vendor risk owner)

title: Pre-engagement vendor due diligence proportional to risk
target_answer: Before a vendor is engaged or integrated, Echelon performs due diligence scaled to tier: for critical vendors, security assurance (SOC 2 Type 2 or equivalent with CUEC mapping), financial condition, ownership and sanctions screening, legal and regulatory standing, business continuity, subcontractor reliance and data location; for low-risk vendors, a short record. Integration with a new vendor is technically blocked until the inventory entry and approval exist: new egress destinations, OAuth applications and dependencies need an approved vendor record. Neither engineers nor AI agents can add a data-processing vendor on their own.
intended_practice: Implement a tiered due diligence checklist and tie it to the SOC2-030 design review gate.
owner: Not assigned (proposed: Echelon vendor risk owner)

title: Vendor contract requirements, including flow-through of customer and regulator rights
target_answer: Contracts with vendors that touch customer data or critical services include: security obligations and right to assess; breach notification fast enough for Echelon to meet its own commitments (for example the bank service provider notice under the 2021 computer-security incident rule and 72-hour service provider notice under amended Regulation S-P); audit and regulator examination access that flows to Echelon's regulated customers; data use limits including no AI training; subcontractor approval; data location; business continuity and SLAs; and termination assistance with data return and deletion certification. A contract template and a gap register record where a vendor's standard terms fall short and who accepted the gap.
intended_practice: Draft a vendor contract standard and gap register before first critical vendor engagement for a production service.
owner: Not assigned (proposed: Echelon counsel)

title: Ongoing monitoring of vendors, assurance report review and CUEC operation
target_answer: Critical vendors are monitored continuously for signals (status pages, breach disclosures, security advisories, ownership changes, financial distress) and reviewed formally at least annually. SOC reports are reviewed for scope, period, opinion, exceptions and CUECs; every CUEC is mapped to an Echelon control with an owner and evidence; bridge letters are recorded as management assertions that do not extend assurance; stale or qualified reports trigger compensating procedures or time-limited risk acceptance. Event triggers (breach, outage, ownership change, scope change) force out-of-cycle review. Issues are tracked to closure.
intended_practice: Run the CNV-GOV-002 annual review task from first vendor engagement; automate gap tracking later.
owner: Not assigned (proposed: Echelon vendor risk owner)

title: Concentration risk and fourth-party visibility
target_answer: Echelon maps which customer-facing services depend on each critical vendor and on that vendor's own critical providers (fourth parties), including carve-out subservice organizations named in vendor SOC reports. It measures concentration on single cloud regions, single AI providers and single identity or source-hosting providers, records the impact of each failing, and sets tolerances. Where a single provider is accepted, the exit plan and degraded-mode design (for example deterministic paths continuing without AI) are the mitigation.
intended_practice: Produce a dependency map from the vendor inventory and vendor SOC report subservice sections.
owner: Not assigned (proposed: Echelon vendor risk owner)

title: Exit and termination plans for critical vendors
target_answer: Each critical vendor has a written exit plan: trigger conditions, alternate provider or in-house fallback, data export format, migration steps, time to exit, cost estimate and owner. Architecture favors substitutability: standard PostgreSQL managed by Strata rather than proprietary databases, provider-neutral AI interfaces with deterministic fallbacks, infrastructure as code. Exit plans for the most critical vendors are rehearsed (data export and restore on an alternate provider) on a defined cadence. Termination includes credential revocation, data return and deletion confirmation.
intended_practice: Write exit plans for cloud hosting and AI providers before production.
owner: Not assigned (proposed: Echelon engineering owner)

title: Third-party risk program governance aligned to the Interagency Guidance lifecycle
target_answer: An approved third-party risk policy defines the lifecycle used by Echelon (planning, due diligence and selection, contract negotiation, ongoing monitoring, termination) with governance across it (oversight, accountability, documentation, independent review), mirroring the stages of the 2023 Interagency Guidance so bank customers can map Echelon's practice to their own. It names the accountable owner and risk acceptance authority, sets reporting to leadership, and is independently reviewed. Echelon provides customers the information they need for their own oversight of Echelon as a third party, including its subcontractor oversight.
intended_practice: Adopt a TPRM policy based on the Interagency Guidance lifecycle when Echelon prepares for its first regulated customer.
owner: Not assigned (proposed: Echelon managing member)

title: Termination assistance, transition period and in-flight transactions
target_answer: On notice of termination, Echelon provides a transition period of up to 12 months at unchanged service levels, a jointly maintained exit plan, cooperation with the successor provider, and a defined treatment for every in-flight item: pending recommendations, approved but unpaid grants, recurring grants, ACH items in process, outstanding checks and open compliance cases are either completed under the sponsor's direction or handed off with full records. The exit plan is tested by a dry-run export and reconciliation at least annually.
intended_practice: Write a standard exit plan template and termination assistance schedule before first contract.
owner: Managing member of Echelon Foundry, LLC

title: Data return, access windows and deletion certification at exit
target_answer: At termination Echelon delivers a final complete export within 10 business days, keeps read-only access open for 90 days, and does not withhold data during a fee dispute. After the customer confirms receipt (or 90 days pass), Echelon deletes the tenant's data by key destruction, lets backups expire on the published cycle, retains only what law requires with the basis stated, and issues an evidence-generated deletion certificate (ANS-RET-007).
intended_practice: Encode exit timelines in the standard agreement; build read-only tenant mode.
owner: Managing member of Echelon Foundry, LLC

title: Wind-down if Echelon fails, is acquired or changes control
target_answer: Customer continuity does not depend on Echelon surviving. Each sponsor receives scheduled full exports to storage it controls; export schemas and a minimal read-only viewer are escrowed or openly published; Echelon maintains a funded wind-down plan covering at least the contractual transition period; contracts allow termination on change of control and require any acquirer to assume exit obligations. A read-only continuity mode can be operated by a successor using the escrowed materials.
intended_practice: Decide whether to offer customer-owned export destinations and a wind-down reserve; draft change-of-control terms.
owner: Managing member of Echelon Foundry, LLC

title: Regulatory continuity for the sponsor through exit
target_answer: Exit never interrupts the sponsor's legal obligations: acknowledgments and statements for the final period are issued or handed over, Form 990 and Schedule D support is exported for every open year, sanctions and eligibility records are preserved, partner exits follow UNB-XIN-SAS-007 with sponsor discretion preserved per fund, payment rail roles and bank arrangements are unwound in sequence with the ODFI, and Echelon remains contractually available to produce records it still holds for regulator or IRS requests during the post-termination retention period.
intended_practice: Add a regulatory continuity checklist to the exit plan template.
owner: Managing member of Echelon Foundry, LLC

title: Fees and contract terms at exit
target_answer: Echelon's standard terms carry no exit fee and no charge for standard exports; termination assistance beyond standard exports is priced in a published rate schedule; customers may terminate for convenience on reasonable notice; renewal requires affirmative notice or allows termination at any time after the initial term; confidentiality, data protection, deletion and record-production obligations survive termination; customers have perpetual rights to use exported data and reports.
intended_practice: Draft exit-friendly standard terms; decide the business tradeoff of no termination fee.
owner: Managing member of Echelon Foundry, LLC

title: Idempotent commands and postings keyed on stable business identifiers
target_answer: Every mutating Unbound command and every posting is idempotent on a stable business key, not a transport retry ID: for example GrantId plus installment, PaymentIntentId, or ScheduleId plus occurrence (UNB-XIN-EVA-005, UNB-RCN-GRT-004). Posting is idempotent per source event ID and accounting book, so at most one original journal exists per pair whatever the posting-rule version (RR-ACC-MDL-007-r1). Each external observation type has a registered key derived from source data (an ACH return is keyed on original trace, return reason code and return trace); a repeat with the same key and payload hash is acknowledged with no effect, while the same key with a different hash is not applied and opens a DuplicateKeyConflict case. Fee runs are idempotent per fund, schedule, period and segment set (RR-ADM-028-r1). Keys are enforced by database unique constraints in the same transaction as the effect, so a race between duplicates cannot produce two effects.
intended_practice: Implement an idempotency key registry per command and observation type with unique constraints and payload hashes; contract tests replay every command.
owner: Not assigned; proposed: Unbound platform architecture owner (role not staffed)

title: External effects: exactly-once internally, at most one live attempt externally
target_answer: Unbound does not claim exactly-once execution at external providers; no local guarantee is represented as provider exactly-once (REQ-X-019). Internally, state changes and the outbound message that will cause an external effect commit in the same transaction through a durable outbox, consumers are idempotent and ordering is per subject (UNB-EVT-002). Every external effect has a durable issuance receipt and external idempotency key so retries, recovery and replay cannot repeat payments, grants, trades, notices or filings (UNB-IMM-006, UNB-DATA-009, UNB-RES-002). Process managers issue commands with stable keys and never hold locks across external calls (UNB-XIN-EVA-007). A payment rail is eligible only if the provider contractually supports idempotent submission and status query (TVR-PAY-002); where a rail lacks an end-to-end key (noted for ACH), reconciliation and the unknown-outcome protocol close the gap. The guarantee offered is at most one live attempt per grant under any failure (TVR-PAY-001).
intended_practice: Implement the transactional outbox and effect-receipt store; select providers only with idempotent submission and status query.
owner: Not assigned; proposed: Unbound platform architecture owner (role not staffed)

title: Atomic approval, reservation and journal commit
target_answer: Routine grant approval and the currency reservation against net capacity commit atomically in one transaction, so two simultaneous grants that together exceed capacity cannot both succeed and a failed grant has neither approval nor reservation (REQ-X-002, CNV-FIN-001). Every domain fact with a financial effect carries the journal batch or reservation ID committed in the same database transaction, and balances are computed only from insert-only journal and reservation tables (UNB-XIN-EVA-001). Deadline-bearing obligations are persisted in the same transaction as the state change that creates them (UNB-XIN-WFA-001). A batch such as a payment file or recurring-grant run is only a container: each item commits in its own transaction with its own key, and a batch ends PartiallyCompleted with per-item outcomes rather than all-or-nothing ambiguity (UNB-XIN-EVA-011).
intended_practice: Keep the authoritative ledger and facts in one PostgreSQL cluster per the architecture so atomicity is a local transaction property, not a distributed protocol (CNV-ARC-001).
owner: Not assigned; proposed: Unbound platform architecture owner (role not staffed)

title: Concurrency control, serializable reservations and dispatch fencing
target_answer: A grant reservation is created only inside one serializable transaction that computes reservable capacity from the authoritative ledger, reservation and hold records for the fund and every constrained ancestor (pool cash buffer, custody account, entity, restricted sub-balance), acquiring locks in a deterministic order; display projections are never used for this check (RR-UNB-GFUND-021-r1). Concurrent recommendations, redemptions or liquidations cannot commit the same liquidity twice (UNB-GFUND-021, UNB-NAV-028). Conflicting instructions from different advisors move both to HeldConflict unless policy resolves them deterministically (UNB-XIN-EVA-012). At the irreversible dispatch step, the release checks the current hold publication version atomically with authorization using a fencing token, and unknown hold state fails closed (CNV-ARC-003). Cancel-versus-submit races resolve by revision with exactly one winner (TVR-GR-004). Tenant migration never permits two active authoritative writers (UNB-TEN-013).
intended_practice: Test the 12 concurrency schedules and 16 invariants named in REQ-X-019 with deterministic interleavings before release.
owner: Not assigned; proposed: Unbound platform architecture owner (role not staffed)

title: Completeness and accuracy of inputs from external sources
target_answer: Each external source (bank statements and return files, custodian files, processor reports, IRS exempt-organization extracts, sanctions lists) has an expected-delivery calendar and a completeness watermark; a batch is accepted only when its control totals (record count, amount sum or source trailer) match, and a source behind schedule opens a SourceFeedGapDetected case that holds automated actions depending on that source's freshness while still allowing protective actions (UNB-XIN-EVA-004). External files and webhooks carry retrieval evidence and authenticity checks, and ingestion alone never grants sponsor approval (UNB-EVT-003). Provider callbacks are authenticated and deduplicated on provider and event ID and on a semantic key (RR-REQ-X-083-r1). Raw feeds are preserved and duplicate or out-of-order observations never overwrite prior evidence (CNV-FIN-013, UNB-KNOW-027). Input validation at trust boundaries uses explicit schemas and size limits (SEC-DATA-001).
intended_practice: Build source adapters with calendar, watermark and control-total checks; preserve raw payloads with hashes.
owner: Not assigned; proposed: Unbound platform architecture owner (role not staffed)

title: Processing integrity and continuously checked financial invariants
target_answer: Unbound defines its processing integrity commitments as explicit invariants that are continuously checkable: balanced journals, valid dimensions, nonduplicated external effects, reconciled control accounts, authorized allocations, preserved restrictions and no unauthorized negative available balance (UNB-ACC-030; Secure Construction Standard, Financial and business invariants). Outputs are computed only from sealed snapshots so they are complete and reproducible (UNB-XIN-EVA-003). Releases deploy in rings and halt automatically when a ledger balance, outbox backlog, unknown-rate or error-budget check breaches its threshold (UNB-XIN-SAS-003). Every business-significant event produces attributable, tamper-evident evidence (SOC2-002), and a missing expected control heartbeat is itself an exception (SOC2-027). These map to the SOC 2 processing integrity criteria if Echelon elects that category in a future SOC 2 scope.
intended_practice: Run the invariant monitor continuously in production and as a release gate; elect processing integrity in SOC 2 scope only after controls operate.
owner: Not assigned; proposed: Unbound platform architecture owner (role not staffed)

title: Deterministic replay and projection rebuild without side effects
target_answer: Rebuilding projections from an immutable snapshot or checkpoint plus subsequent events produces the same state as full replay; the snapshot is a cache, never authority (UNB-IMM-005). Replay is deterministic and side-effect-free: posting rules apply once at posting time and are not re-applied, replay locates existing journals by source event and book, and external effects require durable issuance receipts so replay cannot repeat them (UNB-DATA-009, RR-ACC-MDL-007-r1, UNB-XIN-EVA-001). Stored events carry schema versions; authoritative consumers that meet an unknown version stop and quarantine rather than skip (UNB-XIN-EVA-008). Replay and rebuild times are load-tested at defined scales, including a 10x grant surge, before storage technology is finalized (UNB-IMM-010, UNB-ACC-036).
intended_practice: Run replay-equivalence checks as a release gate and on a schedule against production-shaped synthetic data.
owner: Not assigned; proposed: Unbound platform architecture owner (role not staffed)

title: Unknown outcome handling for timeouts and ambiguous external results
target_answer: When an external call times out or returns an ambiguous result, the item enters an explicit Unknown state; there is no retry button and no automatic retry (TVR-PAY-001, CNV-PAY-004). Each rail has an UnknownResolutionProtocol: status query by idempotency key at defined intervals, reconciliation against bank statements after the settlement window, and a defined evidence combination before NotReceived may be declared, which requires independent approval and creates a linked reissue chain (UNB-RCN-GRT-008). Before the final aging tier a bank trace or rail status request is made; only items still Unobtainable after 30 days go to two independent approvers who record duplicate-risk acceptance and a recovery plan (CNV-PAY-004). A bulk-Unknown event uses graded evidence and dual-control sampling and never bulk-declares NotReceived without per-item proof (TVR-PAY-007). Reissue after a proven NotSubmitted reuses the original idempotency key (UNB-RCN-WF-001). UIs never show success before authoritative confirmation (INT-006, AIN-014).
intended_practice: Implement the payment aggregate with an explicit ProviderKnowledge dimension and an aging queue; drill the bulk-Unknown procedure.
owner: Not assigned; proposed: Unbound platform architecture owner (role not staffed)

title: Vulnerability management program and identification coverage
target_answer: Echelon operates an inventory-driven vulnerability management program: every deployed component is derived from build SBOMs and deployment manifests and continuously matched against OSV, vendor advisories (.NET, PostgreSQL, base images, cloud provider bulletins) and CISA KEV; components missing from the inventory raise gaps; every finding enters one register with lifecycle timestamps; and coverage, aging and exception metrics are reported with raw denominators.
intended_practice: Adopt a vulnerability management procedure under the Secure Construction Standard, implement SBOM-fed SCA in CI, and build the register as a byproduct of the pipeline before Unbound handles real data.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)

title: Risk-based vulnerability prioritization (CVSS v4, EPSS, KEV, reachability, VEX)
target_answer: Each finding carries a CVSS v4.0 vector including threat and environmental metrics, an EPSS score snapshot, KEV membership and a reachability determination. KEV and high-likelihood reachable findings receive accelerated deadlines. Reachability-based deferrals are reviewed by someone other than the fixing engineer and are published to customers as VEX statements. Defects in structural control components (Strata access layer, Limen boundary, authorization core) are escalated one level because other controls depend on them.
intended_practice: Implement as part of the register in ANS-VUL-001.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)

title: Remediation SLAs, verification and zero-day response
target_answer: Proposed contractual ceilings: KEV or actively exploited, 7 days or less (mitigation within 48 hours); critical 15 days; high 30 days; medium 90 days; low at next scheduled release; measured from first detection or public disclosure, whichever is earlier, to deployed fix across all tenants. Closure requires rescan or regression test evidence. A zero-day playbook uses the SBOM index to answer exposure within hours. SLA performance is reported monthly with raw counts.
intended_practice: Set SLA values with counsel and early customers before signing, and enforce them via release gates.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)

title: Vulnerability exceptions and risk acceptance
target_answer: Exceptions are requested in a register, scoped to specific findings and releases, approved by an accountable reviewer other than the requester, accompanied by compensating controls, expire automatically and are re-reviewed; customers are told when an accepted risk affects a control they rely on. AI agents cannot create, approve, extend or close exceptions or suppressions.
intended_practice: Implement the exception register and gate integration with ANS-VUL-003.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)

title: Vulnerability disclosure program and security.txt
target_answer: Echelon publishes a vulnerability disclosure policy aligned with ISO/IEC 29147 and 30111 covering all Echelon domains, products and open-source libraries, with good-faith safe harbor language reviewed by counsel, a monitored reporting address, security.txt files with current expiry on each domain, acknowledgment within 3 business days, triage within 10 business days, and coordinated disclosure.
intended_practice: Publish a VDP and security.txt before any public launch; add SECURITY.md to public Echelon repositories.

title: Bug bounty program
target_answer: No paid bug bounty before production launch; a VDP with safe harbor plus independent penetration testing. Consider a private, invite-only bounty restricted to a dedicated test tenant with synthetic data once Unbound is in production and independently tested.
intended_practice: Decide after production launch.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)

title: Customer notification of vulnerabilities and advisories
target_answer: Customers are notified within 2 business days when a vulnerability affecting their tenant or release is confirmed as exploitable and not yet fixed, with interim mitigations; advisories are issued after fixes; VEX statements are provided for non-affecting components; inquiries during public vulnerability events are answered within 1 business day from the SBOM index; subprocessor and platform vulnerabilities affecting the service are included.

title: Platform component patching and end-of-support management
target_answer: Platform components (.NET runtime, PostgreSQL engine, container base images, OS) are patched by rebuilding immutable artifacts and redeploying through the gated pipeline; deployed versions are monitored against vendor security releases and support windows, with migration plans at least 6 months before end of support.
intended_practice: Adopt immutable build and deploy once hosting is selected.

title: AI agents in vulnerability remediation and AI tooling vulnerabilities
target_answer: AI agents may draft fixes, but every AI-authored change is attributed to the agent and authorizing human, reviewed by a different principal, must pass security regression tests and cannot modify gates, findings or exceptions. Vulnerabilities in agent runtimes, model SDKs and tool integrations are inventoried and managed in the same register.

owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)

title: White-label branding governance and protected legal terms
target_answer: Each sponsor has one governed, versioned Brand Kit (identity, logos, accessible design tokens, typography, terminology, approved assets, support contacts, channel policies) applied consistently to donor portals, administrative interfaces, embedded components, email and Folio documents. Publication validates terminology overrides against a protected-term registry of legally meaningful terms (grant recommendation, sponsoring organization legal name, acknowledgment wording) whose meaning may not be altered, and validates contrast and accessibility of brand tokens. Branding never hides the sponsor's legal identity.
intended_practice: Brand Kit per REQ-X-030 and REQ-X-029, protected terms per UNB-RCN-PLT-007, design system per UNB-PLAT-009 (Forma and Folio).
owner: Unbound product owner (proposed role; not yet assigned)

title: Co-branded disclosures, legal meaning and platform registration
target_answer: In co-branded and partner channels the sponsor is always identified as the legal owner of contributed assets and the party that decides grants; partner copy about sponsor actions is reviewed for legal meaning (donors recommend, the sponsor approves and pays). Partners may display sponsor financial figures only through sponsor widgets or signed data with as-of times. Before white-label, embedded or charity-side donation features are activated for California or Hawaii users, Unbound registers as a charitable fundraising platform with those states' attorneys general and meets the associated disclosure and recordkeeping duties. Email sender identity follows message classification.
intended_practice: Partner copy governance per TVR-WID-005, figure display per TVR-WID-002, platform registration per CNV-LEG-002, sender identity per CNV-PLT-001.
owner: Unbound product owner (proposed role; not yet assigned)

title: Embedded component security: framing, CSP, message validation and launch tokens
target_answer: Embedded components run on a sponsor-controlled widget origin, never inherit host authority, and treat the host page as untrusted. Launch uses a one-use, short-lived launch artifact obtained by the partner backend with a server credential for a mapped subject; the widget sets an exact CSP frame-ancestors allowlist per registered host origin; postMessage traffic is validated by origin and schema and carries only opaque host events; every command is reauthorized server-side at execution. Authority changes clear displayed data within a stated window, review steps resist overlay (visibility checks where supported) and high-value or new-recipient actions hand off to a top-level window. Application JavaScript runs only through the Limen boundary.
intended_practice: Widget trust contract per INT-015, AIN-029, MON-022 and the widget integration model (WG-1..WG-9); revocation per UNB-RCN-WF-013 and TVR-WID-001; SEC-UI-002 (Limen).

title: Partner segregation and tenant isolation
target_answer: The tenant unit is the legal sponsor; every authoritative record carries immutable tenant, sponsor and program context. Partner and program isolation inside a sponsor cell is enforced by typed partitioning and negative tests, and a partner needing dedicated infrastructure is served by a dedicated sponsor cell or separate legal sponsor. Isolation profiles (shared database with separate schemas, dedicated database, dedicated infrastructure) are selectable per sponsor and recorded over time. Tenant routing derives from verified identity, never a client value, and isolation extends to caches, queues, event streams, search indexes, backups and telemetry. Shared services carry no donor PII beyond a registered shared-store list.
intended_practice: Tenancy per UNB-TEN-001..020, CNV-TEN-001, CNV-ARC-002, UNB-XIN-SAS-005; custodian isolation per UNB-CUST-019.

title: Partner access to donor data and event minimization
target_answer: Partners receive the minimum data necessary: domain events are classified private or published, and published integration events are a separately versioned contract carrying opaque references rather than financial details. Partners display sponsor financial data only through sponsor widgets or signed data with as-of times. Partner identity mapping uses a permanent identifier (issuer and subject or SCIM external ID), and mapping changes require dual control and donor notice. On partner offboarding, the partner attests deletion of any data received. No partner appears in the funds flow.
intended_practice: Event classification per UNB-XIN-EVA-008, figure display per TVR-WID-002, identity mapping per AUTH-I8, offboarding per WG-7, funds flow per UNB-XIN-OTH-003.

title: Partner API access, entitlements and deprovisioning
target_answer: Partner APIs authenticate partner backends with scoped server credentials and authorize every call against the partner's per-tenant capability entitlements; external writes express requests, never approvals, money movement or policy publication. Mutating commands require idempotency keys and return stable machine-readable errors; partner events are signed, replay-safe and deduplicated; APIs are versioned with compatibility windows. Partner-side user deprovisioning has a contractual maximum latency per tier, while sponsor-side revocation of all sessions is independent of the partner. Rate limits protect sensitive business flows.
intended_practice: API rules per UNB-API-002..006, entitlements per UNB-XIN-SAS-001, deprovisioning per TVR-WID-006 and WG-2, versioning per WG-8.

title: Partner certification, suspension and exit
target_answer: Partners are onboarded through a governed plan with certification of their integration, including copy review and a combined host-plus-widget accessibility test. Partner suspension stops new launches and new commands while accepted commands proceed under sponsor review and donors are informed through a sponsor channel. Partner exit runs as a PartnerExit case (notification, donor outreach, elections, proposed transfers, sponsor decisions, execution, reconciliation) in which funds move only as individual sponsor-authorized outbound grants with eligibility, sanctions and hold checks, and each partner has an exportable, evidence-complete dataset.
intended_practice: Lifecycle per UNB-TEN-011 and UNB-GAP-025, suspension per TVR-WID-003 and WG-6, exit per UNB-XIN-SAS-007 and CNV-ENT-002, portability per UNB-TEN-016, accessibility per WG-9.
